tl;dr
Memories browses and triages an archive of docs — photos and clips — and doubles as a cabinet photo frame — a Solid app over PostGraphile, told here one story at a time, each written test-first.

The stack

how
Memories is built on the stack the frise proved — PostGraphile (GraphQL) and the free-text labels field.
how
it renders with a third technology, Solid and its fine-grained reactivity.
  • why: the slider already uses Alpine and the frise Preact.
how
there is no build step and no bundler — an import map pulls the framework from esm.sh, and the html tagged template stands in for JSX.
what
Postgres is the source of truth.
how
the app reads and edits labels and state.

Stories

what
a story is a whole use somebody opens the archive for, never one feature such as a download button.
  • example: getting three docs onto a phone before dinner, sorting out a morning’s shooting, leaving the cabinet running through a good afternoon.
what
those stories are what memories promises.
  • therefore: memories is checked against them.
how
every heading after this one takes one piece of one story and says how it is kept.
how
each heading carries narrative, a Playwright test, the code, the CSS — written test-first, blocks short, rewrite over patch.

Showing docs

Sharing a few docs with someone

what
somebody asks for the docs from an afternoon.
  • how: you search the tag, a handful comes back, and you take what you need: the web copies to hand over now, and the originals of the ones you mean to rework.
    • rule: both have to open where they land, and the second must not overwrite the first.
what
nothing here is edited; this is the one story that only reads.
what
it needs three docs that differ in what can be taken from them: one complete, one that was never downscaled, and a clip.
  • how: their bytes are served from the app’s own origin.

SEND_LABEL = "zzsend"
SEND_BYTES = ["send-c", "send-w", "send-t",        # the complete photo
              "send-nc", "send-nt",                # never downscaled: no web copy
              "send-vc", "send-vw", "send-vt"]     # the video
def send_docs():
    b = {n: serve_bytes(n) for n in SEND_BYTES}
    return [
        {"cid": b["send-c"], "date": "2020-05-15T12:00:00Z", "mimetype": "image/jpeg",
         "thumbnailCid": b["send-t"], "webCid": b["send-w"], "filename": "holiday.jpg",
         "labels": SEND_LABEL, "state": "todo"},
        {"cid": b["send-nc"], "date": "2020-05-16T12:00:00Z", "mimetype": "image/jpeg",
         "thumbnailCid": b["send-nt"], "labels": SEND_LABEL, "state": "todo"},
        {"cid": b["send-vc"], "date": "2020-05-17T12:00:00Z", "mimetype": "video/quicktime",
         "thumbnailCid": b["send-vt"], "webCid": b["send-vw"],
         "labels": SEND_LABEL, "state": "todo"},
    ]
how
they are told apart by where they sit, oldest first: the complete photo leads and the clip closes.
what
what becomes of each in turn is selecting and downloading, a step at a time.
  • how: the story below takes it in the order it happens: pick one and take both its forms, check the two files can live side by side, then add the photo that has no web copy, and finally swap to the clip.
what
then the same three docs are handed over the other way, which is not to hand them over at all: put them up on the frame and let the phone in somebody’s pocket take what it wants.
  • what: that is the frame naming what it is showing.
  • rule: it needs a room of this run’s own to name it into, plus somebody listening in it the way the phone would.
  • what: at the end, the same frame is pointed somewhere nothing answers.
    • what: the address that answers nothing is not picked freely either: which port it names is a choice with its own reason.
  • how: both of the show’s knobs — how long a slide stays up, and how long its control bar waits before hiding — are wound past the end of the story rather than to any particular span.
    • what: nothing here is watching the show move: what is read is what the room was told and what one word on the bar says.
      • rule: the slide must not step under either reading.
      • rule: the bar, once a touch has brought it up, must not tidy itself away again before the reading that wants it.

NEVER_MS = 999999                                  # past the end of this session, both times
SHARE_QS = f"?ms={NEVER_MS}&uiidle={NEVER_MS}"
DEAD_PORT = 45999


@testcase
def test_sharing_a_few_photos(page):
    """Someone asks for an afternoon's docs: search the tag, pick, and take each
    at the size that suits — then put the same three up on the frame instead, where a
    phone can help itself, and read off the bar whether anybody is hearing them."""
    docs = send_docs()
    for d in docs: gql(DELETE, {"cid": d["cid"]}); gql(CREATE, {"p": d})
    try:
        open_app(page)
        search_for(page, SEND_LABEL)
        expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(len(docs))
        photo, never_downscaled, video = 0, 1, 2      # shown oldest first
        tiles(page).nth(photo).click()                          # the one worth sending
        expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(1)
        tb, got = toolbar(page), {}
        for res in ["web", "orig"]:
            with page.expect_download() as di:
                tb.get_by_role("button", name=res, exact=True).click()
            got[res] = (di.value.url, di.value.suggested_filename)
        assert docs[photo]["webCid"] in got["web"][0], f"web → webCid: {got}"
        assert docs[photo]["cid"] in got["orig"][0], f"orig → the doc's own cid: {got}"
        print("  PASS: download selection")
        names = {res: name for res, (_, name) in got.items()}   # the two the photo just yielded
        assert len({*names.values()}) == len(names), f"same name → they collide in the folder: {names}"
        for res in names:
            assert res in names[res], f"rendition missing from the name: {names}"
        print("  PASS: download names by resolution")
        tiles(page).nth(never_downscaled).click()
        expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(2)
        saved = []                                              # armed here: only this click's files count
        page.on("download", lambda d: saved.append(d.url))
        toolbar(page).get_by_role("button", name="web", exact=True).click()
        wait_until(page, lambda: len(saved) >= 1, label="the doc that has a web copy saves it")
        page.wait_for_timeout(500)                              # room for a second, unwanted save to land
        assert len(saved) == 1, f"expected the one web copy, got {len(saved)}: {saved}"
        assert docs[photo]["webCid"] in saved[0], f"the wrong rendition came down: {saved[0]}"
        print("  PASS: download skips a missing rendition")
        tiles(page).nth(photo).click()
        tiles(page).nth(never_downscaled).click()
        tiles(page).nth(video).click()
        expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(1)
        tb, ext = toolbar(page), {}
        for res in ["orig", "web"]:
            with page.expect_download() as di:
                tb.get_by_role("button", name=res, exact=True).click()
            ext[res] = di.value.suggested_filename.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
        assert ext["orig"] == "mov", f"original keeps its real type: {ext}"
        assert ext["web"] == "mp4", f"a clip's web copy is mp4: {ext}"
        print("  PASS: download extensions by rendition")
        # …and the same three put up on the frame
        sync_url, room = require_sync(), "memories-test-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
        named = watch_room(page.context, sync_url, room)   # the entry, listened to as the phone will
        open_app(page, SHARE_QS + f"&yws={sync_url}&room={room}")
        expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(len(docs))       # still the afternoon you searched for
        page.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile("frame", re.I)).click()
        strip = page.get_by_role("list", name="slideshow")
        expect(strip).to_be_visible()
        bar = page.get_by_role("toolbar", name="frame actions")
        # nothing is touched here: entering the show is the whole of it
        wait_until(page, lambda: bool(named()), label="the frame names its slide unasked")
        said, shown = named(), docs[photo]
        assert said["cid"] == shown["cid"], f"named the wrong doc: {said}"
        assert said["webCid"] == shown["webCid"], f"no downscaled address: {said}"
        assert said["mimetype"] == shown["mimetype"], f"no file kind: {said}"
        assert page.evaluate("([a, b]) => Date.parse(a) === Date.parse(b)",
                             [said.get("date"), shown["date"]]), \
            f"named a different instant than the doc's {shown['date']}: {said}"
        print("  PASS: frame publishes what is showing")
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")                          # a step, with nothing touched
        wait_until(page, lambda: (named() or {}).get("cid") == docs[never_downscaled]["cid"],
                   label="the name follows the slide", detail=lambda: str(named()))
        print("  PASS: the name follows the slide")
        speak_over(page.context, "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzelsewhere")              # another frame claims the room
        wait_until(page, lambda: (named() or {}).get("cid") == "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzelsewhere")
        strip.click()                                              # a touch, and the slide is not moved
        wait_until(page, lambda: (named() or {}).get("cid") == docs[never_downscaled]["cid"],
                   label="a touch takes the room back", detail=lambda: str(named()))
        print("  PASS: a touch takes the room back")
        wait_until(page, lambda: bar.get_by_text("live", exact=True).count() == 1,
                   label="the bar says the link is live",
                   detail=lambda: f"the bar is up: {bar.is_visible()}; it reads "
                                  f"{bar.text_content() if bar.count() else '—'!r}")
        print("  PASS: the bar says the link is live")
        # and the same frame pointed where nothing answers
        open_app(page, SHARE_QS + f"&yws=ws://127.0.0.1:{DEAD_PORT}&room=nowhere")
        expect(strip).to_be_visible()
        strip.click()                                      # a touch
        expect(bar.get_by_text("offline", exact=True)).to_be_visible()
        print("  PASS: the frame owns up to a dead link")
    finally:
        for d in docs: gql(DELETE, {"cid": d["cid"]})
        unserve_bytes(*SEND_BYTES)
Handing the slide to a phone
what
the doc on the cabinet is often one you want to send to someone right then — and the conversation you would send it in is on your phone.
what
the tablet has no way to hand a file to an app on another device.
  • therefore: the phone has to fetch it.
who
the companion, a small app on the phone, does that: it holds whatever the frame is showing and passes it to the phone’s own share sheet.
rule
everything memories owes it is a name for the doc.
The room the name goes into
what
that name lives in a shared document — a room on the house’s sync server, holding one entry that every frame writes and the companion reads.
  • what: it is a heavier instrument than one value needs.
  • what: the companion is a page with no server of its own.
    • therefore: nothing can hand it an update unless the update arrives over a connection it already holds.
how
Yjs, a shared-document library, holds such a document, and y-websocket carries it over a socket.
  • rule: Yjs has Solid’s one-instance requirement and meets it the same way: the socket library comes in marked ?external=yjs so that it and the import map’s own yjs are the same copy.
  • what: two copies fail quietly in the worst way: the room connects, reports itself live, and never syncs anything.

import * as Y from 'yjs';
import { WebsocketProvider } from 'y-websocket';
how
a frame works out which room and which server for itself: the sync server answers on the same host the app was loaded from, so swapping the scheme is the whole of it.
how
both can be named at launch as well, the way every app here that joins a room takes its address.

const frameParam = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const SYNC_URL = frameParam.get('yws') || location.origin.replace(/^http/, 'ws') + '/ywebsocket';
const SYNC_ROOM = frameParam.get('room') || 'memories-nowshowing';
const [roomLink, setRoomLink] = createSignal('idle');
A frame names its slide unasked
rule
a frame names every slide it comes to rest on, unasked.
  • rule: you look up from the cabinet, take out your phone, and the doc has to be there already.
what
a name is both of the doc’s addresses — the downscaled copy and the original — what kind of file it is, and when the doc was taken.
  • rule: the companion offers you the choice between the two that the lightbox, one doc opened large over the wall, already draws.
  • rule: the kind lets the companion build a file the share sheet will accept.
  • what: the date is what the companion calls the file it hands over.
  • what: only the archive knows that date.
    • therefore: a frame that kept it to itself would leave the companion handing over a file it cannot name.
  • how: In practice the archive gives an instant back in its own offset rather than the Z it was handed, so the two read differently as text while naming the same moment; what is checked is the instant, not its spelling.
  • what: the companion is served from elsewhere and reaches the archive by its own route.
    • therefore: it is the one that can turn an address into something it can fetch.
    • therefore: the addresses go out exactly as the doc carries them, unresolved.

# nothing is touched here: entering the show is the whole of it
wait_until(page, lambda: bool(named()), label="the frame names its slide unasked")
said, shown = named(), docs[photo]
assert said["cid"] == shown["cid"], f"named the wrong doc: {said}"
assert said["webCid"] == shown["webCid"], f"no downscaled address: {said}"
assert said["mimetype"] == shown["mimetype"], f"no file kind: {said}"
assert page.evaluate("([a, b]) => Date.parse(a) === Date.parse(b)",
                     [said.get("date"), shown["date"]]), \
    f"named a different instant than the doc's {shown['date']}: {said}"
print("  PASS: frame publishes what is showing")
rule
a name rides the settle — the show coming to rest after a step — not the scroll.
  • how: the centred slide reads true long before the short wait after scrolling stops, so a step only counts as over once the show has come to rest, and that is when the next name goes out.
rule
keep browsing and the name keeps up with you.

page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")                          # a step, with nothing touched
wait_until(page, lambda: (named() or {}).get("cid") == docs[never_downscaled]["cid"],
           label="the name follows the slide", detail=lambda: str(named()))
print("  PASS: the name follows the slide")
how
the centred doc’s name is written again each time the show settles.

let showingRoom = null;
const nowShowing = () => {
    if(!showingRoom){
        const shared = new Y.Doc();
        const provider = new WebsocketProvider(SYNC_URL, SYNC_ROOM, shared);
        setRoomLink('connecting');
        provider.on('status', e => setRoomLink(e.status === 'connected' ? 'live' : 'offline'));
        showingRoom = shared.getMap('showing');
    }
    return showingRoom;
};
createEffect(() => {
    if(!frame()) return;
    pokes();
    const d = frameDoc(); if(!d) return;
    nowShowing().set('doc', { cid: d.cid, webCid: d.webCid, mimetype: d.mimetype, date: d.date });
});
Several frames, one room
what
memories runs on the phones as much as on the cabinet.
  • therefore: several frames can be playing at once, all writing that same one entry.
rule
the last frame to settle wins, with no arbitration.
rule
where two really are going at once, a touch breaks the tie.
  • rule: taking the room back is the one thing a touch is for: if another frame has spoken over you, touching yours puts your slide back without your having to move it.

speak_over(page.context, "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzelsewhere")              # another frame claims the room
wait_until(page, lambda: (named() or {}).get("cid") == "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzelsewhere")
strip.click()                                              # a touch, and the slide is not moved
wait_until(page, lambda: (named() or {}).get("cid") == docs[never_downscaled]["cid"],
           label="a touch takes the room back", detail=lambda: str(named()))
print("  PASS: a touch takes the room back")
how
In practice, reading pokes() in the naming effect — the counter the show already bumps on every touch — is what makes a touch republish.
  • how: an effect re-runs when anything it read has changed: the settle path comes from the doc, and the claim path from the counter, so nothing has to notice which of the two happened.
The link, in one word on the control bar
rule
the socket opens on the first slide a frame names and lives as long as the page does — on a cabinet tablet, for days.
what
naming a slide is a thing you cannot see working: the frame writes, says nothing, and looks exactly the same whether the name arrived or the socket is down.
  • what: if it is down, somebody on a sofa is looking at a phone that still shows the last doc the room heard about.
  • what: the person standing at the frame is the only one who can notice.
rule
the control bar carries the link’s state in one word beside the date.
  • what: idle until a slide has been named, connecting while the socket is being opened, then live or offline for as long as it holds or does not.
rule
a frame whose names are landing says so.

wait_until(page, lambda: bar.get_by_text("live", exact=True).count() == 1,
           label="the bar says the link is live",
           detail=lambda: f"the bar is up: {bar.is_visible()}; it reads "
                          f"{bar.text_content() if bar.count() else '—'!r}")
print("  PASS: the bar says the link is live")
how
the room’s socket reports its status, and the word follows it.

setRoomLink('connecting');
provider.on('status', e => setRoomLink(e.status === 'connected' ? 'live' : 'offline'));
Owning up to a dead link
what
the word that has to be right is offline, the only one that contradicts what the screen otherwise implies.
what
a frame pointed somewhere nothing answers looks exactly like a frame whose every slide is landing.
  • how: pointing one nowhere takes a little care: the browser vetoes the low port numbers on its own, before any connection is attempted, so a frame aimed at one of those never learns anything about its link.
  • how: a high port nobody is listening on is refused outright, which is the answer wanted.
rule
such a frame says offline.

expect(bar.get_by_text("offline", exact=True)).to_be_visible()
print("  PASS: the frame owns up to a dead link")
who
whoever reads that word is standing back from a screen on a cabinet, and is not looking for it anyway — they are looking at the doc.
rule
the word catches the eye when it is bad news and otherwise stays out of the way.
  • what: only one of the four states is bad news.
  • rule: only offline takes a colour that interrupts, the two that are on their way somewhere share a muted one, and live stays quiet.

<span class="room-link" data-state=${roomLink}>${roomLink}</span>


.frame-bar .room-link{ font:10px/1.6 monospace; text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:.08em;
                       color:#6a7; }
.frame-bar .room-link[data-state="offline"]{ color:#d55; }
.frame-bar .room-link[data-state="connecting"],
.frame-bar .room-link[data-state="idle"]{ color:#aa6; }
Taking the files
what
past triage you often just want the files: a web copy — the downscaled one — to hand over now, and the original to rework.
rule
the toolbar’s ↓ group saves the picked docs, one file each, at whichever of the two you ask for, and hands over no other rendition.
  • scope: like the move, it acts on the picked docs only, there being no list of the whole filter at hand to fetch.

tiles(page).nth(photo).click()                          # the one worth sending
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(1)
tb, got = toolbar(page), {}
for res in ["web", "orig"]:
    with page.expect_download() as di:
        tb.get_by_role("button", name=res, exact=True).click()
    got[res] = (di.value.url, di.value.suggested_filename)
assert docs[photo]["webCid"] in got["web"][0], f"web → webCid: {got}"
assert docs[photo]["cid"] in got["orig"][0], f"orig → the doc's own cid: {got}"
print("  PASS: download selection")
rule
a doc missing that rendition is passed over rather than served its original in the rendition’s place.
  • how: the photo never downscaled joins the first, and asking the pair for web brings down one file, not two.

tiles(page).nth(never_downscaled).click()
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(2)
saved = []                                              # armed here: only this click's files count
page.on("download", lambda d: saved.append(d.url))
toolbar(page).get_by_role("button", name="web", exact=True).click()
wait_until(page, lambda: len(saved) >= 1, label="the doc that has a web copy saves it")
page.wait_for_timeout(500)                              # room for a second, unwanted save to land
assert len(saved) == 1, f"expected the one web copy, got {len(saved)}: {saved}"
assert docs[photo]["webCid"] in saved[0], f"the wrong rendition came down: {saved[0]}"
print("  PASS: download skips a missing rendition")
what
measures the second not overwriting the first: each saved file carries its rendition in its name, holiday-orig.jpg beside holiday-web.jpg.
  • how: In practice nothing is downloaded again: the names of the two forms already in hand are read.

names = {res: name for res, (_, name) in got.items()}   # the two the photo just yielded
assert len({*names.values()}) == len(names), f"same name → they collide in the folder: {names}"
for res in names:
    assert res in names[res], f"rendition missing from the name: {names}"
print("  PASS: download names by resolution")
how
the photos are put down and the clip taken up alone, as the one whose two forms disagree about their type.
rule
the extension follows the rendition: a clip’s web copy is an MP4, a photo’s a JPEG, and the original keeps its true type, as the archive records it.
  • what: an address carries no extension and a missing object answers text/plain, so a name taken from either is unopenable.
  • example: a .mov original saves as …-orig.mov, and its web copy as …-web.mp4.

tiles(page).nth(photo).click()
tiles(page).nth(never_downscaled).click()
tiles(page).nth(video).click()
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(1)
tb, ext = toolbar(page), {}
for res in ["orig", "web"]:
    with page.expect_download() as di:
        tb.get_by_role("button", name=res, exact=True).click()
    ext[res] = di.value.suggested_filename.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
assert ext["orig"] == "mov", f"original keeps its real type: {ext}"
assert ext["web"] == "mp4", f"a clip's web copy is mp4: {ext}"
print("  PASS: download extensions by rendition")
what
the browser asks once before saving several.
how
each picked doc is saved through a link of its own, named after the doc and the rendition asked for.

const MIME_EXT = { 'image/jpeg': 'jpg', 'image/png': 'png', 'image/gif': 'gif',
                   'image/webp': 'webp', 'image/heic': 'heic', 'image/heif': 'heif',
                   'image/tiff': 'tiff', 'video/quicktime': 'mov', 'video/x-matroska': 'mkv',
                   'video/x-msvideo': 'avi' };
const extOf = mt => MIME_EXT[mt] || (mt && mt.split('/')[1]) || '';
function downloadSelection(res){
    const byCid = new Map(items().map(p => [p.cid, p]));
    for(const cid of selected()){
        const p = byCid.get(cid); if(!p) continue;
        const path = res === 'web' ? p.webCid : p.cid;
        if(!path) continue;
        const isVid = (p.mimetype || '').startsWith('video');
        const ext = res === 'web' ? (isVid ? 'mp4' : 'jpg') : extOf(p.mimetype);
        const raw = p.filename || p.cid.split('/').pop() || 'download';
        const dot = raw.lastIndexOf('.'), base = dot > 0 ? raw.slice(0, dot) : raw;
        const a = document.createElement('a');
        a.href = IPFS + path;
        a.download = ext ? `${base}-${res}.${ext}` : `${base}-${res}`;
        document.body.appendChild(a); a.click(); a.remove();
    }
}

The cabinet plays on its own

what
a tablet sits on the cabinet showing the archive, and nobody tends it.
  • how: you set a search going and walk off; it plays through by itself.
  • what: somebody passing touches the screen, gets the controls, reads what per is looking at, and leaves — and the controls tidy themselves away.
  • what: relaunch it and it is still showing, on the slide it stopped on.
    • rule: only when you deliberately leave the show does it stay left.
what
its tempo and the patience of its control bar are the two knobs the show runs on — a minute a slide and twenty seconds of bar by default.
  • how: the cabinet here is wound to a second or two.
  • what: the third number is the suite’s own: how long to leave a just-exited show alone before believing it really isn’t coming back.

CABINET_MS, CABINET_UI_IDLE_MS = 1200, 2000
CABINET_QS = f"?ms={CABINET_MS}&uiidle={CABINET_UI_IDLE_MS}"
FRAME_REENTRY_GRACE_MS = 300
how
the suite’s three standing docs give it a short loop to play, and the show opens on the wall — the grid of thumbnails — they make.
  • what: one occasion is laid over all three of them.
    • therefore: whichever slide the show happens to be resting on has something to say about itself.

CABINET_EVENT = "zzVacancesCabinet"
CABINET_FROM, CABINET_TO = "2020-01-01T00:00:00Z", "2020-03-31T23:59:59Z"
CABINET_EVENTS = [{"rowId": "zzcab-ev", "summary": CABINET_EVENT, "owner": "konubinix",
                   "status": "confirmed", "starttime": CABINET_FROM, "endtime": CABINET_TO}]
what
the passer-by who stops also gets an add-label box.
  • rule: what it offers has to come from somewhere.
    • how: the cabinet brings two words and takes them away after.
      • what: one answers a prefix and is nowhere near these slides.
      • what: one is laid on every slide before the show starts.
        • therefore: whichever slide it is resting on already wears it.
      • what: both answer to the same stem, which is what a prefix has to reach.

CABINET_STEM = "zzcab"
CABINET_FREE, CABINET_WORN = "zzcabfree", "zzcabworn"
CABINET_WORDS = [CABINET_FREE, CABINET_WORN]
what
the show says whether a picture is still arriving or never will.
  • what: saying so is a promise with its own run of slides.
how
it wants one doc in each of the three states there is anything to say about.
  • example: one whose thumbnail arrives and whose full-res never does, so the picture is up with something sharper still pending.
  • example: one where nothing arrives at all.
  • example: one where both arrive, so that there is a slide with nothing left to announce.
  • how: the bytes they answer with are the smallest picture that is still a picture — a single pixel.

MARK_LABEL = "zzmark"
MARK_DOCS = [{"cid": f"https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzmark-{i}", "date": f"2020-0{i + 1}-15T12:00:00Z",
              "mimetype": "image/jpeg", "thumbnailCid": f"https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzmark-t-{i}",
              "webCid": f"https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzmark-web-{i}", "labels": MARK_LABEL, "state": "todo"}
             for i in range(3)]
MARK_ARRIVES = ("zzmark-t-0",                    # the picture, but never anything sharper
                "zzmark-t-2", "zzmark-web-2")    # both — and nothing at all for the one between them
ONE_PIXEL = _b64.b64decode("iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAQAAAC1HAwCAAAAC0lEQVR42mP8z8BQDwAEhQGAhKmMIQAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==")


@testcase
def test_the_cabinet_plays_on_its_own(page):
    """A tablet left on the cabinet: it advances by itself, yields its controls to a
    passer-by — including a box that completes on the archive's own words — comes back
    where it was after a relaunch, and says which of its pictures are still on the way."""
    make_fixtures()
    for f in FIXTURES:                                   # the worn word, on every slide
        gql(UPDATE, {"cid": f["cid"], "patch": {"labels": f"{FIXTURE_LABEL}; {CABINET_WORN}"}})
    seed_vocab(CABINET_WORDS)
    seed_events(CABINET_EVENTS)
    for d in MARK_DOCS: gql(DELETE, {"cid": d["cid"]}); gql(CREATE, {"p": d})
    for c in MARK_ARRIVES:
        page.route(f"**/ipfs/{c}", lambda r: r.fulfill(status=200, content_type="image/png", body=ONE_PIXEL))
    try:
        open_app(page, CABINET_QS)
        search_for(page, FIXTURE_LABEL)
        chip(page, "all").click()
        expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(len(FIXTURES))
        page.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile("frame", re.I)).click()
        strip = page.get_by_role("list", name="slideshow")

        bar = page.get_by_role("toolbar", name="frame actions")
        for src in ["thumb-0", "thumb-1", "thumb-2"]:                   # date order
            wait_until(page, lambda s=src: strip.evaluate(CENTERED) == f"https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzbatchfix-{s}")
        print("  PASS: frame auto-advances")

        colours = [bar.get_by_role("button", name=st, exact=True).evaluate("el => getComputedStyle(el).color")
                   for st in ["todo", "next", "done", "delete"]]
        assert len(set(colours)) == 4, f"each state pill should have its own colour, got {colours}"

        def shown(k):     # the date the bar should be reading, as the browser renders it

        expect(slides.nth(1).get_by_label("loading")).to_be_visible()  # the mark came with the new doc

    finally:
        for c in MARK_ARRIVES: page.unroute(f"**/ipfs/{c}")
        for d in MARK_DOCS: gql(DELETE, {"cid": d["cid"]})
        drop_events(CABINET_EVENTS)
        drop_vocab(CABINET_WORDS)
The frame — a fullscreen slideshow
what
left to itself the app becomes a photo frame — the show: a fullscreen slideshow over whatever the wall is showing.
  • what: no separate app: ▶ frame turns the current wall, whatever the query language has narrowed it to, into a show.
what
the show is not the lightbox — one doc opened large over the wall — but a full-screen horizontal filmstrip, the strip: each doc a viewport-wide slide, laid side by side in a native scroll container.
  • what: it has the feel of a hand-built slider: a fluid lateral swipe whose momentum coasts across several slides, easing onto whichever one it comes to rest nearest.
what
it plays the wall in the order shown — chronological by default, or the random draw under sort:random.
  • scope: ordering is an app-wide concern, not a frame one.
what
clips don’t auto-play, and there’s no chrome.
  • what: a small control bar (pause, interval, exit) is a tap away.
how
the frame is one layer over the wall: the strip, and the control bar laid over it as a sibling — outside the strip that reads taps — so a press on the bar’s own buttons is never taken for a tap on the show.

<${Show} when=${() => frame()}>
  <div class="frame">
    <div class="strip" role="list" aria-label="slideshow"
         ref=${el => { stripEl = el; el.addEventListener('scroll', onFrameScroll); }}>
      <${Index} each=${() => frameSlides()}>${(slide, k) => FrameSlide(slide, k)}<//>
    </div>
    <${Show} when=${() => frameUI()}>
      <div class="frame-bar" role="toolbar" aria-label="frame actions" onPointerDown=${nudge}>
        <button aria-label=${() => playing() ? 'pause' : 'play'}
                onClick=${() => setPlaying(p => !p)}>${() => playing() ? '⏸' : '▶'}</button>
        <label>every <input class="ivl" type="number" min="2" aria-label="seconds per photo"
               value=${() => Math.round(intervalMs() / 1000)}
               onChange=${e => setIntervalMs(Math.max(2, +e.target.value) * 1000)} />s</label>
        <${Show} when=${() => frameEditingDate()}
                 fallback=${html`<button class="frame-date" aria-label="edit date"
                     onClick=${() => setFrameEditingDate(true)}>${() => { const d = frameDoc();
                       return d?.date ? new Date(d.date).toLocaleString("fr-FR") : ''; }}</button>`}>
          <input class="frame-date-edit" type="datetime-local" aria-label="date"
                 ref=${el => { el.value = toLocalInput(frameDoc()?.date); requestAnimationFrame(() => el.focus()); }}
                 onKeyDown=${e => { if(e.key === 'Enter'){ e.preventDefault(); e.target.blur(); } else if(e.key === 'Escape'){ e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); frameCancelDate = true; e.target.blur(); } }}
                 onBlur=${e => frameCommitDate(e.target.value)} />
        <//>
        <span class="room-link" data-state=${roomLink}>${roomLink}</span>
        <${For} each=${() => frameEvents() || []}>${e => html`
          <button class="frame-event" onClick=${() => { searchEvent(e.summary); exitFrame(); }}>${() => e.summary}<span class="ev-when">${() => eventWhen(e)}</span></button>`}
        <//>
        ${STATES.map(st => html`
          <button class="st" data-st=${st} onClick=${() => frameSetState(st)}>${st}</button>`)}
        <div class="complete">
          <input class="frame-label" role="combobox" placeholder="add a label…" aria-label="add a label in the frame"
                 aria-expanded=${() => frameLabelFocus() && (sugLoading() || sugItems().length > 0) ? 'true' : 'false'}
                 value=${() => frameLabel()} onInput=${e => { setFrameLabel(e.target.value); setFrameLabelFocus(true); }}
                 onFocus=${() => setFrameLabelFocus(true)}
                 onBlur=${() => setFrameLabelFocus(false)}
                 onKeyDown=${e => { if(e.key === 'Enter' && e.shiftKey){ e.preventDefault(); frameDropLabel(); return; }
                   sugNav(e, w => w ? setFrameLabel(replaceSeg(frameLabel(), w) + '; ') : frameAddLabel()); }} />
          <${Show} when=${() => frameLabelFocus()}>
            <${Suggest} text=${frameLabel} present=${() => labelsOf(frameDoc())}
                        active=${sugActive} onItems=${reportSug} onLoading=${setSugLoading}
                        onPick=${w => setFrameLabel(replaceSeg(frameLabel(), w) + '; ')} />
          <//>
        </div>
        <button aria-label="exit frame" onClick=${exitFrame}>✕ exit</button>
      </div>
    <//>
  </div>
<//>


.frame-bar{ position:fixed; bottom:calc(18px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom));
            left:50%; transform:translateX(-50%); z-index:3;
            display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:8px 12px; align-items:center; justify-content:center;
            max-width:92vw; background:#11131fdd; border:1px solid #3a3f5a;
            border-radius:10px; padding:8px 14px; font-size:14px; color:#cdd; }

.frame-bar .st{ font-size:12px; text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:.03em;
                border:1px solid #3a3f5a; border-radius:5px; padding:3px 8px; }
[data-st="todo"]{   --st:#6cf; }
[data-st="next"]{   --st:#fb7; }
[data-st="done"]{   --st:#7d7; }
[data-st="delete"]{ --st:#f77; }
button[data-st]:active{ transform:scale(0.9); filter:brightness(1.2); }

.frame-bar .ivl{ width:48px; background:#262a40; color:var(--fg); border:1px solid #3a3f5a;
                 border-radius:4px; padding:3px 5px; }

                        font-family:inherit; cursor:pointer; }
.frame-bar .frame-date:hover{ color:#ccd; text-decoration:underline; }
.frame-bar .frame-date-edit{ font-size:13px; color:var(--fg); background:#262a40; border:1px solid #3a3f5a;
                             border-radius:5px; padding:3px 6px; }
.frame-bar .frame-label{ background:#262a40; color:var(--fg); border:1px solid #3a3f5a;
                         border-radius:5px; padding:4px 8px; font-size:13px; }
.frame-bar .suggest{ top:auto; bottom:100%; margin:0 0 4px; }   /* open upward from the bar */
what
everything the frame does is a reaction to a small cluster of state: whether it is open and playing, which slide has settled, and whether a pinch has taken hold.
  • what: the settled slide comes with its place on the strip, so the slides loaded around it know where they are.
how
the state is kept together, so every reaction below reads one live picture.

const [frame, setFrame] = createSignal(false);
const [playing, setPlaying] = createSignal(true);
const [frameUI, setFrameUI] = createSignal(false);     // controls revealed on tap
const [frameLabel, setFrameLabel] = createSignal('');
const [frameLabelFocus, setFrameLabelFocus] = createSignal(false);
const [frameCenterCid, setFrameCenterCid] = createSignal(null);   // the settled slide
const frameDoc = () => items().find(p => p.cid === frameCenterCid());   // the centred doc
const [frameEditingDate, setFrameEditingDate] = createSignal(false);
const [frameCenterIdx, setFrameCenterIdx] = createSignal(1);
const [frameDir, setFrameDir] = createSignal(1);                  // last travel direction (+1 forward)
const FRAME_MS = Number(new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('ms')) || 60000;
const [intervalMs, setIntervalMs] = createSignal(FRAME_MS);
const FRAME_IDLE_MS = Number(new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('idleresume')) || 60000;
const [pokes, setPokes] = createSignal(0);
const nudge = () => setPokes(n => n + 1);
const [interacting, setInteracting] = createSignal(false);
const [zoomed, setZoomed] = createSignal(false);
Which slide it rests on
what
which slide the show has come to rest on is a question the strip cannot answer directly: a filmstrip has no notion of a current item, only a scroll offset.
how
In practice the answer is arithmetic — the offset divided by a slide’s width, rounded to the nearest.
  • rule: the width is the one the show itself places slides by, the strip’s own rather than the viewport’s, or the reading drifts from the thing it is measuring.
    • what: the two differ, as the measure the show places by tells.
how
the question is asked in five shapes.
  • example: the bare position along the strip.
  • example: the picture sitting there.
  • example: which of the suite’s standing docs that picture belongs to.
  • example: whether what has come to rest is a clip at all — a clip’s slide holds no picture, so the shape that reads a picture’s address has nothing to say about one.
  • example: how much of the screen whatever is there covers — a photo and a clip answering the same question, so it asks after neither by name.

SLIDE_W = "el => (el.scrollWidth / (el.children.length || 1)) || 1"

ON_SLIDE = f"el => Math.round(el.scrollLeft / ({SLIDE_W})(el))"

CENTERED = (f"el => {{ const w = ({SLIDE_W})(el); const i = Math.round(el.scrollLeft / w);"
            " const im = el.children[i] && el.children[i].querySelector('img');"
            " return im && im.getAttribute('src'); }")

CENTERED_IS_CLIP = (f"el => {{ const w = ({SLIDE_W})(el); const i = Math.round(el.scrollLeft / w);"
                    " return !!(el.children[i] && el.children[i].querySelector('video')); }")

CENTERED_MEDIA = (f"el => {{ const w = ({SLIDE_W})(el); const i = Math.round(el.scrollLeft / w);"
                  " const m = el.children[i] && el.children[i].querySelector('video, img');"
                  " if(!m) return null; const r = m.getBoundingClientRect();"
                  " return { width: r.width, height: r.height,"
                  " fit: getComputedStyle(m).objectFit }; }")

def centred_slide(strip):
    src = strip.evaluate(CENTERED) or ""
    return next((k for k, f in enumerate(FIXTURES) if f["thumbnailCid"] == src), None)
Moving through the show

  • Playing, and yielding to a touch

    what : measures it plays through by itself. - how: a ?ms= launch parameter overrides the minute a slide. - what: it runs in date order, so the suite’s standing docs play thumb-0, thumb-1, thumb-2.

    for src in ["thumb-0", "thumb-1", "thumb-2"]:                   # date order
    wait_until(page, lambda s=src: strip.evaluate(CENTERED) == f"https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzbatchfix-{s}")
print("  PASS: frame auto-advances")

    how : one interval timer drives it, standing down while anything holds the show, and each tick smooth-scrolls one slide on from wherever the strip currently sits, so a swipe in between is respected.

    const FRAME_MS = Number(new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('ms')) || 60000;
const [intervalMs, setIntervalMs] = createSignal(FRAME_MS);


    createEffect(() => { if(!frame()) return; const vv = window.visualViewport; if(!vv) return;
    const read = () => setZoomed(vv.scale > 1);
    read(); vv.addEventListener('resize', read); vv.addEventListener('scroll', read);
    onCleanup(() => { vv.removeEventListener('resize', read); vv.removeEventListener('scroll', read); }); });
createEffect(() => {
    if(!frame() || !playing() || zoomed() || interacting()) return;
    const id = setInterval(() => {
        if(stripEl && [...stripEl.querySelectorAll('video')].some(v => !v.paused && !v.ended)) return;
        frameGo(1);
    }, intervalMs());
    onCleanup(() => clearInterval(id));
});
createEffect(() => { if(!pokes()) return;
    setInteracting(true);
    const id = setTimeout(() => setInteracting(false), FRAME_IDLE_MS); onCleanup(() => clearTimeout(id)); });
createEffect(() => { if(!frame() || !stripEl) return;
    stripEl.addEventListener('pointerdown', nudge);
    onCleanup(() => stripEl.removeEventListener('pointerdown', nudge)); });

    what : measures it yields the moment it is touched, and picks up again once you have gone. - how: any tap or swipe stops the auto-advance, which picks back up only after a span of quiet — a minute, which ?idleresume overrides. - therefore: a slide you’ve stopped on to look at is never pulled out from under you.

    opened = strip.evaluate(ON_SLIDE)                              # wherever the show resumed
wait_until(page, lambda: strip.evaluate(ON_SLIDE) > opened,    # …and it is advancing from there
           label="the show is running before we touch it")
page.mouse.click(box["x"] + box["width"] / 2, box["y"] + box["height"] / 2)  # a centre tap: real interaction, no nav
page.wait_for_timeout(LIVE_MS + LIVE_SETTLE_MS)                # let any in-flight step settle
held = strip.evaluate(ON_SLIDE)
page.wait_for_timeout(LIVE_RESUME_MS // 2)                     # several tempo ticks, still inside the resume span
assert strip.evaluate(ON_SLIDE) == held, f"interaction must stop the show; it drifted {held}→{strip.evaluate(ON_SLIDE)}"
wait_until(page, lambda: strip.evaluate(ON_SLIDE) > held)      # quiet long enough → resumes on its own
print("  PASS: frame pauses on interaction")

    how : a press on the strip marks the show busy, and the mark lapses once that span has passed since the last press.

    const FRAME_IDLE_MS = Number(new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('idleresume')) || 60000;
const [pokes, setPokes] = createSignal(0);
const nudge = () => setPokes(n => n + 1);
const [interacting, setInteracting] = createSignal(false);


    createEffect(() => { if(!pokes()) return;
    setInteracting(true);
    const id = setTimeout(() => setInteracting(false), FRAME_IDLE_MS); onCleanup(() => clearTimeout(id)); });
createEffect(() => { if(!frame() || !stripEl) return;
    stripEl.addEventListener('pointerdown', nudge);
    onCleanup(() => stripEl.removeEventListener('pointerdown', nudge)); });

  • Flinging the strip

    what : the swipe is the frame’s main gesture: you fling the strip and it coasts a few slides on its own momentum, like the slider it grew out of.

    what : the browser’s own scroll-snap reaches for that feel but overshoots — a quick flick is flung clear across the wall, ten slides gone in one careless swipe.

    what : a mouse drag carries no momentum. - therefore: the behaviour only shows under a real touch fling. - how: both checks below ride one such fling, driven (as for the lightbox) through Chromium’s touch pipeline: the finger flies left across the screen and lets go.

    what : knowing when the fling is over is the awkward part, because the strip goes still twice. - what: momentum runs out first, then the settle waits out its own beat of quiet before easing onto the nearest slide. - therefore: a reading taken during that lull would measure a resting place the show is about to leave. - how: the test insists on a stillness longer than the beat — seven still reads, 100ms apart: only the rest that follows the ease can be that quiet, and any motion starts the count again. - how: the ceiling on waiting, six seconds, clears the worst case — the fling, the beat and the ease together.

    what : that first lull is where momentum alone left the strip — the resting place the ease exists to correct, and the only evidence that there was anything to correct. - what: each question asked from outside costs a round trip, and two of them together are already about as long as the beat. - therefore: an answer from outside is as likely to describe the strip after the ease as before it. - how: the lull is found where it happens: the strip reports every scroll it makes, timestamped, and the beat is the one gap in that record wide enough to be the show waiting. - how: whatever the strip read just before that gap is where momentum left it, and everything after is the ease.

    rule : what counts as wide enough is pinned on both sides. - what: too wide, and it reaches past the beat into the ease, which reports its own scrolls a frame apart. - what: too narrow, and an ordinary stutter in the fling passes for the show’s wait. - how: a 30ms grace under the beat clears both: longer than any gap momentum makes, shorter than the one gap it is looking for.

    SETTLE_BEAT_MS = 150            # the show's own wait for quiet before it eases
FRAME_MS = 30                   # the grace under it: wider than any gap momentum makes
STILL_READS = 7                 # a stillness longer than that beat, in 100ms reads
SETTLE_CAP_MS = 6000            # fling + beat + ease, with room to spare
CENTRED_PX = 20                 # slack against a boundary
FLING_TRIES = 4                 # flings, until one coasts to rest off a boundary

# Record every scroll the strip makes, then read the beat back out of the record.
TRACE_SCROLL = """el => { const s = []; el.__scrolls = s;
    el.addEventListener('scroll', () => s.push([performance.now(), el.scrollLeft])); }"""
COASTED_AT = """(el, beat) => { const s = el.__scrolls || [];
    for(let i = 1; i < s.length; i++) if(s[i][0] - s[i - 1][0] > beat) return s[i - 1][1];
    return s.length ? s[s.length - 1][1] : null; }"""

def hard_frame_flick(page, strip):
    """A hard, fast touch fling — the finger flies ~900px left in ten quick steps —
    returning where momentum alone left the strip, and once the ease has come to rest."""
    box = strip.bounding_box()
    cx, cy = box["x"] + box["width"] / 2, box["y"] + box["height"] / 2
    strip.evaluate(TRACE_SCROLL)
    cdp = page.context.new_cdp_session(page)
    cdp.send("Input.dispatchTouchEvent", {"type": "touchStart", "touchPoints": [{"x": cx, "y": cy}]})
    for k in range(1, 11):
        cdp.send("Input.dispatchTouchEvent", {"type": "touchMove", "touchPoints": [{"x": cx - 90 * k, "y": cy}]})
        time.sleep(0.001)
    cdp.send("Input.dispatchTouchEvent", {"type": "touchEnd", "touchPoints": []})
    prev, stable, step = None, 0, 100
    for _ in range(SETTLE_CAP_MS // step):
        cur = strip.evaluate("el => el.scrollLeft")
        stable = stable + 1 if (prev is not None and abs(cur - prev) < 1) else 0
        if stable >= STILL_READS: break
        prev = cur; page.wait_for_timeout(step)
    return strip.evaluate(COASTED_AT, SETTLE_BEAT_MS - FRAME_MS)
Showing each doc

  • Saying a picture is on its way

    rule : a doc with nothing yet to show says so rather than sit black: it reads as loading, not broken. - how: until the thumbnail base paints, the slide carries a 🖼 mark — the wall’s missing-thumbnail glyph — labelled loading, so a screen reader announces it too. - rule: the instant the thumbnail’s load fires, the mark clears and the picture stands.

    expect(slides.nth(2).get_by_label("loading")).to_be_visible()   # its thumbnail never arrives: still loading
wait_until(page, lambda: slides.nth(1).get_by_label("loading").count() == 0,
           label="the mark clears on the slide whose thumbnail arrived")
print("  PASS: frame shows placeholder while loading")

    what : once the thumbnail stands, a near doc’s web copy may still be on its way: the picture is already up, only sharper detail is pending.

    how : In practice the clearing of the mark below is read on the slide where both arrive, in two steps: the picture is established first, and from there the mark’s absence is the landing. - what: the absence of a mark means nothing on its own — a slide with no picture yet has none either.

    rule : a quieter mark takes the big one’s place: a small pulse tucked in the corner, labelled fetching full resolution, that reads as “this is the thumbnail; the full image is coming.” - rule: when the web copy paints over the base, it clears.

    expect(slides.nth(1).get_by_label("fetching full resolution")).to_be_visible()   # picture up, full-res still out
wait_until(page, lambda: slides.nth(3).get_by_label("loading").count() == 0,
           label="the picture is up on the slide where both arrive")
expect(slides.nth(3).get_by_label("fetching full resolution")).to_have_count(0)  # …and nothing sharper is pending
print("  PASS: frame thumbnail shows upgrade mark")

  • The marks follow what the box shows

    what : a slide is a reused box: after an edit re-anchors the show (a doc leaves the filter and the strip closes the gap), a box that held one doc comes to hold another.

    rule : the mark follows the new doc, not lingering from the old: a freshly-shown doc whose image is still arriving wears the mark even though its box had finished loading something else.

    strip.click()                                                  # the bar, on the doc the show opened on
bar.get_by_role("button", name="done", exact=True).click()     # it leaves todo → its box goes to the one that never arrives
wait_until(page, lambda: (strip.evaluate(CENTERED) or "").endswith("zzmark-t-1"),
           label="the box that had finished loading now holds the doc that never will")
expect(slides.nth(1).get_by_label("loading")).to_be_visible()  # the mark came with the new doc
print("  PASS: frame placeholder after edit remaps slot")

    what : a slot swap is not the only way a slide’s base image changes under it: as the centre moves, a slide keeps its doc but its base layer is re-picked — a blank far out, the thumbnail in range. - what: a slide flung in from the blank band carries an already-painted blank.

    rule : the big mark keys on the base layer’s current source: it returns whenever that source changes — a new doc dropped in the box, or the thumbnail re-picked for the doc already there — and clears once the thumbnail paints.

    far_mark = strip.get_by_role("listitem").nth(FAR).get_by_label("loading")
expect(far_mark).to_have_count(0)         # let go of, and its blank painted: nothing to announce
goto(FAR)                                 # fling onto it
expect(far_mark).to_have_count(1)         # its source turns real → the mark is back until that paints
print("  PASS: frame placeholder returns on band flip")

    how : the slide stacks two images — the thumbnail base and, when close enough, the web copy overlay above it — with the marks between them. - how: each layer re-arms its own mark when its source changes (a new doc, a band that swaps blank↔thumbnail, or one that adds or drops the overlay), so neither mark lingers from a source no longer shown.

    const FrameSlide = (slide, k) => {
    const thumbSrc = createMemo(() => thumbBand(slide(), k));   // base layer's source
    const webSrc = createMemo(() => webBand(slide(), k));       // overlay's source ('' when far from centre)
    const [thumbOn, setThumbOn] = createSignal(false);          // the base thumbnail has painted
    const [webOn, setWebOn] = createSignal(false);              // the full-res overlay has painted
    createEffect(() => { thumbSrc(); setThumbOn(false); });     // each layer re-arms its mark on its own source change
    createEffect(() => { webSrc(); setWebOn(false); });
    return html`
    <div class="slide" role="listitem">
      <${Show} when=${() => hasMedia(slide())}
               fallback=${html`<div class="slide-media noimg">
                 <span class="ph">${() => isVideo(slide()) ? '🎬' : '🖼'}</span></div>`}>
        <${Show} when=${() => isVideo(slide())}
                 fallback=${html`<div class="slide-pic">
                   <${Show} when=${() => !thumbOn()}>
                     <span class="ph load-ph" aria-label="loading">🖼</span><//>
                   <img class="slide-media" loading="lazy"
                        src=${thumbSrc} onLoad=${() => setThumbOn(true)} />
                   <${Show} when=${() => webSrc()}>
                     <img class="slide-media web" classList=${() => ({ shown: webOn() })}
                          loading="lazy" src=${webSrc} onLoad=${() => setWebOn(true)} />
                     <${Show} when=${() => thumbOn() && !webOn()}>
                       <span class="upgrading" aria-label="fetching full resolution"></span><//>
                   <//></div>`}>
          <video class="slide-media" controls src=${() => IPFS + slide().webCid}></video>
        <//>
      <//>
    </div>`;
};

    how : the big mark sits centred over the slide until the picture paints over it, the web copy fades in over the thumbnail, and the quiet mark pulses tucked in a corner.

    /* the loading mark sits centred over the slide until the image paints over it */
.slide-pic{ position:relative; width:100vw; height:100vh; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; }
.slide-pic .load-ph{ position:absolute; font-size:80px; opacity:.5; color:#9aa; }
.slide-pic .slide-media.web{ position:absolute; inset:0; opacity:0; transition:opacity .25s; }  /* full-res fades in over the thumbnail */
.slide-pic .slide-media.web.shown{ opacity:1; }
/* a quiet pulse, corner-tucked, while the full-res is still on its way */
.slide-pic .upgrading{ position:absolute; bottom:16px; right:16px; width:10px; height:10px;
    border-radius:50%; background:#cdd; animation:upgrading 1.3s ease-in-out infinite; }
@keyframes upgrading{ 0%,100%{ opacity:.15 } 50%{ opacity:.6 } }
Triaging from the frame
what
a tap reveals the control bar, and it turns the slideshow into a review station.
  • what: everything on it acts on the centred doc, so you can triage without leaving the show.

  • What the bar says

    rule : the bar’s state buttons are each tinted their own hue — todo cyan, next amber, done green, delete red.

assert len(set(colours)) == 4, f"each state pill should have its own colour, got {colours}"
print("  PASS: frame state pills are colour coded")

  • The bar steps back

    what : measures the controls tidy themselves away. - how: Under the hood the wait below needs no clock of its own: the assertion polls, so the window simply elapses inside it.

    expect(bar).to_be_visible()                       # still up from the tap that raised it
expect(bar).to_be_hidden()                        # and gone once the window has run out
print("  PASS: frame bar auto-hides when idle")

    rule : “quiet” means quiet: any interaction while the bar is up — a tap, a swipe, a press on its own controls — restarts the count. - therefore: it never vanishes mid-use, and leaves only once you have truly stopped. - how: the bar is pressed repeatedly at less than a window’s interval, past the moment a bar that ignored the presses would already have gone, then left alone.

expect(bar).to_be_visible()

    pause.click(); page.wait_for_timeout(CABINET_UI_IDLE_MS // 3)

expect(bar).to_be_visible()                       # still up: each press restarted the count
expect(bar).to_be_hidden()                        # now left alone → it finally hides
print("  PASS: frame bar idle resets on use")

    how : the bar’s window is its own knob — ?uiidle overrides the twenty seconds — apart from the minute of quiet that lets the auto-advance resume. - what: this timer tidies away a menu, that one guards a slide you are studying: they pace different things. - therefore: they don’t share a number.

    how : the count restarts whenever you touch the show, riding the same interaction signal the frame already tracks.

    const FRAME_UI_IDLE_MS = Number(new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('uiidle')) || 20000;
createEffect(() => { if(!frameUI()) return; pokes();
    const id = setTimeout(() => setFrameUI(false), FRAME_UI_IDLE_MS); onCleanup(() => clearTimeout(id)); });

    what : that signal is fed by the strip, and the bar sits beside the strip rather than in it, so a press on the bar’s own controls never reaches it.

    how : the bar forwards its presses there, so working the menu counts as touching the show and keeps it up.

    onPointerDown=${nudge}

  • Coming back after a relaunch

    what : a show that resumes where it went down is hard to catch in the act, in two ways. - what: coming back on the first slide is what a show with no memory does, so if it went down on the opening slide a resume and a cold start are the same picture. - what: a show that is playing wanders onto the right slide by itself within a few ticks, so an answer waited for is no answer at all: the slide it comes back on is read the moment it lands.

    how : In practice both ends of the reboot are pinned down. - what: going down, the slide is written a beat after the show settles on it, so waiting for merely something to be written would accept the slide before last. - what: coming back, the show is placed from what was written only once the wall’s docs are in hand, in an animation frame of its own; before they arrive it sits on the opening slide. - therefore: the reading waits for the write to name the slide it is on, and afterwards for the docs and that frame — never for the position to become the expected one, the very thing in question.

    what : measures relaunched, it is still showing, on the slide it stopped on — the one last centred, not the first.

    if centred_slide(strip) == 0:                              # park it away from the cold-start slide
    page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")
    wait_until(page, lambda: centred_slide(strip) != 0,
               label="the show steps off the slide a cold start would pick")
i = centred_slide(strip)
was = strip.evaluate(CENTERED)                             # the slide it is showing when it goes down
remembered = lambda: page.evaluate("() => localStorage.getItem('memories.frame.cid')")
wait_until(page, lambda: remembered() == FIXTURES[i]["cid"],
           label="the slide it is on is the one written down",
           detail=lambda: f"written down: {remembered()}")
open_app(page, CABINET_QS)                                 # reboot: a plain relaunch
strip = page.get_by_role("list", name="slideshow")
expect(strip).to_be_visible()
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(len(FIXTURES))           # the docs it places from are in
page.evaluate("() => new Promise(r => requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(r)))")
came_back_on = strip.evaluate(CENTERED)                    # read at once, not waited for
assert came_back_on == was, f"resumed on {came_back_on}, not the {was} it went down on"
print("  PASS: frame resumes position")

    what : staying on the wall is a thing that fails to happen, and nothing that fails to happen can be seen the instant a page opens — an empty page and a page whose show has yet to appear look the same. - how: so the relaunch is given what it would need to start the show, the wall’s docs, and then the time it would have taken.

    what : measures only a deliberate leave stays left: the next launch opens on the wall.

    page.keyboard.press("Escape")                              # leaving turns the memory off
expect(strip).to_be_hidden()
open_app(page, CABINET_QS)
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(len(FIXTURES))           # the docs an auto-entry would place from
page.wait_for_timeout(FRAME_REENTRY_GRACE_MS)              # long enough for one to have fired
expect(page.get_by_role("list", name="slideshow")).to_be_hidden()   # stays on the wall
print("  PASS: frame mode persists")

    rule : set it going again and the memory comes back with it: a relaunch carrying only the cabinet’s tempo, no instruction to enter the frame, opens the show over the query the wall had persisted. - rule: that auto-entry fires once per launch: exiting it stays exited, so a tablet you have walked over to and switched off doesn’t snap straight back in. - what: standing still is not what keeps it out: auto-entry waits on the wall having docs to show, so a wall that never reads again never gives it a second chance. - what: a tablet’s wall reads again on its own, as the archive it is pointed at fills up. - how: here the reading is provoked by hand, with a state filter chip. - rule: a fresh set of docs is not a fresh launch.

    expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(len(FIXTURES))           # the persisted query brought the wall back
page.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile("frame", re.I)).click()   # set it going again → remembered
expect(page.get_by_role("list", name="slideshow")).to_be_visible()
open_app(page, CABINET_QS)                                 # relaunch: remembered → auto-enters, no click
strip = page.get_by_role("list", name="slideshow")
expect(strip).to_be_visible()
page.keyboard.press("Escape")                              # exit within this launch
chip(page, "todo").click()                                 # …and the wall reads again, as it will
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(len(FIXTURES))           # fresh docs — the chance a re-entry would take
page.wait_for_timeout(FRAME_REENTRY_GRACE_MS)              # long enough for one to have fired
expect(strip).to_be_hidden()                               # once per launch — it doesn't
print("  PASS: frame autostart")

    what : the cabinet tablet has no address bar: the frame launches from a home-screen shortcut, which opens with no query string, so an auto-start can’t ride a launch parameter. - how: being in the frame is remembered instead: when the persisted wall loads and the show was last on, it auto-starts, once only, so exiting doesn’t immediately re-enter. - how: on opening, the show is placed on the doc the settle last wrote down, before any scroll, and falls back to the first real slide.

    const FRAME_AUTO = localStorage.getItem(FRAME_ON_KEY) === '1';
let autoEntered = false;
createEffect(() => {
    if(FRAME_AUTO && !autoEntered && items().length > 0){ autoEntered = true; enterFrame(); }
});
createEffect(() => { if(frame() && stripEl) requestAnimationFrame(() => {
    const saved = localStorage.getItem(FRAME_CID_KEY);
    const r = saved ? items().findIndex(p => p.cid === saved) : -1;
    stripEl.scrollLeft = slideLeft(r >= 0 ? r + 1 : 1);   // +1 for the leading clone
    setFrameCenterIdx(r >= 0 ? r + 1 : 1);                             // seed the centre before any scroll
    setFrameCenterCid((items()[r >= 0 ? r : 0] || {}).cid || null);
}); });

box.blur()

    how : that list is read in a single snapshot rather than asked twice: the bar it hangs under takes itself away when nothing has touched it, and a question asked twice can be answered the second time by an empty room.

    what : measures completion never proposing a label the doc already wears, on the centred doc.

    <div class="complete">
  <input class="frame-label" role="combobox" placeholder="add a label…" aria-label="add a label in the frame"
         aria-expanded=${() => frameLabelFocus() && (sugLoading() || sugItems().length > 0) ? 'true' : 'false'}
         value=${() => frameLabel()} onInput=${e => { setFrameLabel(e.target.value); setFrameLabelFocus(true); }}
         onFocus=${() => setFrameLabelFocus(true)}
         onBlur=${() => setFrameLabelFocus(false)}
         onKeyDown=${e => { if(e.key === 'Enter' && e.shiftKey){ e.preventDefault(); frameDropLabel(); return; }
           sugNav(e, w => w ? setFrameLabel(replaceSeg(frameLabel(), w) + '; ') : frameAddLabel()); }} />
  <${Show} when=${() => frameLabelFocus()}>
    <${Suggest} text=${frameLabel} present=${() => labelsOf(frameDoc())}
                active=${sugActive} onItems=${reportSug} onLoading=${setSugLoading}
                onPick=${w => setFrameLabel(replaceSeg(frameLabel(), w) + '; ')} />
  <//>
</div>

    how : a pick fills the word in; Enter adds the typed words to the centred doc through the one edit, never doubling a label it wears, and Shift+Enter takes them off instead.

    const frameAddWord = input => { const words = splitWords(input); if(!words.length) return;
    return frameEdit(p => { const cur = splitLabels(p);
        for(const w of words) if(!cur.includes(w)) cur.push(w); return { labels: cur.join('; ') }; }); };
const frameAddLabel = () => frameAddWord(frameLabel());
const frameDropLabel = () => { const words = splitWords(frameLabel()); if(!words.length) return;
    return frameEdit(p => ({ labels: splitLabels(p).filter(x => !words.includes(x)).join('; ') })); };
Back, and the occasions on the bar

  • The occasions on the bar

    rule : the frame carries the same occasions the lightbox does: beside the date, the centred slide’s occasions ride on the bar, so a slideshow tells you not just when a doc was taken but what was happening then. - rule: stepping to the next slide brings its own.

    expect(bar.get_by_text(CABINET_EVENT)).to_be_visible()   # whatever slide it rests on, it is that

expect(bar.get_by_text(day(CABINET_TO))).to_be_visible()     # …and its end
print("  PASS: frame shows events")

    rule : the bar’s pill carries the occasion’s when too — its start and end, the same muted date aside as the lightbox, kept on the bar’s single line.

    day = lambda iso: page.evaluate("s => new Date(s).toLocaleDateString('fr-FR')", iso)
expect(bar.get_by_text(day(CABINET_FROM))).to_be_visible()   # the span's start, beside the name
expect(bar.get_by_text(day(CABINET_TO))).to_be_visible()     # …and its end

  <button class="frame-event" onClick=${() => { searchEvent(e.summary); exitFrame(); }}>${() => e.summary}<span class="ev-when">${() => eventWhen(e)}</span></button>`}
