                                  f" scrollWidth={strip.evaluate('el => el.scrollWidth')} srcs[{FAR}]={srcs(FAR)}")
        # full-res leads the way you're going: it reaches 3 ahead but only 1 behind
        assert web(FAR + 3) and not web(FAR + 4), f"full-res should reach 3 ahead, got {srcs(FAR + 3)} / {srcs(FAR + 4)}"
        assert web(FAR - 1) and not web(FAR - 2), f"full-res should reach only 1 behind, got {srcs(FAR - 1)} / {srcs(FAR - 2)}"
        # the kept-thumbnail band leans the same way: 14 ahead, 6 behind
        assert thumb(FAR + 14) and blank(FAR + 15), f"thumbnail kept 14 ahead, got {srcs(FAR + 14)} / {srcs(FAR + 15)}"
        assert thumb(FAR - 6) and blank(FAR - 7),  f"thumbnail kept 6 behind, got {srcs(FAR - 6)} / {srcs(FAR - 7)}"
        back = FAR - 5; goto(back)                               # turn round → the lean must turn with you
        wait_until(page, lambda: web(back - 3),
                   label=f"the full-res leads the reversed way (slot {back - 3})",
                   detail=lambda: f"scrollLeft={strip.evaluate('el => el.scrollLeft')}"
                                  f" srcs[{back - 3}]={srcs(back - 3)} srcs[{back}]={srcs(back)}")
        assert not web(back + 3), f"after turning, full-res should not still reach the old way, got {srcs(back + 3)}"
        print("  PASS: frame preloads web window")
        back_to_the_start()
        wait_until(page, lambda: blank(FAR),          # the bands are re-picked a beat after the show moves
                   label="the slide to be flung onto has been let go of, so the fling has something to prove",
                   detail=lambda: f"srcs[{FAR}]={srcs(FAR)}")
        mid_fling = strip.evaluate(f"""async (el, k) => {{
            ({SLIDE_JUMP})(el, k);
            await new Promise(r => requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(r)));
            return ({SLOT_SRCS})(el, k);
        }}""", FAR)
        assert mid_fling and not is_blank(mid_fling), \
            f"the slide flung onto must be asked for, not blank: {mid_fling}"
        print("  PASS: frame fling loads into view")
    finally:
        page.unroute("**/ipfs/zzclip-web")
        for d in SWIPE_DOCS + CLIP_DOCS + BAND_DOCS: gql(DELETE, {"cid": d["cid"]})

Sorting out a shoot

Fixing a date that came out wrong

Spotting the stray
what
a camera with a flat battery stamps everything with the day it was switched on, and a scan carries the day it was scanned.
  • therefore: whole batches of docs land in the archive under a date that is plainly not theirs.
what
nothing about the picture says so, though.
what
the wall is sorted by date.
  • therefore: a strayed doc sits quietly among strangers, looking exactly as settled as they do.
what
what gives it away is the calendar.
  • how: the wall marks each doc with the occasion it was taken during.
  • what: the wall runs in date order.
    • therefore: one occasion’s docs land together as a stripe of a single colour.
  • what: a doc carried weeks off by a bad timestamp lands outside that stripe, wearing no occasion at all.
    • therefore: the gap in the stripe is the thing the eye catches.
  • rule: an occasion colours its owner’s docs and nobody else’s.
  • rule: an occasion with hours in it has to say them, and one filling a whole day has none to say.
how
from there it is a doc at a time — open the one with the gap, see what it says, correct it, and read back from its occasions that it now sits where it belongs.
what
that is the easy half; the hard half is not correcting.
  • rule: reaching for the picker — where a doc’s date is set — and thinking better of it has to leave the doc exactly as it was.
  • rule: the key that opens the picker must not go off while you are typing a label, or standing on the wall with nothing open at all.
Seeing a doc’s labels
what
each tile shows its labels — the free words already on the doc — as a caption across its foot.
  • rule: the caption reads on any doc.
    • how: it sits over a dark gradient.
  • rule: many labels keep to one line, ending in an ellipsis, and hovering the tile shows the full list.
  • what: a tile with no labels shows nothing.
  • what: the state chip stays small in the corner.
how
the wall read here is the run somebody is putting a date right in, every doc of which was found by the one word they all carry.
  • therefore: that word is on the wall by construction.
rule
the tiles say so: the run’s word reads on its tiles.

expect(grid(page).get_by_text(FIX_LABEL).first).to_be_visible()
print("  PASS: tiles show labels")
Events on the wall
what
a thumbnail is a moment with its occasion stripped away: you see the scene, not that it was a swim, a birthday, a week in the mountains.
what
the calendar holds the occasion, and the lightbox — one doc opened large over the wall — already names it for the open doc.
rule
here the occasion rides onto the tile itself, so it stays with the doc while you triage.
  • what: you read a doc back in its context, remembering what it belonged to.

  • The pill

    rule : a stripe only reads as one once the occasions are told apart at a glance, and that is colour’s job.

    how : it is reached in two steps — first the pill, then its colour.

    what : a doc taken during an occasion shows a small pill on its tile, captioned with the occasion’s name.

    expect(pills_on(page, f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-02")).to_have_text([RANDO])   # the occasion, on the tile
print("  PASS: tiles show event pill")

    how : each tile’s foot carries one pill per occasion its doc falls within.

    <${Show} when=${() => docEvents(photo).length}>
  <div class="events">
    <${For} each=${() => docEvents(photo)}>${e => html`
      <span class="ev-pill" style=${() => 'background:' + eventColour().get(eventKey(e))}>${() => e.summary}</span>`}<//>
  </div>
<//>

  • One read for the whole wall

    what : occasions cannot ride on each doc the way its labels do: they come from the calendar, the lookup the lightbox runs one doc at a time.

    how : the wall reads the shared layer’s events_in_window once: every occasion overlapping the range the wall shows. - rule: the read is capped at five thousand occasions, above the whole calendar, so the connection never truncates the window.

    const EVENTS_IN_WINDOW = `query($since:Datetime!,$until:Datetime!){
  eventsInWindow(since:$since, until:$until, first:5000){ nodes{ summary starttime endtime owner } } }`;
const fetchWindowEvents = async w => (await gql(EVENTS_IN_WINDOW, w))?.eventsInWindow?.nodes ?? [];

    how : that read follows the wall’s own window, keyed on the running search’s date range. - therefore: it reads again only when the range moves, and a search on labels alone keeps its occasions. - how: In practice the key is that range written out as text, not the object holding it, so a re-render with the same window does not read again — object identity would.

    const eventWindow = createMemo(() => { const k = JSON.parse(running().key);
                                       return JSON.stringify({ since: k.since, until: k.until }); });
const [wallEvents] = createResource(eventWindow, w => fetchWindowEvents(JSON.parse(w)));

    what : a doc’s own occasions are the ones that bracket it: the same owner, and its date inside the occasion’s span.

    const docEvents = photo => { const evs = wallEvents(); if(!evs || !photo.owner) return [];
    const t = new Date(photo.date).getTime();
    return evs.filter(e => e.owner === photo.owner
        && new Date(e.starttime).getTime() <= t && t <= new Date(e.endtime).getTime()); };

  • A colour per occasion

    what : a pill that only names an occasion marks it, but does not set its stripe apart from the neighbours.

    rule : each occasion wears a colour of its own, from a palette of eight contrasted light pastels. - rule: adjacent occasions land on different hues. - what: measures one occasion’s docs read as one stripe of colour, and the next occasion breaks it.

    BG = "el => getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor"
hue = lambda day, name: pills_on(page, day).filter(has_text=name).evaluate(BG)
first = hue(f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-02", RANDO)
assert hue(f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-08", RANDO) == first, "one occasion should read as one band"
assert hue(f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-22", PISCINE) != first, "the next occasion should break it"
print("  PASS: event pills coloured per event")

    how : the colours are handed out in one pass over the shown wall, in the order occasions first appear down it. - what: they are not fixed to particular occasions, but handed out afresh each time the wall is drawn. - scope: far-apart occasions may reuse a hue — the palette cycles. - rule: two occasions of the same name still take different colours.

    const EVENT_HUES = ['#8ecae6', '#ffb703', '#90be6d', '#ff8fab', '#bdb2ff', '#ffd6a5', '#a0c4ff', '#caffbf'];
const eventKey = e => e.summary + '|' + e.starttime + '|' + e.owner;
const eventColour = createMemo(() => { const m = new Map(); let i = 0;
    for(const p of items()) for(const e of docEvents(p))
        if(!m.has(eventKey(e))) m.set(eventKey(e), EVENT_HUES[i++ % EVENT_HUES.length]);
    return m; });

    rule : each pill is filled with its occasion’s hue, the name dark on the light pastel so it still reads.

    .tile .events{ display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:3px; padding:4px 5px 0; pointer-events:none; }
.tile .ev-pill{ font-size:9px; line-height:1.35; padding:0 6px; border-radius:999px;
                background:#cbd5e1; color:#101426; max-width:100%; overflow:hidden;
                text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap; }

  • The stripe across tiles

    what : the stripe is a property of a row of tiles rather than of any one of them.

    rule : within a tile the pill comes last, after the label, landing on the tile’s bottom edge whatever the label above it turned out to be.

    rule : across tiles those edges agree: two docs of one occasion, side by side, carry their pills at the same height.

    at = lambda day: tile_of(page, f"{FIX_YEAR}-{day}")
lbl = at("06-02").get_by_text(FIX_LABEL).bounding_box()
pill = at("06-02").locator(".ev-pill").bounding_box()
assert pill["y"] > lbl["y"], f"the pill should come after the label: pill={pill['y']} label={lbl['y']}"
other = at("06-08").locator(".ev-pill").bounding_box()          # the same occasion, further along
assert abs(other["y"] - pill["y"]) < 1, f"the band should be level: {pill['y']} vs {other['y']}"
print("  PASS: event pill sits below label")

  • Overlaps, gaps and owners

    what : occasions can overlap.

    rule : a doc caught inside two at once — an afternoon out within a week away — wears a pill for each, in each occasion’s own colour, so both read at a glance.

    both = pills_on(page, f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-05")
expect(both).to_have_text([RANDO, SOMMET])              # the week, and the two days within it
assert both.nth(0).evaluate(BG) != both.nth(1).evaluate(BG), "the two should be told apart"
print("  PASS: overlapping events show two pills")

    what : measures a stray wears no occasion, a gap in the stripe.

    expect(pills_on(page, STRAY_DAY)).to_have_count(0)      # the gap in the band: nothing was on that day
print("  PASS: out-of-event doc has no pill")

    what : an occasion is its owner’s alone, and a day belongs to everybody. - example: two people out with cameras on the same afternoon each have their own account of it in their own calendar.

    what : measures an occasion colours only its owner’s docs. - example: on a day where both accounts exist, each doc wears one, rather than each wearing both.

    shared = tile_of(page, f"{FIX_YEAR}-08-01")
expect(shared).to_have_count(2)                        # the same day, one doc each
expect(shared.nth(0).locator(".ev-pill")).to_have_count(1)   # one occasion apiece…
expect(shared.nth(1).locator(".ev-pill")).to_have_count(1)
expect(grid(page).get_by_text(AYLAS, exact=True)).to_have_count(1)   # …and it is their own
expect(grid(page).get_by_text(MINE, exact=True)).to_have_count(1)
print("  PASS: event pill owner scoped")
Seeing a doc’s events
what
a doc sits in time, and the calendar knows what was happening then.
  • rule: the lightbox names it: the occasions the doc falls within ride under its date as small pills.
what
the calendar is Google’s, managed elsewhere.
  • rule: memories never edits the occasions themselves; it only surfaces the overlap they name.
what
a date is only ever wrong relative to something, and the pills are that something.
  • therefore: they are where a correction is confirmed or found to be wrong again.
rule
correct the date and the pills are recomputed for where the doc now sits, without leaving the doc.

expect(d.get_by_text(RANDO)).to_be_visible()               # the week it was taken during…
expect(d.get_by_text(SOMMET)).to_be_visible()              # …and the two days within it
span = lambda iso: page.evaluate("s => new Date(s).toLocaleDateString('fr-FR')", iso)
expect(d.get_by_text(span(f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-01T00:00:00Z"))).to_be_visible()   # the week's start…
expect(d.get_by_text(span(f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-10T23:59:59Z"))).to_be_visible()   # …and its end
print("  PASS: lightbox shows events")
how
the lookup rides on the open doc, asking the calendar for its date and owner.
  • therefore: it follows whatever doc is shown.
  • rule: a doc with no owner has nothing to scope by, so nothing is asked.
  • how: the wall’s search carries each doc’s owner for exactly this.

const EVENTS_FOR_DOC = `query($d:Datetime!,$o:OwnerType!){ eventsAt(d:$d, o:$o){ nodes{ summary starttime endtime } } }`;
const fetchDocEvents = async o => (await gql(EVENTS_FOR_DOC, { d: o.date, o: o.owner }))?.eventsAt?.nodes ?? [];
const dayBased = (s, en) => s.getUTCHours() === 0 && s.getUTCMinutes() === 0 && s.getUTCSeconds() === 0
                         && en.getUTCHours() === 23 && en.getUTCMinutes() === 59 && en.getUTCSeconds() === 59;
const hhmm = t => t.toLocaleTimeString('fr-FR', { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' });
const eventWhen = e => {
    const s = new Date(e.starttime), en = new Date(e.endtime);
    const sd = s.toLocaleDateString('fr-FR'), ed = en.toLocaleDateString('fr-FR');
    if (dayBased(s, en)) return sd === ed ? sd : `${sd} – ${ed}`;
    return sd === ed ? `${sd} ${hhmm(s)} – ${hhmm(en)}` : `${sd} ${hhmm(s)} – ${ed} ${hhmm(en)}`;
};
// run the occasion's own event: search — the pill's jump into it
const searchEvent = summary => { setSearch('event:' + summary); commit(); };
const [lbEvents] = createResource(
    () => { const o = opened(); return o?.owner && o?.date ? o : null; }, fetchDocEvents);

  • When each occasion ran

    what : the name alone would not settle it. - example: knowing a doc falls inside zzRando says nothing about whether that is a week or an afternoon.

    rule : each pill carries the occasion’s own bounds beside its name, as the reader’s locale and timezone write them.

    span = lambda iso: page.evaluate("s => new Date(s).toLocaleDateString('fr-FR')", iso)
expect(d.get_by_text(span(f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-01T00:00:00Z"))).to_be_visible()   # the week's start…
expect(d.get_by_text(span(f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-10T23:59:59Z"))).to_be_visible()   # …and its end

    what : an occasion need not fill a day, and its bounds are stored as instants.

    what : measures an occasion with hours in it says them, on the reader’s clock.

    tile_of(page, f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-22").click(click_count=2)
d = dialog(page)
when = page.evaluate("""([a, b]) => {
  const s = new Date(a), en = new Date(b);
  const t = x => x.toLocaleTimeString('fr-FR', {hour:'2-digit', minute:'2-digit'});
  return `${s.toLocaleDateString('fr-FR')} ${t(s)} – ${t(en)}`;
}""", [f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-22T09:00:00Z", f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-22T17:00:00Z"])
expect(d.get_by_text(when)).to_be_visible()          # the day, and the hours of it
d.get_by_role("button", name="close").click()
back_on_the_wall(page)
print("  PASS: lightbox shows timed event hours")

    what : a whole-day occasion’s dates collapse to one when it lasted a single day. - how: Under the hood, whole-day is read off the span’s UTC bounds — 00:00:00 to 23:59:59, a day’s last second — the inclusive end the calendar spans carry, the same bound events_at matches on.

    const dayBased = (s, en) => s.getUTCHours() === 0 && s.getUTCMinutes() === 0 && s.getUTCSeconds() === 0
                         && en.getUTCHours() === 23 && en.getUTCMinutes() === 59 && en.getUTCSeconds() === 59;
const hhmm = t => t.toLocaleTimeString('fr-FR', { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' });
const eventWhen = e => {
    const s = new Date(e.starttime), en = new Date(e.endtime);
    const sd = s.toLocaleDateString('fr-FR'), ed = en.toLocaleDateString('fr-FR');
    if (dayBased(s, en)) return sd === ed ? sd : `${sd} – ${ed}`;
    return sd === ed ? `${sd} ${hhmm(s)} – ${hhmm(en)}` : `${sd} ${hhmm(s)} – ${ed} ${hhmm(en)}`;
};

    rule : beside its name, a pill’s when is a quiet aside: it tells apart occasions whose name recurs, without shouting. - example: a doc’s occasion is Piscine, juin 2020.

    /* the span reads as a quiet aside beside the name — the discreet part of "name + when" */
.ev-when{ margin-left:6px; opacity:.6; }

  • Only the owner’s

    what : two people’s calendars can hold occasions on the very same day, and a doc belongs to just one of them.

    what : measures an occasion goes to its owner’s docs and nobody else’s in the lightbox too: another owner’s, spanning the same instant, stays hidden.

    mine = tile_of(page, f"{FIX_YEAR}-08-01").filter(has=page.locator(f'.ev-pill:text-is("{MINE}")'))
mine.click(click_count=2)                              # of the two that day, the one that is mine
d = dialog(page)
expect(d.get_by_text(MINE)).to_be_visible()                # my account of that afternoon…
expect(d.get_by_text(AYLAS)).to_have_count(0)              # …and not Ayla's, of the same one
print("  PASS: lightbox events are owner-scoped")

    how : the scoping is done where the occasions are read: the app passes the doc’s own owner and gets back what belongs to it. - therefore: showing too much would have to come from the archive, beyond anything the app alone can break.

  • A way into the occasion

    what : a pill is also a way in: clicking one asks for every doc of its occasion and gets out of the way. - what: it is a jump, not an edit: the calendar is untouched.

    what : the query it writes is the whole query, not an addition to it — any window you had narrowed to is spent.

    rule : one click stands for typing it, and having asked, the doc you were looking at is no longer in front of the answer.

    d.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile(MINE)).click()     # the occasion in front of you
expect(search_box(page)).to_have_value(f"event:{MINE}")    # the search typed out for you…
back_on_the_wall(page)                                     # …and the doc stood aside for it
print("  PASS: lightbox event pill searches")

    how : it asks the event: search, written out in the search box — where the wall’s search is typed — and committed. - scope: where that leads is the search’s business, measured with the rest of the query language.

    // run the occasion's own event: search — the pill's jump into it
const searchEvent = summary => { setSearch('event:' + summary); commit(); };

    what : the pills are small and rounded, muted against the dark panel, and wrap onto another line when there are several.

    what : unlike a label’s chip they carry no ×: there is no occasion to edit here.

    how : the whole pill is a button: a pointer and a hover lift mark it as a jump into the occasion.

    <div class="lb-events">
  <${For} each=${() => lbEvents() || []}>${e => html`
    <button class="lb-event" onClick=${() => { searchEvent(e.summary); dismissPhoto(); }}>${() => e.summary}<span class="ev-when">${() => eventWhen(e)}</span></button>`}
  <//>
</div>


    .lb-events{ display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:6px; }
.lb-event{ font:inherit; font-size:12px; color:#bcd; background:#20293f; border:1px solid #34406088;
           border-radius:999px; padding:3px 10px; cursor:pointer; }
.lb-event:hover{ background:#2a3450; border-color:#4a5680; }
/* the span reads as a quiet aside beside the name — the discreet part of "name + when" */
.ev-when{ margin-left:6px; opacity:.6; }
Fixing a wrong date
rule
the correction is right there in the moment you catch it, eyes on the doc and no detour to a form.
  • how: the date on the lightbox’s meta row — its date, the original’s link beside it — is already what you are reading, so it is what you edit.
how
it saves through the very lbPatch a state button uses.
  • therefore: a doc that just changed date re-anchors just as one that changed state.
what
the wall and the open doc read the same list.
  • therefore: the doc takes its new place in both at once, while the lightbox keeps its footing.
what
going back to the wall is how the story carries on, not a second look at the same fact.
what
the edit is a small state machine.
what
measures a corrected doc reads back from its occasions: still open, it wears the occasions of the day you gave it.

d.get_by_role("button", name="edit date").click()          # the date is a button — open the picker
box = d.get_by_label("date", exact=True)
box.fill(f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-06T12:00")              # the day it was really taken
box.press("Enter")                               # save
expect(d.get_by_text(RANDO)).to_be_visible()               # the week it was taken during…
expect(d.get_by_text(SOMMET)).to_be_visible()              # …and the two days within it
span = lambda iso: page.evaluate("s => new Date(s).toLocaleDateString('fr-FR')", iso)
expect(d.get_by_text(span(f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-01T00:00:00Z"))).to_be_visible()   # the week's start…
expect(d.get_by_text(span(f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-10T23:59:59Z"))).to_be_visible()   # …and its end
print("  PASS: lightbox shows events")
d.get_by_role("button", name="close").click()    # back to the wall
back_on_the_wall(page)
print("  PASS: lightbox edit date rejoins its occasions")

  • The picker

    what : the date on the meta row is a button, and clicking it opens the picker.

    rule : the picker opens seeded with what the date held. - rule: the seed keeps the hours and minutes too, so a save that fixes just the year leaves the time of day standing.

    want = page.evaluate("d => { const t = new Date(d), p = n => String(n).padStart(2, '0');"
                     " return `${t.getFullYear()}-${p(t.getMonth()+1)}-${p(t.getDate())}T${p(t.getHours())}:${p(t.getMinutes())}`; }",
                     f"{STRAY_DAY}T12:00:00Z")
expect(d.get_by_label("date", exact=True)).to_have_value(want)   # seeded with the stored instant, in local time
print("  PASS: date editor seeds current value")

    how : the date stays a button until clicked, and the picker standing in for it saves as soon as it lets go of the keys.

    <${Show} when=${() => editingDate()}
         fallback=${html`<button class="lb-date" aria-label="edit date"
             onClick=${() => setEditingDate(true)}>${() => opened()?.date ? new Date(opened().date).toLocaleString("fr-FR") : ''}</button>`}>
  <input class="lb-date-edit" type="datetime-local" aria-label="date"
         ref=${el => { el.value = toLocalInput(opened()?.date); requestAnimationFrame(() => el.focus()); }}
         onKeyDown=${e => { if(e.key === 'Enter'){ e.preventDefault(); e.target.blur(); } else if(e.key === 'Escape'){ e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); cancelEdit = true; e.target.blur(); } }}
         onBlur=${e => commitDate(e.target.value)} />
<//>


    .lb-date{ background:none; border:none; padding:0; font-family:inherit; cursor:pointer; }
.lb-date:hover{ color:#ccd; text-decoration:underline; }
.lb-date-edit{ font-size:13px; color:var(--fg); background:#262a40; border:1px solid #3a3f5a;
               border-radius:6px; padding:2px 6px; }

    how : In practice the picker is a datetime-local input, which speaks the browser’s local clock time while the stored date is a zoned instant: a small formatter seeds it, and the save converts back.

    const toLocalInput = iso => { if(!iso) return '';
    const d = new Date(iso), p = n => String(n).padStart(2, '0');
    return `${d.getFullYear()}-${p(d.getMonth()+1)}-${p(d.getDate())}T${p(d.getHours())}:${p(d.getMinutes())}`; };
let cancelEdit = false;
const commitDate = v => { const skip = cancelEdit; cancelEdit = false; setEditingDate(false);
    if(!skip && v) lbPatch({ date: new Date(v).toISOString() }); };

  • Backing out

    what : a date that saves can carry its doc clean out of the window the wall is showing, and the open doc then re-anchors to a neighbour. - therefore: after a save that should never have happened, the picker’s row shows a third doc’s date altogether, and cannot answer whether the backing-out took.

    how : the backing-out is read off the wall behind: the doc is missing from it, and the dates it lists are the ones actually stored.

    how : the claim is that nothing happened, so the reading waits out the span a save would have needed before believing it.

    what : measures thinking better of the picker leaves the doc as it was: backing out with Escape leaves it open.

    unmoved = tile_dates(page)                                            # the wall as it stands
box = d.get_by_label("date", exact=True)
box.fill("1999-01-01T00:00")
box.press("Escape")
expect(d).to_be_visible()                                             # still open
page.wait_for_timeout(SAVE_GRACE_MS)                                  # room for a save to land
assert tile_dates(page) == unmoved, f"the backed-out date was written anyway: {tile_dates(page)}"
print("  PASS: date edit escape cancels")

    how : Escape would otherwise reach the lightbox’s own key handling and close the whole doc, so the picker swallows the key and vetoes the save before it lets go.

    else if(e.key === 'Escape'){ e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); cancelEdit = true; e.target.blur(); }

  • A key for the date

    rule : reaching the picker costs no more than reaching the add-label box: d — for date — opens it on the doc in view, the same reflex as l for labels.

    page.keyboard.press("d")
expect(d.get_by_label("date", exact=True)).to_be_focused()
print("  PASS: date shortcut focuses editor")

    what : measures the key stays quiet while you type a label: in any text field, it is a letter like any other.

    d.get_by_placeholder("add a label…").click()                  # focus the label box
page.keyboard.press("d")
expect(d.get_by_label("date", exact=True)).to_have_count(0)   # the picker stayed shut
print("  PASS: date shortcut stands aside in a field")

    what : measures the key stays quiet on the wall with nothing open: nor may it lie in wait and spring on the next one opened.

    page.keyboard.press("d")                                      # no doc open
tiles(page).filter(has_not=page.locator(".ev-pill")).click(click_count=2)   # the one with the gap
d = dialog(page)
expect(d.get_by_role("button", name="edit date")).to_be_visible()   # opens in display mode…
expect(d.get_by_label("date", exact=True)).to_have_count(0)         # …not the picker
print("  PASS: date shortcut ignored without a doc")

    how : the key is heard across the whole app, wherever the eye is, and gives way to any field.

    onMount(() => {
    const onKey = e => {
        if(e.key !== 'd' || !opened()) return;                     // only while a doc is open
        if(/^(INPUT|TEXTAREA)$/.test(e.target.tagName)) return;     // a field already owns the key
        e.preventDefault(); setEditingDate(true);
    };
    window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey);
    onCleanup(() => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey));
});
The run
how
the run has one hole in it.
  • what: a second bare tile — a thumbnail on the wall wearing no occasion — and the gap stops being a signal.
    • therefore: the hole has to be the only one.
how
two occasions a fortnight apart, three docs inside the first and two inside the second.
  • how: one doc dated a month past both — the stray, and the only doc here without an occasion.
  • how: a third occasion sits inside the first, two days of a longer week.
    • therefore: one doc is caught by two at once.
how
two more cover a single later day on which Ayla and I each took a doc — one occasion hers, one mine.
how
a sixth is an afternoon rather than a day, laid over a doc already inside the second.
how
those dates are years ahead of today, in a stretch of calendar nobody has been to yet.
  • how: the occasions on the wall are read from the real calendar over the window the wall shows.
    • therefore: a window over a year somebody has lived would bring their own occasions in alongside these, and the colours would stop meaning what they are said to mean here.
how
one span below is the suite’s own.
  • what: a save travels to the archive and back before the wall shows it.
    • therefore: claiming a save did not happen means waiting out the time one would have taken.
  • what: closing an open doc is likewise not instant.
    • what: the wall underneath is not usable until the doc is gone rather than merely invisible — a sheet still lying over it takes the click meant for a tile.
      • therefore: going back to the wall is something to wait for, and the thing to wait for is the doc’s absence.
A run named onto an occasion
what
typing the day in is only bearable for one doc.
  • what: the dates that really go wrong go wrong by the dozen.
    • example: an afternoon that came back through a messaging app, every copy stamped with the day it was saved.
what
the whole point is that nobody remembers which day it was.
  • therefore: there is no day to type.
  • what: what is remembered is the occasion — the hike, the swim.
how
the second half of this story is a second run, named onto an occasion — moved to its dates in one go — rather than dated.
  • what: the wall above rests on the stray being the only doc wearing no occasion, and four more bare tiles would have taken that signal away.
    • therefore: the second run has its own label.
rule
a move must leave everyone else’s docs alone.
rule
the move offers occasions with no doc yet, and ones outside the wall’s window.
how
one of the second run is somebody else’s, a day apart from the rest.
how
two occasions join the six.
  • example: a namesake of the hike, months further off.
  • example: one with no doc at all, a year past the window the wall is showing.
Moving a stray doc onto its occasion
what
measures a run named onto an occasion moves to its dates in one go: the strays take the occasion’s own first day, sliding back into the stripe.
how
pick the strays up, name the occasion in the toolbar’s move box, and pick it.
  • what: the toolbar is the row of buttons acting on what is picked up.
  • rule: once the move is applied, nothing is picked up any more.

select_all(page).click()
box.click(); box.press_sequentially(RANDO, delay=20)
tb.get_by_role("option").first.click()             # the hike itself: the nearer of the two
move_btn.click()
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(0)                              # applied → the selection clears
# they wear the occasion's start day now — the wall re-anchors, and a tile's alt is its day
expect(grid(page).get_by_role("img", name=f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-01")).to_have_count(3)
expect(tile_of(page, f"{FIX_YEAR}-11-21")).to_have_count(1)   # hers stayed where it was saved
print("  PASS: move selection to event")

  • Which occasions it offers

    how : the move box lives in the selection toolbar, beside the add-label box. - how: it holds the text you type, whether it has focus, and — once you pick — the occasion you armed.

    const [moveText, setMoveText] = createSignal('');
const [moveFocus, setMoveFocus] = createSignal(false);
const [moveTarget, setMoveTarget] = createSignal(null);   // the armed occasion, or null → nothing to apply

    what : a stray’s date sits nowhere near the occasion it belongs to. - therefore: a list bounded by what the wall happens to show could never reach it.

    how : the occasions are read from the whole calendar the moment the box opens, over an all-time span, capped like the wall’s own event read.

    const [moveEvents] = createResource(moveFocus,
    f => f ? fetchWindowEvents({ since: '1900-01-01T00:00:00Z', until: '2100-01-01T00:00:00Z' }) : []);

    rule : when the name fits several occasions, the list leads with the one nearest the strays. - example: a « Karaté » that recurs every week.

    what : the order only suggests — you still pick. - therefore: a misleading « nearest » costs a glance, never a silent mis-move.

    box.fill(""); box.press_sequentially(RANDO, delay=20)
opts = tb.get_by_role("option")
expect(opts).to_have_count(2)                       # the hike and its namesake both answer to it
expect(opts.first).not_to_contain_text(RANDO_FAR)   # the nearer of the two leads
print("  PASS: move ranks by mean closeness")

    how : an occasion’s closeness is how far the mean of the picked-up docs’ dates sits from its span — zero when the mean falls inside, otherwise the gap to the nearer bound.

    const selectedDocs = () => { const byCid = new Map(items().map(p => [p.cid, p]));
    return [...selected()].map(c => byCid.get(c)).filter(Boolean); };
const selMean = () => { const ts = selectedDocs().map(p => new Date(p.date).getTime()).filter(n => !isNaN(n));
    return ts.length ? ts.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / ts.length : null; };
const eventDist = (e, mean) => { if(mean == null) return 0;
    const s = new Date(e.starttime).getTime(), en = new Date(e.endtime).getTime();
    return mean < s ? s - mean : mean > en ? mean - en : 0; };

  • Only the owner’s occasions

    rule : the move is owner-scoped, on both sides.

    what : measures a move leaves everyone else’s docs alone: it touches only a doc whose owner holds the picked occasion. - example: the count landing on the occasion’s day above is three and not four: the fourth was hers, and the move declined it.

    rule : the rule survives the widening — the toolbar’s all matching switch, from what is picked up to everything the search matches — but by a different road. - how: the picked-up path declines doc by doc; the wide one pins the filter to the owner before it goes out.

    rule : one doc picked up, the switch on, and every doc of his the search holds moves, and still none of hers.

    t.nth(0).click()                                             # one of the three that are mine
tb.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile("all .* matching")).click()

    rule : the list offers only the occasions of the picked-up docs’ own owners. - therefore: a namesake in someone else’s calendar — which could never apply — is never even shown, and a pick cannot land on a silent no-op.

    const selOwners = () => new Set(selectedDocs().map(p => p.owner).filter(Boolean));

  • The list and the move

    rule : a long calendar never floods the box: the eight nearest are shown.

    how : as you type, the box narrows the calendar to the occasions whose name contains the text, kept to those owners and ordered by closeness, ties going to the earlier occasion.

    const moveCandidates = () => { const q = moveText().trim().toLowerCase(), mean = selMean(), owners = selOwners();
    return (moveEvents() || []).filter(e => owners.has(e.owner))
        .filter(e => !q || (e.summary || '').toLowerCase().includes(q))
        .sort((a, b) => eventDist(a, mean) - eventDist(b, mean) || new Date(a.starttime) - new Date(b.starttime))
        .slice(0, 8); };

    how : picking one arms that exact occasion and closes the list.

    what : the occasion could only have been offered because somebody on the wall owns it. - therefore: the widened move is a tightening and never a reach: it stays inside what the person is looking at, as everything on the toolbar must.

    const pickMove = e => { setMoveTarget(e); setMoveText(e.summary); setMoveFocus(false); };
const moveToEvent = async () => { const ev = moveTarget(); if(!ev) return;
    if(allMatching()) await applyBulk('SetDate', ev.starttime, { owners: [ev.owner] });
    else await patchSelected(p => p.owner === ev.owner ? { date: ev.starttime } : null);
    setMoveText(''); setMoveTarget(null); };

  • The keyboard and the rows

    rule : the box’s keyboard is the other completion boxes’: arrows move through the rows and Enter picks the highlighted occasion, as in the search and add-label boxes. - rule: a pick need not be a click: arrowing down to an occasion and pressing Enter arms the → event button no differently.

    box.fill(""); box.press_sequentially(RANDO, delay=20)

expect(opt).to_be_visible()                              # the list is open
expect(move_btn).to_be_disabled()                        # nothing picked yet
box.press("ArrowDown")                                   # highlight the first candidate
expect(opt).to_have_attribute("aria-selected", "true")   # the shared highlight landed on it
box.press("Enter")                                       # Enter picks the highlighted one → arms
expect(move_btn).to_be_enabled()
expect(box).to_have_value(RANDO)                         # the pick filled the box
print("  PASS: move box keyboard picks")

    rule : with nothing highlighted, Enter applies the armed pick, the same as the → event button beside it, which applies the move.

    how : the box hands its candidates up to the single keyboard highlight the whole app keeps.

    createEffect(() => { if(moveFocus()) reportSug(moveCandidates()); });

    what : each row names the occasion and, beside it, when it ran — the same aside the lightbox reads off a pill. - therefore: a recurring occasion is told apart by its date.

    what : the highlighted row is marked as the shared highlight moves over it.

    <div class="complete">
  <input class="batch-move" role="combobox" placeholder="move to event…" aria-label="move the selection to an event"
         aria-expanded=${() => moveFocus() && moveCandidates().length > 0 ? 'true' : 'false'}
         value=${() => moveText()}
         onInput=${e => { setMoveText(e.target.value); setMoveTarget(null); setMoveFocus(true); }}
         onFocus=${() => setMoveFocus(true)}
         onKeyDown=${e => sugNav(e, picked => picked ? pickMove(picked) : moveToEvent())}
         onBlur=${() => setMoveFocus(false)} />
  <${Show} when=${() => moveFocus() && moveCandidates().length > 0}>
    <ul class="suggest" role="listbox" aria-label="events">
      <${For} each=${() => moveCandidates()}>${(e, i) => html`
        <li class=${() => 'sug' + (i() === sugActive() ? ' active' : '')} role="option"
            aria-selected=${() => i() === sugActive() ? 'true' : 'false'}
            onMouseDown=${ev => { ev.preventDefault(); pickMove(e); }}>
          ${() => e.summary}<span class="ev-when">${() => eventWhen(e)}</span></li>`}
      <//>
    </ul>
  <//>
</div>
<button class="movebtn" aria-label="move to event" disabled=${() => !moveTarget()}
        onClick=${moveToEvent}>→ event</button>

    what : the box looks like the toolbar’s add-label box; its rows reuse the shared completion look and the pill’s muted when aside.

    what : the → event button dims while no pick is armed.

    .batch-move{ width:100%; box-sizing:border-box; padding:5px 8px; font-size:14px;
             background:#262a40; color:var(--fg); border:1px solid #3a3f5a; border-radius:5px; }
.movebtn:disabled{ opacity:.45; cursor:default; }

  • A move fires only from a pick

    rule : a move fires only from an explicit pick. - rule: the → event button stays disabled until a pick arms it. - therefore: an unpicked box, however fully typed, can never fire it. - rule: editing the name after picking disables it again, waiting for a fresh pick.

    rule : a pick is bound to the pick-up it was made against: a stale pick can never move a set you have since changed.

    rule : touching the pick-up drops the armed pick, and the box clears, ready for a fresh pick.

    createEffect(() => { selected(); setMoveText(''); setMoveTarget(null); });

  • An occasion with no doc yet

    what : the occasion you move onto usually has no doc of its own yet — assigning docs to it is the whole point. - scope: the search box’s event: completion offers only occasions that already hold a doc, and would hide exactly this one.

    what : measures the move offers photoless and far-off occasions: one with no doc, a year past the window, is still there to pick.

def tile_of(page, day):
    """The tile of the doc taken on that day."""
    return tiles(page).filter(has=page.get_by_alt_text(day, exact=True))

def pills_on(page, day):
    """The occasions written across the tile of the doc taken on that day."""
    return tile_of(page, day).locator(".ev-pill")

def back_on_the_wall(page):
    expect(dialog(page)).to_be_hidden()


@testcase
def test_fixing_a_date(page):
    """Spotting a doc whose date has drifted — it alone wears no occasion — then opening
    it, reaching for the picker and backing out, putting the date right, and reading back
    off the occasions it has rejoined that it now sits where it belongs. Then the same
    trouble at a scale nobody types their way out of: a pile of copies all stamped the day
    they were saved, named onto the occasion they came from instead."""
    docs = fix_docs() + move_docs()
    for d_ in docs: gql(DELETE, {"cid": d_["cid"]}); gql(CREATE, {"p": d_})
    seed_events(FIX_EVENTS)
    try:
        open_app(page); chip(page, "all").click()
        search_for(page, f"{FIX_LABEL}; since:{FIX_YEAR}; until:{FIX_YEAR}")
        expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(len(FIX_DOCS))
        expect(grid(page).get_by_text(FIX_LABEL).first).to_be_visible()
        print("  PASS: tiles show labels")
        expect(pills_on(page, f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-02")).to_have_text([RANDO])   # the occasion, on the tile
        print("  PASS: tiles show event pill")
        BG = "el => getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor"
        hue = lambda day, name: pills_on(page, day).filter(has_text=name).evaluate(BG)
        first = hue(f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-02", RANDO)
        assert hue(f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-08", RANDO) == first, "one occasion should read as one band"
        assert hue(f"{FIX_YEAR}-06-22", PISCINE) != first, "the next occasion should break it"
        print("  PASS: event pills coloured per event")
        at = lambda day: tile_of(page, f"{FIX_YEAR}-{day}")
        lbl = at("06-02").get_by_text(FIX_LABEL).bounding_box()
        pill = at("06-02").locator(".ev-pill").bounding_box()
        assert pill["y"] > lbl["y"], f"the pill should come after the label: pill={pill['y']} label={lbl['y']}"
        other = at("06-08").locator(".ev-pill").bounding_box()          # the same occasion, further along
        assert abs(other["y"] - pill["y"]) < 1, f"the band should be level: {pill['y']} vs {other['y']}"
        print("  PASS: event pill sits below label")

        assert both.nth(0).evaluate(BG) != both.nth(1).evaluate(BG), "the two should be told apart"
        print("  PASS: overlapping events show two pills")

Putting words on a doc

what
labelling is really the whole of triage — going through what came in.
  • what: the state chips — buttons marking where a doc stands: todo, next, done — say how far along a doc is, but the labels are what make it findable again in ten years.
what
this is the story that runs most — open a doc, put the words on it, move to the next.
  • what: the add-label box takes several words at once.
  • what: the keyboard does add and remove without reaching for the × on a label.
  • what: the word you just used is offered on the next doc for a single tap.
  • rule: the archive has to actually keep them.
  • rule: a run is worked without ever leaving it — once one doc is up, reaching the next must not cost a trip back to the wall to find it.
    • what: the doc in front of you is what steps.
what
a doc takes two fingers as readily as any picture anywhere else.
what
a doc is sometimes worth putting up properly, which is what the frame is for.
  • how: that is a tap from the doc already open, rather than a trip back to the wall to start the show over.
  • what: coming out of it lands back on the doc you left, not at the beginning of everything.
what
the add-label box offers words from the archive’s vocabulary.
  • how: the story brings its own three words and takes them away after.
    • example: one to complete onto the doc.
    • example: one that must leave the list once the doc wears it.
    • example: one to take with the keyboard.

LABEL_WORDS = ["zzcalanque", "zzcigale", "zzcousin"]


@testcase
def test_putting_words_on_a_photo(page):
    """Working a run doc by doc: opening one, stepping to the next without leaving it,
    handing one to the big show and stepping back out onto the doc, labelling — several
    words at once, the keyboard for add and remove, the last word reused on the next, and
    all of it written down — and getting close enough to read what is in one.  Throughout,
    the browser's own menu stays out of the way, except where the words are typed."""
    seed_vocab(LABEL_WORDS)
    try:
        open_fixtures(page)
        assert native_menu(page, tiles(page).nth(0)) is False, "a press on a tile should raise no menu"
        print("  PASS: tile context menu suppressed")
        assert native_menu(page, search_box(page)) is True, "the search box should keep its own menu"
        print("  PASS: context menu allowed in text field")
        tiles(page).nth(0).dblclick()
        expect(dialog(page)).to_be_visible()
        expect(dialog(page).get_by_role("img")).to_have_count(1)   # the photo, full size
        print("  PASS: double-click opens lightbox")
        d = dialog(page)
        expect(d.locator(".lb-date")).to_have_text(page.evaluate(f"() => new Date('{FIXTURES[0]['date']}').toLocaleString('fr-FR')"))   # its date
        expect(d.get_by_text(FIXTURE_LABEL)).to_be_visible()     # its labels are shown
        d.get_by_role("button", name="close").click()
        expect(d).to_be_hidden()
        print("  PASS: lightbox opens and closes")
        open_doc(page, 0)
        img = d.get_by_role("img")
        assert native_menu(page, img) is False, "a press on the open doc should raise no menu"
        print("  PASS: lightbox context menu suppressed")
        shown = img.bounding_box()
        assert shown["width"] >= VIEWPORT["width"] * 0.9, f"media width {shown['width']} < 90% of viewport"
        assert shown["height"] >= VIEWPORT["height"] * 0.65, f"media height {shown['height']} < 65% of viewport"
        assert img.evaluate("el => getComputedStyle(el).objectFit") == "contain", "media crops instead of fitting whole"
        print("  PASS: lightbox media fills screen")
        link = d.locator(".lb-meta").get_by_role("link", name="original")   # on the date row
        expect(link).to_have_text("⤢")
        expect(link).to_have_attribute("title", re.compile("full resolution.*new tab"))
        expect(link).to_have_attribute("href", FIXTURES[0]["cid"])    # the original's /ipfs/ path
        expect(link).to_have_attribute("target", "_blank")
        print("  PASS: lightbox links to original")
        expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzbatchfix-thumb-0")
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")
        expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzbatchfix-thumb-1")
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowLeft")
        expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzbatchfix-thumb-0")
        d.get_by_role("button", name="next photo").click()
        expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzbatchfix-thumb-1")
        d.get_by_role("button", name="previous photo").click()                # back where we started
        expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzbatchfix-thumb-0")
        d.get_by_role("button", name="previous photo").click()                # and off the front
        expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzbatchfix-thumb-2")      # → the last, not a dead stop
        d.get_by_role("button", name="next photo").click()                    # off the end again
        expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzbatchfix-thumb-0")
        print("  PASS: lightbox prev/next")
        over = img.bounding_box()
        page.mouse.move(over["x"] + over["width"] / 2, over["y"] + over["height"] / 2)
        page.keyboard.down("Shift")
        page.mouse.wheel(0, 240)                          # one flick down…
        page.mouse.wheel(0, 240)                          # …and its tail, still inside the deaf window
        page.wait_for_timeout(250)
        expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzbatchfix-thumb-1")   # one doc, not two
        page.mouse.wheel(0, -240)                         # shift-scroll up → prev
        expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzbatchfix-thumb-0")
        page.keyboard.up("Shift")
        page.wait_for_timeout(250)
        page.mouse.wheel(0, 240)                          # no Shift → the panel's scroll, not ours
        page.wait_for_timeout(250)
        expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzbatchfix-thumb-0")
        print("  PASS: lightbox shift-scroll nav")
        asked = []
        def note_leave(ask): asked.append(ask.message); ask.dismiss()
        page.on("dialog", note_leave)
        page.go_back()
        expect(d).to_be_hidden()
        expect(grid(page)).to_be_visible()
        page.remove_listener("dialog", note_leave)
        assert not asked, f"closing a doc with Back asked to leave the app: {asked}"
        print("  PASS: back button closes lightbox")
        middle = FIXTURES[1]
        open_doc(page, 1)                        # not the first
        expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", middle["thumbnailCid"])
        d.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile("frame", re.I)).click()
        expect(d).to_be_hidden()                         # the lightbox gives way to the show
        strip = page.get_by_role("list", name="slideshow")
        expect(strip).to_be_visible()
        wait_until(page, lambda: strip.evaluate(CENTERED) == middle["thumbnailCid"],
                   label="the show opens on the doc you were looking at",
                   detail=lambda: f"it opened on {strip.evaluate(CENTERED)!r}")
        print("  PASS: frame from lightbox")
        page.go_back()                                   # out of the show…
        expect(strip).to_be_hidden()
        expect(d.get_by_role("img")).to_have_attribute("src", middle["thumbnailCid"])   # …onto the doc it came from
        page.go_back()                                   # out of the lightbox…
        expect(d).to_be_hidden()
        expect(grid(page)).to_be_visible()               # …back to the wall
        print("  PASS: back from frame returns to lightbox")
        open_doc(page, 0)
        sel = d.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile("select"))
        sel.click()                                        # a control acts → the modal stays
        expect(sel).to_have_text(re.compile("selected"))   # the click reached the button, didn't leak to close
        expect(d).to_be_visible()
        d.get_by_role("img").click()                       # the image doesn't act → the modal closes
        expect(d).to_be_hidden()
        print("  PASS: lightbox click outside content closes")
        open_doc(page, 0)
        expect(d).to_be_visible()
        box = d.get_by_placeholder("add a label…")
        hold_completions(page)                       # the vocabulary, left unanswered
        expanded_while_loading(page, box)
        print("  PASS: lightbox label expanded while loading")
        page.unroute("**/graphql")               # the vocabulary answers again
        box.press_sequentially("zzc")
        expect(box).to_have_attribute("aria-expanded", "true")
        box.press("Tab")                                       # out of the box, the ordinary way
        expect(box).to_have_attribute("aria-expanded", "false")
        assert page.get_by_role("listbox", name="suggestions").count() == 0, "the popover outlived the focus"
        print("  PASS: lightbox label combobox state")
        box.fill(""); box.press_sequentially(FIXTURE_LABEL + "; zzmulti-a; zzmulti-b", delay=20)   # one existing + two new, typed
        box.press("Enter")
        expect(d.get_by_role("button", name="zzmulti-a", exact=True)).to_be_visible()
        expect(d.get_by_role("button", name="zzmulti-b", exact=True)).to_be_visible()
        expect(d.get_by_role("button", name=FIXTURE_LABEL, exact=True)).to_have_count(1)  # not duplicated
        print("  PASS: lightbox adds several labels")
        box.fill(""); box.press_sequentially("zztest;zzcal", delay=20)   # typed, as a user would
        opt = options(page).filter(has_text=re.compile(r"^zzcalanque$")).first
        expect(opt).to_be_visible()
        opt.click()
        expect(box).to_have_value("zztest;zzcalanque; ")    # earlier segment kept, completed, auto-';
        box.press("Enter")                                  # commit the built list
        expect(d.get_by_role("button", name="zztest", exact=True)).to_be_visible()
        expect(d.get_by_role("button", name="zzcalanque", exact=True)).to_be_visible()
        print("  PASS: lightbox completes last segment")
        box.press_sequentially("zzcal", delay=20)
        expect(options(page).filter(has_text=re.compile(r"^zzcalanque$"))).to_have_count(0)
        box.fill(""); box.press_sequentially("zzcig", delay=20)
        expect(options(page).filter(has_text=re.compile(r"^zzcigale$")).first).to_be_visible()
        print("  PASS: lightbox completion skips present")
        box.fill(""); box.press_sequentially("zzcou", delay=20)
        expect(options(page).first).to_be_visible()
        box.press("ArrowDown"); box.press("Enter")              # apply the highlight → fills "zzcousin; "
        expect(box).to_have_value("zzcousin; ")
        box.press("Enter")                                      # nothing highlighted now → commit
        expect(d.get_by_role("button", name="zzcousin", exact=True)).to_be_visible()   # chip added
        print("  PASS: lightbox label keyboard")
        box.click(); box.press_sequentially("zzlbret", delay=10); box.press("Enter")
        expect(d.get_by_role("button", name="zzlbret", exact=True)).to_be_visible()    # added
        box.press_sequentially("zzlbret", delay=10); box.press("Shift+Enter")
        expect(d.get_by_role("button", name="zzlbret", exact=True)).to_have_count(0)   # removed
        print("  PASS: lightbox enter adds, shift-enter removes")
        src0 = img.get_attribute("src")
        box.fill("abc")
        box.press("ArrowRight")                                  # would step to the next doc if unguarded
        page.wait_for_timeout(200)
        expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", src0)               # same doc — the arrow stayed in the field
        print("  PASS: label edit keeps arrows in text")
        box.fill("zzreuse"); box.press("Enter")
        expect(d.get_by_role("button", name="zzreuse", exact=True)).to_be_visible()  # applied here
        d.get_by_role("button", name="next photo").click()
        reuse = d.get_by_role("button", name="＋ zzreuse", exact=True)
        expect(reuse).to_be_visible()                                                # offered on the next
        reuse.click()
        expect(d.get_by_role("button", name="zzreuse", exact=True)).to_be_visible()  # reused, no retype
        print("  PASS: lightbox reuse last label")
        box.click(); box.press_sequentially("lbadded", delay=20); box.press("Enter")
        d.get_by_role("button", name="remove " + FIXTURE_LABEL).click()
        d.get_by_role("button", name="close").click()
        search_for(page, "lbadded")                             # the word put on: the doc answers
        expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(1)
        search_for(page, FIXTURE_LABEL)                         # the word taken off: it no longer does
        expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(len(FIXTURES) - 1)
        print("  PASS: lightbox edits labels")
        open_doc(page, 0)
        d.get_by_role("button", name="zzcalanque", exact=True).click()
        expect(d).to_be_hidden()                                   # the lightbox closes
        expect(search_box(page)).to_have_value("zzcalanque")       # the filter switched to that label
        expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(1)                       # the one doc wearing it
        print("  PASS: lightbox chip filters")
        open_doc(page, 0)
        box.press_sequentially("zzcig", delay=20)
        listbox = page.get_by_role("listbox", name="suggestions")
        expect(listbox).to_be_visible()
        lb = listbox.bounding_box(); ib = box.bounding_box()
        assert lb["y"] + lb["height"] <= ib["y"] + 1, f"the completion must open above the input: list {lb} input {ib}"
        print("  PASS: lightbox completion opens upward")
        area = img.bounding_box()
        cx, cy = area["x"] + area["width"] / 2, area["y"] + area["height"] / 2
        seen = lambda: page.evaluate("() => [visualViewport.scale, visualViewport.pageLeft]")
        assert seen()[0] <= 1.01, "started already magnified"
        pinch_in(page, cx, cy)
        wait_until(page, lambda: seen()[0] > 1.5, label="the pinch reached the browser's zoom",
                   detail=lambda: f"scale is {seen()[0]}")
        at = seen()[1]
        drag_touch(page, cx + 150, cy, cx - 150, cy)      # one finger, straight across the doc
        wait_until(page, lambda: abs(seen()[1] - at) > 5, label="the magnified doc panned sideways",
                   detail=lambda: f"pageLeft went {at} → {seen()[1]}")
        print("  PASS: lightbox pinch zooms and pans")
    finally:
        drop_vocab(LABEL_WORDS)
Opening a doc — the lightbox
what
the lightbox is one doc, full size, opened over the wall — where you look closely and edit what the archive holds about it: its labels, its state, its date.
  • example: to actually watch a clip, or to read and fix a doc’s labels.
Opening and closing
what
an open doc shows its web copy — a clip as a clip with its controls, a photo as an image — its date, and its labels as removable chips.
  • rule: the ✕ or Escape closes it again.

expect(d.locator(".lb-date")).to_have_text(page.evaluate(f"() => new Date('{FIXTURES[0]['date']}').toLocaleString('fr-FR')"))   # its date
expect(d.get_by_text(FIXTURE_LABEL)).to_be_visible()     # its labels are shown
d.get_by_role("button", name="close").click()
expect(d).to_be_hidden()
print("  PASS: lightbox opens and closes")
rule
a click that lands on nothing that acts — the backdrop, the image, the empty margins — closes it too.
  • rule: only a control swallows the click and keeps it open.

sel = d.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile("select"))
sel.click()                                        # a control acts → the modal stays
expect(sel).to_have_text(re.compile("selected"))   # the click reached the button, didn't leak to close
expect(d).to_be_visible()
d.get_by_role("img").click()                       # the image doesn't act → the modal closes
expect(d).to_be_hidden()
print("  PASS: lightbox click outside content closes")
how
the lightbox is one modal over the wall, and a click anywhere in it closes it unless it lands on something that acts.

<${Show} when=${() => opened()}>
  <div class="lb" onClick=${e => {
         if(!e.target.closest('button, a, input, textarea, select, video, [role=option], [role=listbox]')) dismissPhoto(); }}>
    <div class="lb-inner" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="photo" onWheel=${onWheel}>
      <button class="lb-close" aria-label="close" onClick=${dismissPhoto}>✕</button>
      <button class="lb-select" aria-pressed=${() => isSel(opened()?.cid) ? 'true' : 'false'}
              onClick=${() => toggle(opened().cid)}>${() => isSel(opened()?.cid) ? '✓ selected' : 'select'}</button>
      <button class="lb-frame" aria-label="frame from here" onClick=${frameFromHere}>▶ frame</button>
      <button class="lb-nav lb-prev" aria-label="previous photo" onClick=${() => step(-1)}>‹</button>
      <button class="lb-nav lb-next" aria-label="next photo" onClick=${() => step(1)}>›</button>
      <${Show} when=${() => hasMedia(opened())}
               fallback=${html`<div class="lb-media noimg">
                 <span class="ph">${() => isVideo(opened()) ? '🎬' : '🖼'}</span>
                 <span class="mt">no preview · ${() => opened()?.filename || opened()?.mimetype || ''}</span></div>`}>
        <${Show} when=${() => isVideo(opened())}
                 fallback=${html`<img class="lb-media" src=${() => mediaSrc(opened())} />`}>
          <video class="lb-media" controls autoplay ref=${el => lbVideo = el} src=${() => IPFS + opened()?.webCid}></video>
        <//>
      <//>
      <div class="lb-meta">
        <${Show} when=${() => editingDate()}
                 fallback=${html`<button class="lb-date" aria-label="edit date"
                     onClick=${() => setEditingDate(true)}>${() => opened()?.date ? new Date(opened().date).toLocaleString("fr-FR") : ''}</button>`}>
          <input class="lb-date-edit" type="datetime-local" aria-label="date"
                 ref=${el => { el.value = toLocalInput(opened()?.date); requestAnimationFrame(() => el.focus()); }}
                 onKeyDown=${e => { if(e.key === 'Enter'){ e.preventDefault(); e.target.blur(); } else if(e.key === 'Escape'){ e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); cancelEdit = true; e.target.blur(); } }}
                 onBlur=${e => commitDate(e.target.value)} />
        <//>
        <a class="lb-orig" href=${() => IPFS + (opened()?.cid || '')} target="_blank" rel="noopener"
           aria-label="original" title="original — full resolution, new tab">⤢</a>
      </div>
      <div class="lb-events">
        <${For} each=${() => lbEvents() || []}>${e => html`
          <button class="lb-event" onClick=${() => { searchEvent(e.summary); dismissPhoto(); }}>${() => e.summary}<span class="ev-when">${() => eventWhen(e)}</span></button>`}
        <//>
      </div>
      <div class="lb-states">
        <${For} each=${() => STATES}>${st => html`
          <button class="lb-st" data-st=${st} aria-pressed=${() => opened()?.state === st ? 'true' : 'false'}
                  onClick=${() => lbSetState(st)}>${st}</button>`}
        <//>
      </div>
      <div class="lb-labels">
        <${For} each=${() => labelsOf(opened())}>${w => html`
          <span class="lb-chip"><button class="lb-chip-word"
                onClick=${() => { setSearch(w); commit(); dismissPhoto(); }}>${w}</button><button class="x"
                aria-label=${'remove ' + w} onClick=${() => lbRemove(w)}>×</button></span>`}
        <//>
        <${Show} when=${() => lastLabel() && !labelsOf(opened()).includes(lastLabel())}>
          <button class="lb-reuse" onClick=${() => lbAdd(lastLabel())}>＋ ${() => lastLabel()}</button>
        <//>
        <div class="complete">
          <input class="batch-label" role="combobox" placeholder="add a label…" aria-label="add a label"
                 aria-expanded=${() => lbFocus() && (sugLoading() || sugItems().length > 0) ? 'true' : 'false'}
                 value=${() => lbText()} onInput=${e => { setLbText(e.target.value); setLbFocus(true); }}
                 onFocus=${() => setLbFocus(true)} onBlur=${() => setLbFocus(false)}
                 onKeyDown=${e => { if(e.key === 'Enter' && e.shiftKey){ e.preventDefault(); lbDrop(lbText()); return; }
                   sugNav(e, w => w ? setLbText(replaceSeg(lbText(), w) + '; ') : lbAdd(lbText())); }} />
          <${Show} when=${() => lbFocus()}>
            <${Suggest} text=${lbText} present=${() => labelsOf(opened())} active=${sugActive} onItems=${reportSug}
                        onLoading=${setSugLoading} onPick=${w => setLbText(replaceSeg(lbText(), w) + '; ')} />
          <//>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
<//>
what
the open gesture itself is a double-click.
  • what: a single tap stays the pick — a doc picked up, for an edit that acts on many at once — and a long-press arms a range.
  • therefore: opening one doc full size has its own gesture, and the three don’t collide.

tiles(page).nth(0).dblclick()
expect(dialog(page)).to_be_visible()
expect(dialog(page).get_by_role("img")).to_have_count(1)   # the photo, full size
print("  PASS: double-click opens lightbox")
what
the device back button leaves the lightbox, landing back on the wall.
  • how: opening a doc pushes a history entry, and Back pops it.
  • rule: Esc and ✕ unwind that same entry, so an explicit close and Back stay balanced — just as they do for the frame.
  • what: a doc that pushed nothing would still close on Back — by spending the app’s own root entry, the one that stands between a stray thumb and leaving Memories.
    • therefore: closing a doc would drag up the leaving-the-app question, over and over, all through a run.
  • rule: closing a doc never raises it.

asked = []
def note_leave(ask): asked.append(ask.message); ask.dismiss()
page.on("dialog", note_leave)
page.go_back()
expect(d).to_be_hidden()
expect(grid(page)).to_be_visible()
page.remove_listener("dialog", note_leave)
assert not asked, f"closing a doc with Back asked to leave the app: {asked}"
print("  PASS: back button closes lightbox")
how
the lightbox turns on one thing — the doc in view, or none — with the add-label box’s text and focus beside it.

const [opened, setOpened] = createSignal(null);
const [lbText, setLbText] = createSignal('');
const [lbFocus, setLbFocus] = createSignal(false);
const [editingDate, setEditingDate] = createSignal(false);
const isVideo = p => (p?.mimetype || '').startsWith('video');
const mediaSrc = p => IPFS + (p?.webCid || p?.thumbnailCid || '');
const hasMedia = p => isVideo(p) ? !!p?.webCid : !!(p?.webCid || p?.thumbnailCid);
const labelsOf = p => splitWords(p?.labels);
const openPhoto = p => { history.pushState({ lb: p.cid }, ''); setOpened(p); };
const closePhoto = () => { setOpened(null); setLbText(''); };
const dismissPhoto = () => (history.state && history.state.lb) ? history.back() : closePhoto();
The browser’s own menu stays shut
what
the long-press that arms a range is also how a touchscreen asks for its own save image callout, and the right button asks for the same thing on a desk.
  • what: on a tile the app has its own use for every press — this one starts a pick.
  • how: In practice, no browser will tell a test whether it went on to draw the menu; what can be read is whether the request was refused, so a listener sitting behind the app’s own reports what the app did with it.
  • how: the gesture is the right button, the one a headless browser can actually make; the finger takes the same road once it has been read as a request.

def native_menu(page, target):
    """Ask for the native menu on something, and say whether the app let it through."""
    page.evaluate("() => { window.__menu = null; addEventListener('contextmenu',"
                  " e => { window.__menu = !e.defaultPrevented; }, { once: true }); }")
    target.click(button="right")
    answer = page.evaluate("() => window.__menu")
    assert answer is not None, "no menu was ever asked for, so nothing was answered"
    return answer
rule
on a tile, the app turns that request down.

assert native_menu(page, tiles(page).nth(0)) is False, "a press on a tile should raise no menu"
print("  PASS: tile context menu suppressed")
rule
the refusal covers every surface the app draws — the open lightbox’s media as much as a tile.

assert native_menu(page, img) is False, "a press on the open doc should raise no menu"
print("  PASS: lightbox context menu suppressed")
rule
the text fields alone keep the native menu.

assert native_menu(page, search_box(page)) is True, "the search box should keep its own menu"
print("  PASS: context menu allowed in text field")
how
one listener on the window turns the request down everywhere but in a text field.

onMount(() => {   // suppress the OS context menu on our surfaces; text fields keep it (paste/select)
    const noMenu = e => { if(!e.target.closest('input, textarea, [contenteditable]')) e.preventDefault(); };
    window.addEventListener('contextmenu', noMenu);
    onCleanup(() => window.removeEventListener('contextmenu', noMenu));
});
Up close
what
the lightbox shows the downscaled web copy.
  • rule: it also offers the original file, opened in a new tab for a full-resolution look or a download.
  • how: a doc’s own address in the archive is the original’s /ipfs/ address.
rule
the metadata rows leave the media every pixel they can.
  • therefore: the offer rides on the date row as a small ⤢ glyph — an icon that reads as “open full” carries it without spending a line or a word.
  • what: an icon has no text to name it.
    • therefore: the link labels itself original for a screen reader.
  • rule: its hover title spells out the full-resolution, new-tab behaviour.

link = d.locator(".lb-meta").get_by_role("link", name="original")   # on the date row
expect(link).to_have_text("⤢")
expect(link).to_have_attribute("title", re.compile("full resolution.*new tab"))
expect(link).to_have_attribute("href", FIXTURES[0]["cid"])    # the original's /ipfs/ path
expect(link).to_have_attribute("target", "_blank")
print("  PASS: lightbox links to original")
how
the glyph follows the date on one row.

<div class="lb-meta">
  <${Show} when=${() => editingDate()}
           fallback=${html`<button class="lb-date" aria-label="edit date"
               onClick=${() => setEditingDate(true)}>${() => opened()?.date ? new Date(opened().date).toLocaleString("fr-FR") : ''}</button>`}>
    <input class="lb-date-edit" type="datetime-local" aria-label="date"
           ref=${el => { el.value = toLocalInput(opened()?.date); requestAnimationFrame(() => el.focus()); }}
           onKeyDown=${e => { if(e.key === 'Enter'){ e.preventDefault(); e.target.blur(); } else if(e.key === 'Escape'){ e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); cancelEdit = true; e.target.blur(); } }}
           onBlur=${e => commitDate(e.target.value)} />
  <//>
  <a class="lb-orig" href=${() => IPFS + (opened()?.cid || '')} target="_blank" rel="noopener"
     aria-label="original" title="original — full resolution, new tab">⤢</a>
</div>


.lb-meta{ display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; }
.lb-date{ font-size:13px; color:#9aa; }
.lb-orig{ color:#6cf; text-decoration:none; font-size:17px; line-height:1; }
.lb-orig:hover{ color:#9df; }
rule
up close means big: the lightbox takes the whole band the system leaves it.
rule
the media — photo or clip alike, they share one box — gets every pixel the metadata rows leave, scaled up as well as down.
  • what: those rows spend height and no width at all.
  • rule: the date, the state chips, the label chips and the add-label box are held to about a third of the height between them; the media gets the rest — at least 90% of the width and 65% of the height.
rule
the media is shown whole, never cropped, at the largest size that fits its box.
  • example: a portrait photo on a landscape screen, or the reverse, keeps every edge — the bars on the spare axis are the price of seeing all of it.

shown = img.bounding_box()
assert shown["width"] >= VIEWPORT["width"] * 0.9, f"media width {shown['width']} < 90% of viewport"
assert shown["height"] >= VIEWPORT["height"] * 0.65, f"media height {shown['height']} < 65% of viewport"
assert img.evaluate("el => getComputedStyle(el).objectFit") == "contain", "media crops instead of fitting whole"
print("  PASS: lightbox media fills screen")
how
the lightbox is a column filling the screen inside the system’s insets; the media is the one part allowed to grow, and fits its picture inside whatever it gets.

Putting words on it

  • A chip leads back

    what : a doc’s labels show as chips, and a chip is also the shortest way back. - rule: click one and the lightbox closes with the wall re-filtered to that label.

    d.get_by_role("button", name="zzcalanque", exact=True).click()

    how : each chip is two buttons — the word, which searches it, and its ×.

        aria-label=${'remove ' + w} onClick=${() => lbRemove(w)}>×</button></span>`}

  • Words into the box

    rule : the add-label box takes several words at once, ;-separated, and skips any the doc already carries.

    how : adding merges the typed words into the doc’s own, and dropping filters them out of it, both ending in one write of the whole list. - how: adding also remembers the last word applied, so labelling the next doc is one tap away.

    async function applyLabels(labels){
    const cid = opened().cid;
    setOpened({ ...opened(), labels });
    await gql(UPDATE_PHOTO, { cid, patch: { labels } });
    await refetch();
}
const lbAdd = input => {
    const words = splitWords(input); if(!words.length) return;
    setLastLabel(words[words.length - 1]);
    const cur = labelsOf(opened());
    for(const w of words) if(!cur.includes(w)) cur.push(w);
    setLbText('');
    return applyLabels(cur.join('; '));
};
const lbRemove = w => applyLabels(labelsOf(opened()).filter(x => x !== w).join('; '));
const lbDrop = input => { const words = splitWords(input); if(!words.length) return;
    setLbText(''); return applyLabels(labelsOf(opened()).filter(x => !words.includes(x)).join('; ')); };

  • The box at the foot of the lightbox

    rule : this box — and the frame’s add-label box — is a combobox on the same terms as the search box. - rule: it tells a screen reader whether its list of suggestions is open. - rule: a close is a state flip, not a timed guess.

    what : measures the arrows belonging to the text inside the add-label box.

    src0 = img.get_attribute("src")

    how : one window listener routes the keyboard while a doc is open, gathering the browsing keys and the triage keys — Enter to pick up, Delete to condemn, that is to mark for deletion — into one place. - scope: the whole set stands aside whenever a text field has focus, the add-label box’s suggestions included.

    onMount(() => {
    const onKey = e => {
        if(!opened()) return;
        const editing = /^(INPUT|TEXTAREA)$/.test(e.target.tagName);
        if(e.key === 'Escape') dismissPhoto();
        else if(!editing && e.key === 'ArrowRight'){ e.preventDefault(); seekOrStep(1); }
        else if(!editing && e.key === 'ArrowLeft'){ e.preventDefault(); seekOrStep(-1); }
        else if(!editing && e.key === 'Delete'){ e.preventDefault(); lbDelete(e.shiftKey); }
        else if(!editing && e.key === 'Enter'){ e.preventDefault(); toggle(opened().cid); }
        else if(!editing && e.key === ' ' && isVideo(opened()) && lbVideo){
            e.preventDefault(); const v = lbVideo;
            if(v.currentTime >= v.duration - 0.25){ v.currentTime = 0; v.play(); }
            else if(v.paused) v.play(); else v.pause();
        }
    };
    window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey);
    onCleanup(() => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey));
});

    what : one thing about that box is peculiar to the lightbox: it sits at the very foot of it, and nothing in the lightbox scrolls. - therefore: whatever ends up below that foot is not awkward but gone — a doc you opened in order to label it is a doc you cannot label. - rule: the lightbox ends where the navigation bar’s strip begins.

    rule : the completion list opens upward, above the input, rather than dropping off the bottom of a short screen with the rows you want out of reach.

Browsing without closing

  • A clip, and the run around it

    what : the original of a clip is the whole file off the camera.

    rule : a clip opens as a clip pointed at its web copy, not at its original.

    how : what fills the media box is chosen by kind, and a doc with nothing to show gets a placeholder naming it. - rule: a photo can fall back to its thumbnail when its web copy is missing, but a clip has nothing to show without one.

         fallback=${html`<div class="lb-media noimg">

    rule : the doc in front of you steps — the ‹ / › buttons or the keyboard arrows go to the previous or next doc, in the order the wall is showing. - what: measures the run wrapping into a ring.

    rule : a wheel over the doc steps too, but only with Shift held — the bare flick is left alone. - rule: a flick moves one doc, not a run: after a step the wheel goes deaf for a fifth of a second.

    over = img.bounding_box()
page.mouse.move(over["x"] + over["width"] / 2, over["y"] + over["height"] / 2)
page.keyboard.down("Shift")

    how : the ‹ / › buttons, the arrows and a Shift+wheel are three ways of asking for the same thing, so they meet in one step. - how: the wheel reads whichever axis Shift maps it to, and is held to one step per burst, plain scroll left free for the panel.

    const step = delta => {
    const list = items(); if(!list.length || !opened()) return;
    const i = list.findIndex(p => p.cid === opened().cid);
    setOpened(list[((i < 0 ? 0 : i) + delta + list.length) % list.length]); setLbText('');
};
let lbVideo = null;
const seekOrStep = dir => {
    const v = lbVideo;
    if(v && isVideo(opened()) && !v.paused &&
       (dir > 0 ? v.currentTime < v.duration - 0.25 : v.currentTime > 0.25))
        v.currentTime = Math.max(0, Math.min(v.duration, v.currentTime + dir * 5));
    else step(dir);
};
let wheelAt = 0;
const onWheel = e => {
    if(!e.shiftKey) return;
    const d = e.deltaY || e.deltaX;
    const now = performance.now();
    if(Math.abs(d) < 1 || now - wheelAt < 200) return;
    wheelAt = now; step(d > 0 ? 1 : -1);
};

    rule : the lightbox shows whether the open doc is picked up, and lets you toggle it. - how: one doc is already picked up when this one is opened, so what the wall has to show is the two of them together. - rule: the wall, still visible around the lightbox, takes the change as it happens, and goes on holding it once the doc is put away.

    what : a chip’s × is the other half of the box: the way to take a word off a doc without typing it again.

    what : a removal that never landed looks, on screen, exactly like one that did.

    rule : whatever the chips show, the archive actually keeps them: a fresh search finds the doc by the word just put on it, and no longer by the word just taken off.

    async function applyLabels(labels){
    const cid = opened().cid;
    setOpened({ ...opened(), labels });

}
