Closer than the screen
what
this is what earns the lightbox its name: the whole point of opening a doc full size is to look closer, and closer than the screen means two fingers.
  • example: to read a sign in the background, or to be sure whose face that is.
rule
magnified, you have to move about.
  • what: a zoom you cannot travel shows you the middle of the doc and nothing else.
what
the browser does both of those perfectly on its own.
  • therefore: the app puts no pinch and no drag of its own on the media.
rule
two fingers magnify, as on any picture, and one then travels.

area = img.bounding_box()
cx, cy = area["x"] + area["width"] / 2, area["y"] + area["height"] / 2
seen = lambda: page.evaluate("() => [visualViewport.scale, visualViewport.pageLeft]")
assert seen()[0] <= 1.01, "started already magnified"
pinch_in(page, cx, cy)
wait_until(page, lambda: seen()[0] > 1.5, label="the pinch reached the browser's zoom",
           detail=lambda: f"scale is {seen()[0]}")
at = seen()[1]
drag_touch(page, cx + 150, cy, cx - 150, cy)      # one finger, straight across the doc
wait_until(page, lambda: abs(seen()[1] - at) > 5, label="the magnified doc panned sideways",
           detail=lambda: f"pageLeft went {at} → {seen()[1]}")
print("  PASS: lightbox pinch zooms and pans")
Into the frame, from the lightbox
what
The frame launches from the wall, over whatever the query narrowed to.
how
landing on a chosen slide is something the frame already does: it opens on whichever slide matches the one it remembers, the way it resumes after a reboot.
  • therefore: launching from the lightbox is seeding that memory with the open doc, dropping the lightbox, and entering — the strip settles on that very slide.
rule
the lightbox carries a ▶ frame button too — a tap from the doc already open — and it opens the show on the doc you’re looking at rather than back at the first slide.

d.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile("frame", re.I)).click()
expect(d).to_be_hidden()                         # the lightbox gives way to the show
strip = page.get_by_role("list", name="slideshow")
expect(strip).to_be_visible()
wait_until(page, lambda: strip.evaluate(CENTERED) == middle["thumbnailCid"],
           label="the show opens on the doc you were looking at",
           detail=lambda: f"it opened on {strip.evaluate(CENTERED)!r}")
print("  PASS: frame from lightbox")
how
the button sits at the top of the lightbox, between the pick toggle and close.

<button class="lb-frame" aria-label="frame from here" onClick=${frameFromHere}>▶ frame</button>


.lb-frame{ position:absolute; top:-6px; left:50%; transform:translateX(-50%); z-index:2;
           padding:6px 12px; border:none; border-radius:8px; background:#262a40;
           color:var(--fg); font-size:12px; cursor:pointer; }
.lb-frame:hover{ background:#33395a; }
rule
the back button unwinds the whole way down — frame → lightbox → wall — so coming out of the frame lands back on the doc you left.

page.go_back()                                   # out of the show…
expect(strip).to_be_hidden()
expect(d.get_by_role("img")).to_have_attribute("src", middle["thumbnailCid"])   # …onto the doc it came from
page.go_back()                                   # out of the lightbox…
expect(d).to_be_hidden()
expect(grid(page)).to_be_visible()               # …back to the wall
print("  PASS: back from frame returns to lightbox")
how
the handler writes the open doc’s address where the frame looks for the slide to resume on, closes the lightbox, and enters.
  • how: the lightbox’s history entry stays underneath the frame’s.

const frameFromHere = () => { const cur = opened(); if(!cur) return;
    localStorage.setItem(FRAME_CID_KEY, cur.cid);    // the slide the frame will open on
    closePhoto();                                    // hide the modal but leave its history entry
    enterFrame(); };

Saying no, quickly

what
most of a burst is not worth keeping.
  • example: eleven near-identical shots of the same moment, and one of them is the one.
  • therefore: sweeping a burst down to the keepers means saying no far more often than yes.
rule
the no has to be the cheapest gesture in the app.
  • what: it is also the only destructive one, which pulls the other way.
  • rule: cheap enough to repeat forty times, dear enough that it cannot happen by accident.
    • how: it asks the first time, and there is a way to tell it you know what you are doing.
what
the same keyboard is being used to type labels a second earlier.
  • therefore: it has to know the difference between condemning a doc and rubbing out a letter.
rule
a run like this is read with nothing filtered out.
  • scope: working the todo run instead, each doc would drop off the wall as you condemned it and the run would shrink under you — which is its own story, and a different feeling.
  • what: here you are going along a row looking at everything.
    • therefore: a doc you have just condemned stays where it is, and the next one is still next.
  • how: none of them starts out condemned — whatever else they are.
    • therefore: a doc reading condemned afterwards can only have been marked by the key just pressed.
what
a card dump — everything off a camera’s card — is not all photographs.
  • what: a clip is the one thing on the wall that cannot be judged from a still — you have to watch some of it.
  • how: the run opens on one.
  • rule: the keys that would step you along the row have to serve the clip first — space to start and stop it, the arrows to jump through it — right up until it has nothing left to show.
    • what: at that point an arrow gives up and hands you the next doc.

@testcase
def test_saying_no_quickly(page):
    """Running down a stack marking rejects: spotting the clip at the head of it from the
    wall, watching it, then asking the first time, taking Shift for the rest, and staying
    out of the way while you are typing."""
    make_fixtures()
    gql(CREATE, {"p": VIDEO_FIXTURE})
    page.route("**" + VIDEO_FIXTURE["webCid"], lambda r: r.fulfill(
        status=200, body=CLIP_WEBM, content_type="video/webm",
        headers={"Accept-Ranges": "bytes"}))
    try:
        open_app(page); chip(page, "all").click()
        search_for(page, FIXTURE_LABEL)
        expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(len(FIXTURES) + 1)
        expect(grid(page).get_by_title("video")).to_have_count(1)   # one of them, and only one, is badged
        print("  PASS: clip tiles are marked")
        open_doc(page, 0)                       # the clip: earliest in the run
        d = dialog(page)
        v = d.locator("video")
        expect(v).to_be_visible()
        assert VIDEO_FIXTURE["webCid"] in (v.get_attribute("src") or ""), "wrong clip src"
        print("  PASS: lightbox clip")
        v.evaluate("el => { el.muted = true; el.playbackRate = 0.1; el.play().catch(() => {}); }")
        wait_until(page, lambda: v.evaluate("el => !el.paused && el.readyState >= 2"))
        page.keyboard.press(" ")                                  # SPC pauses
        wait_until(page, lambda: v.evaluate("el => el.paused"))
        page.keyboard.press(" ")                                  # SPC plays again
        wait_until(page, lambda: v.evaluate("el => !el.paused"))
        v.evaluate("el => el.currentTime = el.duration - 0.1")    # running still, and all but over
        page.keyboard.press(" ")                                  # SPC replays from the start
        wait_until(page, lambda: v.evaluate("el => el.currentTime") < 1
                                 and not v.evaluate("el => el.paused"))
        print("  PASS: lightbox clip SPC")
        v.evaluate("el => el.currentTime = 0")
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")                      # → jumps 5s in
        wait_until(page, lambda: v.evaluate("el => el.currentTime") >= 4.5)
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowLeft")                       # ← jumps back to the head of it
        wait_until(page, lambda: v.evaluate("el => el.currentTime") < 0.25)
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowLeft")                       # nothing behind it now → out of the clip
        expect(d.get_by_role("img")).to_have_attribute("src", FIXTURES[2]["thumbnailCid"])   # the run wraps back
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")                      # forward again, onto the clip…
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")                      # …and straight off it
        expect(d.get_by_role("img")).to_have_attribute("src", FIXTURES[0]["thumbnailCid"])
        print("  PASS: lightbox clip arrows")
        del_btn = d.get_by_role("button", name="delete", exact=True)
        expect(del_btn).to_have_attribute("aria-pressed", "false")
        asked = []
        page.on("dialog", lambda dlg: (asked.append(dlg.message), dlg.accept()))
        page.keyboard.press("Delete")
        expect(del_btn).to_have_attribute("aria-pressed", "true")   # moved to delete
        assert asked, "Delete should have asked to confirm"
        print("  PASS: lightbox delete confirms")
        d.get_by_role("button", name="next photo").click()
        expect(del_btn).to_have_attribute("aria-pressed", "false")   # a fresh doc, not yet condemned
        asked.clear()
        page.keyboard.press("Shift+Delete")
        expect(del_btn).to_have_attribute("aria-pressed", "true")
        assert not asked, "Shift+Delete should not ask to confirm"
        print("  PASS: lightbox shift-delete skips confirm")
        d.get_by_role("button", name="next photo").click()
        expect(del_btn).to_have_attribute("aria-pressed", "false")
        box = d.get_by_placeholder("add a label…")
        box.click(); box.press_sequentially("zzoops", delay=10)
        box.press("ArrowLeft"); box.press("Delete")                  # rubbing out the last letter
        expect(box).to_have_value("zzoop")
        expect(del_btn).to_have_attribute("aria-pressed", "false")   # the doc is untouched
        print("  PASS: lightbox delete in a field is text editing")
    finally:
        page.unroute("**" + VIDEO_FIXTURE["webCid"])
        gql(DELETE, {"cid": VIDEO_FIXTURE["cid"]})
Telling a clip from a photo
what
a clip’s poster — the still its tile shows — looks like any photo.
  • therefore: on the wall you can’t tell you could press play.
rule
a clip wearing a poster earns a play badge.
  • how: the file’s kind, as the archive records it, says which is which.
  • scope: a clip with no poster at all already shows the film placeholder (placeholder tiles), so it needs no extra mark.
rule
on a wall of photos holding a single clip, exactly one tile carries the badge.

expect(grid(page).get_by_title("video")).to_have_count(1)   # one of them, and only one, is badged
print("  PASS: clip tiles are marked")
how
the badge is a play triangle laid over the poster, shown for a clip that carries one.

<${Show} when=${() => isVideo(photo) && photo.thumbnailCid}>
  <span class="play" title="video">▶</span>
<//>
rule
the badge is pure decoration — the tap, the double-click and the long-press reach the tile untouched.
  • how: it lets pointer events fall through to the tile.
how
a small translucent disc, centred, with the triangle nudged right so it reads as centred to the eye.

.tile .play{ position:absolute; top:50%; left:50%; transform:translate(-50%, -50%);
             width:34px; height:34px; border-radius:50%; background:#000a; color:#fff;
             display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center;
             font-size:15px; padding-left:3px; pointer-events:none; }
Condemning with a key
rule
in the lightbox — one doc opened large over the wall — the Delete key condemns the open doc, marking it delete.
  • rule: it then re-anchors and closes just as a button press would.
  • how: it goes through the same state-setting a button press uses.
rule
it asks the first time — pressing Delete raises a confirm, and accepting it moves the open doc to delete.

del_btn = d.get_by_role("button", name="delete", exact=True)
expect(del_btn).to_have_attribute("aria-pressed", "false")
asked = []
page.on("dialog", lambda dlg: (asked.append(dlg.message), dlg.accept()))
page.keyboard.press("Delete")
expect(del_btn).to_have_attribute("aria-pressed", "true")   # moved to delete
assert asked, "Delete should have asked to confirm"
print("  PASS: lightbox delete confirms")
rule
Shift+Delete is the way to tell it you know what you are doing — the same move without the question.

d.get_by_role("button", name="next photo").click()
expect(del_btn).to_have_attribute("aria-pressed", "false")   # a fresh doc, not yet condemned
asked.clear()
page.keyboard.press("Shift+Delete")
expect(del_btn).to_have_attribute("aria-pressed", "true")
assert not asked, "Shift+Delete should not ask to confirm"
print("  PASS: lightbox shift-delete skips confirm")
how
Shift is what forces past the confirm.

const lbDelete = force => { if(force || confirm('Mark this for deletion?')) lbSetState('delete'); };
rule
condemning a doc is told from rubbing out a letter — mid-word in the add-label box, reaching to rub out a typo, Delete is nothing but text editing.
  • how: it obeys the same guard as the arrows, which act only while no field has focus.

d.get_by_role("button", name="next photo").click()
expect(del_btn).to_have_attribute("aria-pressed", "false")
box = d.get_by_placeholder("add a label…")
box.click(); box.press_sequentially("zzoops", delay=10)
box.press("ArrowLeft"); box.press("Delete")                  # rubbing out the last letter
expect(box).to_have_value("zzoop")

print("  PASS: lightbox delete in a field is text editing")
A clip under the keys
what
a clip’s last quarter-second counts as its end, whether or not the element has got round to saying so.
  • what: a clip that is all but over and one that has just stopped are the same thing to the hand on the key.
how
that edge is a quarter of a second wide, and a clip running at speed crosses it between a key being sent and the app seeing it.
  • therefore: this one is played at a tenth speed, at which a quarter-second is long enough to press a key inside.
  • how: it is played with the sound off, too.
  • how: it stays slowed for as long as it is the clip on screen; stepping away and back mounts a fresh one, at ordinary speed.
rule
SPC is the space that starts and stops the clip, whether or not the clip’s own controls have focus.
  • rule: on a clip at its end it replays from the start rather than leaving you on a frozen last frame.

v.evaluate("el => { el.muted = true; el.playbackRate = 0.1; el.play().catch(() => {}); }")
wait_until(page, lambda: v.evaluate("el => !el.paused && el.readyState >= 2"))
page.keyboard.press(" ")                                  # SPC pauses
wait_until(page, lambda: v.evaluate("el => el.paused"))
page.keyboard.press(" ")                                  # SPC plays again
wait_until(page, lambda: v.evaluate("el => !el.paused"))
v.evaluate("el => el.currentTime = el.duration - 0.1")    # running still, and all but over
page.keyboard.press(" ")                                  # SPC replays from the start
wait_until(page, lambda: v.evaluate("el => el.currentTime") < 1
                         and not v.evaluate("el => el.paused"))
print("  PASS: lightbox clip SPC")
how
the key goes to whichever clip is on screen, reading that last quarter-second as the end.

else if(!editing && e.key === ' ' && isVideo(opened()) && lbVideo){
    e.preventDefault(); const v = lbVideo;
    if(v.currentTime >= v.duration - 0.25){ v.currentTime = 0; v.play(); }
    else if(v.paused) v.play(); else v.pause();
}
rule
while a clip is playing, the arrows jump through it — → 5s on, ← 5s back — instead of leaving it.
  • rule: the end, or the start, at which an arrow gives up and steps to the next, or previous, doc is that same quarter-second.
  • rule: a paused clip, or a photo, steps as before.
  • rule: a clip you have stepped away from and come back to is a paused clip — nothing starts it but the hand — so pressing on leaves it at once.

v.evaluate("el => el.currentTime = 0")
page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")                      # → jumps 5s in
wait_until(page, lambda: v.evaluate("el => el.currentTime") >= 4.5)
page.keyboard.press("ArrowLeft")                       # ← jumps back to the head of it
wait_until(page, lambda: v.evaluate("el => el.currentTime") < 0.25)
page.keyboard.press("ArrowLeft")                       # nothing behind it now → out of the clip
expect(d.get_by_role("img")).to_have_attribute("src", FIXTURES[2]["thumbnailCid"])   # the run wraps back
page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")                      # forward again, onto the clip…
page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")                      # …and straight off it
expect(d.get_by_role("img")).to_have_attribute("src", FIXTURES[0]["thumbnailCid"])
print("  PASS: lightbox clip arrows")
how
a playing clip takes the arrows first, seeking within it before it steps off it.

let lbVideo = null;
const seekOrStep = dir => {
    const v = lbVideo;
    if(v && isVideo(opened()) && !v.paused &&
       (dir > 0 ? v.currentTime < v.duration - 0.25 : v.currentTime > 0.25))
        v.currentTime = Math.max(0, Math.min(v.duration, v.currentTime + dir * 5));
    else step(dir);
};

Judging a run down to nothing

what
this is the story triage exists for.
how
a state filter on the wall — todo, say — holds everything still waiting on you, and you open the first of them.
rule
from then on you should not have to steer — judge, and the next one is in front of you; judge again, and so on until there is nothing left and the app gets out of your way.
what
what makes it awkward to build is that judging a doc removes it from the filter you are reading.
  • what: the run shifts under the open doc at the very moment you need it to say where to go next.
  • what: the obvious implementations all land you on the one you just finished with, or on the one before it that you dealt with a minute ago.
what
the run wraps — past its last doc comes its first again — so it is a ring.
what
in a ring of two, the one after and the one before are the same doc.
  • therefore: a step forward cannot be told from a step back.
  • therefore: the wrap has to be judged from a ring of at least three.
what
one is already gone by then.
  • therefore: four is the smallest run that can show the difference at every stage.
  • therefore: the run needs four docs at todo rather than the usual three.

RUN_N = len(FIXTURES) + 1                      # the usual three, and one more to wrap on


@testcase
def test_judging_a_run_down_to_nothing(page):
    """Working a filter to the end: each judgement hands you the next doc, the last
    comes round to the first, emptying the run closes it — and the docs are all still
    there, under the chip you sent them to, which is where you come back to."""
    make_fixtures()
    fourth = {"cid": "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzbatchfix-3", "date": "2020-04-15T12:00:00Z", "mimetype": "image/jpeg",
              "thumbnailCid": "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzbatchfix-thumb-3", "labels": FIXTURE_LABEL, "state": "todo"}
    gql(DELETE, {"cid": fourth["cid"]}); gql(CREATE, {"p": fourth})
    for f in FIXTURES[1:]:
        gql(UPDATE, {"cid": f["cid"], "patch": {"state": "todo"}})    # four todos, Jan..Apr
    try:
        open_app(page)
        search_for(page, FIXTURE_LABEL)
        expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(RUN_N)              # default filter is todo
        expect(thumb_imgs(page).nth(3)).to_have_attribute("src", re.compile(r"/ipfs/"))  # loaded, not still blank
        behind, ahead = (thumb_imgs(page).nth(i).get_attribute("src") for i in (0, 2))
        open_doc(page, 1)                                     # the second of four
        d = dialog(page)
        img = d.get_by_role("img")
        d.get_by_role("button", name="done", exact=True).click()   # leaves the todo filter
        expect(d).to_be_visible()                             # still open…
        expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", ahead)           # …on the doc that took its place
        assert img.get_attribute("src") != behind, "the modal stepped backwards"
        print("  PASS: judging one lands on the next, not the previous")
        onto_last = thumb_imgs(page).nth(2).get_attribute("src")   # the last of the three left
        d.get_by_role("button", name="next photo").click()
        expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", onto_last)            # settled on it before judging it
        d.get_by_role("button", name="done", exact=True).click()
        expect(d).to_be_visible()
        expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", behind)          # round to the first, not back to the end
        print("  PASS: judging the last comes round to the first")
        d.get_by_role("button", name="done", exact=True).click()
        expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", ahead)           # round again, to the one still standing…
        d.get_by_role("button", name="done", exact=True).click()
        expect(d).to_be_hidden()                              # …and with that one gone, nothing to show
        expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(0)
        print("  PASS: the last one judged closes the run")
        # the run is empty because they moved, not because they went
        expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(0)                  # the todo chip has nothing left
        chip(page, "all").click()
        expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(RUN_N)              # they are all still there
        chip(page, "done").click()
        expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(RUN_N)              # under the verdict you gave them
        expect(grid(page).get_by_text("done")).to_have_count(RUN_N)   # and their badges say so
        print("  PASS: state filter")
        page.reload(wait_until="commit")
        heading(page).wait_for(timeout=8000)
        expect(chip(page, "done")).to_have_attribute("aria-pressed", "true")   # remembered, not back to todo
        expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(RUN_N)                              # and the wall it was showing
        print("  PASS: state filter persists")
    finally:
        gql(DELETE, {"cid": fourth["cid"]})
Change state from the lightbox
rule
judging a doc does not need closing it.
  • what: the lightbox — one doc opened large over the wall — carries the state buttons too, and tapping one saves the state at once.
what
you are reading the run in order — one, then the next, then the next.
  • what: measures judging a doc removing it from the filter you are reading, in the lightbox.
  • rule: the lightbox stays open, the next one in front of you — never the one before, which you read a moment ago and dealt with.

d.get_by_role("button", name="done", exact=True).click()   # leaves the todo filter
expect(d).to_be_visible()                             # still open…
expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", ahead)           # …on the doc that took its place
assert img.get_attribute("src") != behind, "the modal stepped backwards"
print("  PASS: judging one lands on the next, not the previous")
what
the run is a ring — the arrows already come round at its ends.
  • therefore: judging the one at the end is no special case at all: you carry on to the first, the same single step forward as anywhere else.

onto_last = thumb_imgs(page).nth(2).get_attribute("src")   # the last of the three left
d.get_by_role("button", name="next photo").click()
expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", onto_last)            # settled on it before judging it
d.get_by_role("button", name="done", exact=True).click()
expect(d).to_be_visible()
expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", behind)          # round to the first, not back to the end
print("  PASS: judging the last comes round to the first")
what
carry on and the run empties.
  • rule: when the one you just judged was the only one left, there is nothing to show at all, and the lightbox gets out of your way rather than sitting on an empty wall.

d.get_by_role("button", name="done", exact=True).click()
expect(img).to_have_attribute("src", ahead)           # round again, to the one still standing…
d.get_by_role("button", name="done", exact=True).click()
expect(d).to_be_hidden()                              # …and with that one gone, nothing to show
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(0)
print("  PASS: the last one judged closes the run")
how
all of it falls out of one write and one re-anchor — setting the lightbox back on a doc of the run as it stands after the write.
  • what: after the write, the doc that was next around the ring has moved up into the gap, and its neighbour would answer instead.
    • therefore: the doc that was next is noted before the write.

async function lbPatch(patch){
    const list = items(), cur = opened(); if(!cur) return;
    const i = list.findIndex(p => p.cid === cur.cid);
    const nextCid = list.length > 1 ? list[(i + 1) % list.length].cid : null;
    await gql(UPDATE_PHOTO, { cid: cur.cid, patch });
    await refetch();
    requestAnimationFrame(() => {
        const l2 = items(); if(!l2.length){ dismissPhoto(); return; }
        const stay = l2.find(p => p.cid === cur.cid);
        setOpened(stay || (nextCid && l2.find(p => p.cid === nextCid)) || l2[0]);
    });
}
const lbSetState = st => lbPatch({ state: st });
Filtering by state
what
triage needs a way to ask « show me only what’s still todo ».
  • what: each doc carries a state — todo, next, done or delete.
  • what: the state filter is a row of buttons under the search box — all, plus one per state — that narrows the wall to the one pressed.
  • rule: a first-ever visit opens on todo.
what
the wall shows a spread — about 2000 docs the server draws from across the archive’s whole span.
  • rule: on an archive that is almost entirely done, todo still surfaces ~2000 todos spread across the whole span.
  • what: the spread of such an archive is mostly done, so a filter applied after it finds nearly nothing.
  • therefore: crucially, the filter is applied by the server, before it draws the spread.
scope
where that ordering is applied is not something this note measures.
  • what: a wall of four reads the same whether the filter went in before the spread or after it.
  • what: a set of fixtures large enough to tell the two apart would have to be most of an archive.
  • therefore: what is pinned below is the narrowing itself, and where the docs went.
what
a run judged down to nothing is the plainest way to see that narrowing.
  • rule: the wall you were working is empty.
  • rule: every doc that left it is still there under all, and waiting under the state you sent it to, its state chip saying so.

expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(0)                  # the todo chip has nothing left
chip(page, "all").click()
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(RUN_N)              # they are all still there
chip(page, "done").click()
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(RUN_N)              # under the verdict you gave them
expect(grid(page).get_by_text("done")).to_have_count(RUN_N)   # and their badges say so
print("  PASS: state filter")
rule
thereafter the wall opens on whatever you last chose — the choice is remembered, like the search box.
  • scope: a reload — or the frame’s reboot — comes back to the state you were last triaging, and the view you were working, not always todo.
  • how: flipping a button fetches the wall again, the state travelling with the search, and stores the choice in the browser.

page.reload(wait_until="commit")
heading(page).wait_for(timeout=8000)
expect(chip(page, "done")).to_have_attribute("aria-pressed", "true")   # remembered, not back to todo
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(RUN_N)                              # and the wall it was showing
print("  PASS: state filter persists")


// the chip choice persists; the first-ever visit defaults to the triage view (todo)
const STATE_KEY = 'memories.state';
const [stateFilter, setStateFilter] = createSignal(localStorage.getItem(STATE_KEY) || 'todo');
createEffect(() => localStorage.setItem(STATE_KEY, stateFilter()));
rule
a filter button cannot be mistaken for the like-named button of the toolbar.
  • how: the state filter’s buttons sit in a group labelled as the filter.
rule
the active button reads as pressed — to the eye, and to a screen reader alike.
  • how: to the eye, the pressed button fills with its state’s colour.

<div class="chips" role="group" aria-label="filter by state">
  ${['all', ...STATES].map(st => html`
    <button class="chip" data-st=${st} disabled=${() => photos.loading}
            aria-pressed=${() => stateFilter() === st ? 'true' : 'false'}
            onClick=${() => setStateFilter(st)}>${st}</button>`)}
  <button class="chip selall" aria-pressed=${() => allSelected() ? 'true' : 'false'}
          onClick=${toggleAll}>${() => allSelected() ? 'clear' : 'select all'}</button>
  <button class="chip frame-start" onClick=${enterFrame}>▶ frame</button>
</div>


.chips{ display:flex; gap:6px; margin-bottom:12px; flex-wrap:wrap; }
.chip{ padding:4px 12px; font-size:12px; text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:.04em;
       cursor:pointer; border-radius:999px; border:1px solid #3a3f5a;
       background:#262a40; color:#9aa; }
.chip[data-st]{ border-color:var(--st,#3a3f5a); color:var(--st,#9aa); }
.chip[aria-pressed='true']{ background:var(--st,#6cf); color:#08111e; border-color:var(--st,#6cf); font-weight:700; }
.selall{ margin-left:auto; }

Doing one thing to forty docs

what
some of triage is per-doc and some of it plainly is not.
  • example: a whole afternoon wants the same word on it; a whole card-dump wants the same state.
what
the wall lets you take a run in hand and act on all of it at once.
The size of the wall
rule
before any of that, the wall has to be at a size you can work at.
what
which size that is depends on the job.
  • example: picking a run out of a card-dump wants small tiles and a lot of them on screen.
  • example: telling two nearly-identical frames apart wants the opposite.
how
the size is yours to set, from the controls or from the hand already on the wall.
rule
it stays set.
what
nor is the size the only thing that survives coming back: the run itself is still on the wall afterwards.
what
the work carries on from where the size was settled.
Customizable thumbnail size
what
measures the size set from the controls: the − / ＋ buttons, opening at 96 for a first visit.

w0 = t.nth(0).bounding_box()["width"]
page.get_by_role("button", name="bigger thumbnails").click()
page.get_by_role("button", name="bigger thumbnails").click()
wait_until(page, lambda: t.nth(0).bounding_box()["width"] > w0 + 8)
rule
measures it stays set: reopen the app and the wall comes back at the size you left it.
  • rule: measures the run still on the wall afterwards too — the query that put those docs there comes back with it.

w1 = t.nth(0).bounding_box()["width"]
open_app(page, launch)
wait_until(page, lambda: abs(tiles(page).nth(0).bounding_box()["width"] - w1) < 2)
expect(search_box(page)).to_have_value(FIXTURE_LABEL)      # and the run is still the run
how
the size is one number kept in the browser’s own storage, so a relaunch reads back what the last session wrote, and every step is held inside the slider’s range.

const SIZE_KEY = 'memories.thumbSize';
const [thumbSize, setThumbSize] = createSignal(+localStorage.getItem(SIZE_KEY) || 96);
createEffect(() => localStorage.setItem(SIZE_KEY, thumbSize()));
const bumpSize = d => setThumbSize(s => Math.max(80, Math.min(320, s + d * 40)));
rule
measures the size set from the hand already on the wall: Ctrl+scroll over the tiles, up to grow them, down to shrink.

w2 = t.nth(0).bounding_box()["width"]
box = grid(page).bounding_box()
page.mouse.move(box["x"] + box["width"] / 2, box["y"] + 10)
page.keyboard.down("Control")
page.mouse.wheel(0, -240)                            # ctrl-scroll up → bigger
page.keyboard.up("Control")
wait_until(page, lambda: t.nth(0).bounding_box()["width"] > w2 + 8)
what
Ctrl+wheel is the browser’s own page zoom.
  • rule: the wall claims the event outright before it resizes anything, rather than leave the whole app scaling around the wall instead of the tiles in it.
  • what: page zoom happens in the browser’s own furniture rather than in the page, though, so nothing inside the document can report whether it was headed off.
  • therefore: it wants a real hand on a real trackpad.
what
a wheel arrives as a burst of notches where a finger meant one movement.
  • rule: a burst buys a single step: notches less than 120 ms apart are the same gesture, and stepping back once returns the size the burst started from.

page.wait_for_timeout(200)                           # a fresh gesture, clear of the notch above
w3 = t.nth(0).bounding_box()["width"]
page.keyboard.down("Control")
page.mouse.wheel(0, -240)
page.mouse.wheel(0, -240)                            # a second notch inside the same burst
page.keyboard.up("Control")
wait_until(page, lambda: t.nth(0).bounding_box()["width"] > w3 + 8)   # the burst moved the wall
page.get_by_role("button", name="smaller thumbnails").click()         # …by exactly one step
wait_until(page, lambda: abs(t.nth(0).bounding_box()["width"] - w3) < 2)
how
one wheel handler on the wall holds both rules, timing each notch against the last one it let through.

const SIZE_KEY = 'memories.thumbSize';
const [thumbSize, setThumbSize] = createSignal(+localStorage.getItem(SIZE_KEY) || 96);
createEffect(() => localStorage.setItem(SIZE_KEY, thumbSize()));
const bumpSize = d => setThumbSize(s => Math.max(80, Math.min(320, s + d * 40)));
let zoomAt = 0;
const onGridWheel = e => {
    if(!e.ctrlKey) return;
    e.preventDefault();
    const now = performance.now();
    if(now - zoomAt < 120) return;
    zoomAt = now; bumpSize(e.deltaY < 0 ? 1 : -1);
};

  • What a sharp tile costs

    what : a tile at the top of that range shows a 256px thumbnail at 320 — a stretch of a quarter on a desktop, and more on a phone, whose device pixels outnumber its CSS ones.

    what : sharpness here is priced per tile. - how: the price is read off the archive itself: ten docs at each of twelve evenly spaced points through it, each one’s thumbnail and its web copy, web_cid, weighed in kB.

    photos thumbnail kB web copy kB web / thumbnail
    120 5–89 33–622 3.4–16.6

    what : the next search draws a fresh wall of them. - therefore: buying the heavier rendition for a contact sheet multiplies what each fold costs by the ratio above, for pictures nobody is looking at yet.

    what : what changes as the tiles grow is not that price but the number of tiles paying it. - what: a fold holds about its area over the cell’s square in tiles. - therefore: growing the cell from the default 96px to the slider’s top, 320px, cuts the tiles by (320 / 96)² — about eleven. - therefore: the area falls out, so a phone strikes the same trade as a desktop. - therefore: a grown fold of web copies costs between about a third of and half again as much as a dense fold of thumbnails, the measured ratio running 3.4 to 16.6 against elevenfold fewer tiles.

  • Sharpening past a width

    rule : past a width the wall does the refining, to the same rendition the lightbox and the frame show.

    what : where the two curves cross is a judgement call, fixed at a drawn cell of 300px — to move by eye if the wall comes to feel either soft or heavy. - what: drawn, not chosen: the wall’s columns stretch into whatever width is left over, and a phone at the top of the slider draws a single column across its whole screen. - therefore: the threshold reads the pixels the picture is actually painted at, taken from the resolved column and not from the setting. - rule: below that width the wall buys thumbnails and nothing else — scroll it as far as you like.

    assert cell_px(page) <= 300, f"a contact sheet should be drawn under 300px, and this is {cell_px(page)}px"
page.mouse.move(REFINE_VIEWPORT["width"] / 2, REFINE_VIEWPORT["height"] / 2)
for _ in range(10):                              # all the way down the wall
    page.mouse.wheel(0, 400)
    page.wait_for_timeout(100)
assert tiles(page).last.bounding_box()["y"] < REFINE_VIEWPORT["height"], \
    "the wall never overflowed — nothing was scrolled into reach"
assert not web(), f"the dense wall fetched {len(web())} web renditions"
print("  PASS: a dense wall buys thumbnails and nothing else")

    how : in code the threshold is read off the grid itself, and two triggers keep that reading true. - how: a ResizeObserver re-measures the resolved column whenever the wall’s own box changes. - how: an effect re-measures when the slider moves the columns inside a box that has not changed. - how: Under the hood, getComputedStyle makes that reading current: it flushes the pending layout, so the effect reads the columns the new setting produces rather than the ones the last frame drew.

    const REFINE_CELL = 300;                    // drawn px
const [cellPx, setCellPx] = createSignal(0);
const measureCell = () => gridEl && setCellPx(parseFloat(getComputedStyle(gridEl).gridTemplateColumns) || 0);
const watchCell = el => { const ro = new ResizeObserver(measureCell);
                          ro.observe(el); onCleanup(() => ro.disconnect()); };
createEffect(() => { thumbSize(); measureCell(); });   // the slider moves the columns, not the grid's box
const [thumbsInFlight, setThumbsInFlight] = createSignal(0);
const refining = () => cellPx() > REFINE_CELL && thumbsInFlight() === 0;

    rule : grow the tiles past the threshold and that same wall sharpens, the thumbnail staying underneath so that nothing blinks out while the fuller picture is on its way.

    tiles(page).first.scroll_into_view_if_needed()
grow_the_wall(page)
wait_until(page, lambda: any(u.endswith("zzref-web-1") for u in web()),
           label="the tile on screen trades up to its web rendition",
           detail=lambda: f"srcs={tile_srcs(page, 1)} web={web()}")
assert any("zzref-t-1" in (s or "") for s in tile_srcs(page, 1)), "the thumbnail left from under it"
print("  PASS: a grown wall trades up, the thumbnail staying under it")

    how : a tile trades up only once its own thumbnail has settled and the wall is refining. - rule: once it has traded up it holds that claim until it leaves — whether it leaves the viewport or the wall.

    const [sharp, setSharp] = createSignal(false);
createEffect(() => { if(!near()) setSharp(false);       // gone → both layers go
                     else if(thumbOn() && refining()) setSharp(true); });
const webSrc = () => sharp() && !isVideo(photo) && photo.webCid ? IPFS + photo.webCid : '';
const [webOn, setWebOn] = createSignal(false);
createEffect(() => { webSrc(); setWebOn(false); });     // a new source → fade the overlay in again

    how : the picture is then two stacked images, as in the frame: the thumbnail carries the tile, and the fuller rendition fades in over it once it has painted. - rule: both are the same doc, so only the layer beneath is named — the overlay’s alt is empty, which keeps it out of the accessibility tree. - what: two layers is also two decoded images, and decoded pixels — not bytes on the wire — are what the reach window exists to bound. - what: whichever way a browser unpacks a rendition, that comes to at most about twice the decoded image a dense wall already held; the annex works it out.

    <${Show} when=${webSrc}>
  <img class="thumb web" classList=${() => ({ shown: webOn() })} alt="" draggable="false"
       src=${webSrc} onLoad=${() => setWebOn(true)} />
<//>


    .tile .thumb.web{ position:absolute; inset:0; opacity:0; transition:opacity .25s; }
.tile .thumb.web.shown{ opacity:1; }

    rule : measures what is off screen is not bought and a clip keeps its poster — its web copy being a film rather than a bigger poster.

    assert not [u for u in web() if u.endswith("web-79")], f"a tile far below the fold refined: {web()}"
assert not [u for u in web() if u.endswith("web-vid")], f"the clip's tile fetched its film: {web()}"
print("  PASS: a grown wall buys narrowly")

  • Thumbnails first

    what : a web copy is ten thumbnails on the wire, and issued alongside them it competes for the same bandwidth and pushes back the moment a screenful of blanks turns into pictures you can triage.

    rule : settled, not painted, is what a thumbnail owes — an address the gateway cannot serve must not hold the whole wall soft for good.

    rule : measures thumbnails first, web copies after: refinement never costs the wall its legibility — nothing refines until every thumbnail the wall is waiting for has settled.

    expect(thumb_imgs(page).first).to_have_attribute("src", f"/ipfs/{WAIT_HELD}")   # asked for…
assert not [u for u in fetched() if u.endswith(WAIT_HELD)], "…and still unanswered"
wait_until(page, lambda: len([u for u in fetched() if "zzwait-t-" in u]) >= 2,
           label="its neighbours' thumbnails have settled",
           detail=lambda: f"settled={[u for u in fetched() if 'zzwait-t-' in u]}")
page.wait_for_timeout(REFINE_GRACE_MS)
assert not web(), f"the wall refined with a thumbnail still in flight: {web()}"
print("  PASS: the wall waits for its thumbnails before refining")

    how : a tile’s part is to declare itself: it counts itself among what the wall is waiting for from the moment it comes into reach until its thumbnail settles. - how: the wall refines only past the threshold and with that count at zero.

    const [thumbOn, setThumbOn] = createSignal(false);
const thumbSettled = () => setThumbOn(true);           // painted, or failed and never coming
createEffect(() => { near(); setThumbOn(false); });     // re-shown → its source is refetched → waiting again
createEffect(() => {                                   // one of the thumbnails the wall waits for…
    if(!(near() && photo.thumbnailCid && !thumbOn())) return;
    setThumbsInFlight(n => n + 1);
    onCleanup(() => setThumbsInFlight(n => n - 1));     // …until it settles or leaves
});
const [sharp, setSharp] = createSignal(false);
createEffect(() => { if(!near()) setSharp(false);       // gone → both layers go
                     else if(thumbOn() && refining()) setSharp(true); });
const webSrc = () => sharp() && !isVideo(photo) && photo.webCid ? IPFS + photo.webCid : '';
const [webOn, setWebOn] = createSignal(false);
createEffect(() => { webSrc(); setWebOn(false); });     // a new source → fade the overlay in again


    const [thumbsInFlight, setThumbsInFlight] = createSignal(0);
const refining = () => cellPx() > REFINE_CELL && thumbsInFlight() === 0;

    what : scrolling reopens the question: fresh tiles bring fresh thumbnails to wait for, and the wall is waiting again. - rule: measures the sharpening going on past a stuck thumbnail: a tile that has already traded up keeps what it has, so the sharpening only ever moves forward, a screenful at a time.

    wait_until(page, lambda: sharp(0), label="the tile on screen sharpens",
           detail=lambda: f"srcs={tile_srcs(page, 0)}")
tiles(page).nth(2).scroll_into_view_if_needed()
wait_until(page, lambda: sharp(3), label="the tiles scrolled into reach sharpen too",
           detail=lambda: f"srcs={tile_srcs(page, 3)}")
tiles(page).nth(4).scroll_into_view_if_needed()       # doc 4 comes into reach, and never lands
wait_until(page, lambda: inreach(5), label="doc 5 has come into reach behind it",
           detail=lambda: f"srcs={tile_srcs(page, 5)}")
page.wait_for_timeout(REFINE_GRACE_MS)
assert inreach(4), f"doc 4 must be in reach to hold anything back: {tile_srcs(page, 4)}"
assert sharp(3), f"a tile handed its picture back: {tile_srcs(page, 3)}"
assert not sharp(5), f"a tile refined behind a thumbnail in flight: {tile_srcs(page, 5)}"
print("  PASS: a late thumbnail holds back what arrives behind it")

    rule : a tile out of sight lets go of its picture — the fuller one along with its thumbnail, so a wall you have left behind holds no more decoded pixels for having been sharpened.

    wait_until(page, lambda: not inreach(0), label="doc 0 has been left behind",
           detail=lambda: f"srcs={tile_srcs(page, 0)}")
assert not sharp(0), f"the fuller picture outlived the thumbnail: {tile_srcs(page, 0)}"
print("  PASS: a tile left behind drops both its pictures")

    what : a tile can also leave the wall altogether, when a search swaps the whole of it while a thumbnail is still on its way. - what: nothing here can pin that one on its own: the tally of thumbnails waited for is let go of in one place, the same place a thumbnail settling releases it. - therefore: a break that strands the departed strands the settled too, and then nothing refines anywhere — caught by the reading that a grown wall trades up, long before this one. - how: what this adds is the case the release is hardest in: everything on the wall leaving at once, while one of them was still owed an answer. - rule: the tally lets go of whatever left with it, and the wall that replaced it sharpens too.

    search_for(page, FWD_LABEL_AFTER)                    # swapped out from under a thumbnail in flight
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(len(FWD_DOCS_AFTER))
wait_until(page, lambda: any("zzfwd2-web-0" in (s or "") for s in tile_srcs(page, 0)),
           label="the wall that replaced it sharpens too",
           detail=lambda: f"srcs={tile_srcs(page, 0)}")
print("  PASS: a wall swapped out from under a thumbnail refines again")
Picking a run up
rule
picking things up has to be quiet.
  • what: the toolbar — the row of buttons that act on what is picked up — appears the moment the first one is taken.
  • rule: nothing on the wall may move as it does.
what
the wall is not the only place a run gets picked up — half of it comes together while you are looking at the docs one at a time.
how
the open doc carries the same toggle, under the mouse and under the keys.
  • rule: what it picks is the same run the wall is holding.
what
the same box that labels one doc labels the lot — by button or by keyboard, the two never drifting apart.
what
it takes words off again as readily as it puts them on.
rule
on a screen so short that the search box’s offers come down over the toolbar, the offers sit on top and take the touch.
Saying when the wall holds a slice
what
a match can hold more than the 2000 docs the wall shows at most — its cap — and the wall then shows a spread of it.
  • rule: the wall names the slice it shows against the true total of the match.
    • example: showing a spread of N from M — narrow… when the spread is the one that chose.
    • how: the query asks the archive for that true total alongside the docs.
rule
the subtle part is when: the notice fires only on a genuine spread.
  • what: every match is shown — one with no thumbnail as a placeholder tile — so « shown » equals what the archive returned.
  • therefore: the honest signal is simply whether the archive dropped rows — returned fewer docs than match.
    • what: a thumbnail-less match never raises it.
  • what: a spread that hands back a few short of what it was asked for is a different spread.
  • rule: the N the line names is the cap on the nose, not roughly two thousand — this line is where the difference shows.

expect(page.get_by_text(re.compile(r"showing a spread of 2000 from \d+"))).to_be_visible()
print("  PASS: sampling notice")
rule
under the cap there is nothing to confess, and the line says so rather than going quiet: showing all N.

expect(page.get_by_text(re.compile(rf"^showing all {len(FIXTURES)}$"))).to_be_visible()
print("  PASS: count always shown")
what
a spread is not the only slice the wall can be holding: ask it for the first or last twenty and twenty is what arrives.
  • what: those are one end of the match, not a taste of the whole of it.
  • what: measures the wall saying which slice it holds: it never calls an end a spread.
  • what: the distinction reaches past the notice — an end is a run and a spread is not, and a run is what a range selection needs to mean anything.
the wall holds the line reads it advises range selection
every match showing all N — yes
the first N showing the first N of M — yes
the last N showing the last N of M — yes
a spread showing a spread of N from M narrow it no
how
each slice is one gesture — a query typed and committed — and the wall says at once which slice it holds and which docs.
  • how: so the asking happens here, once per row of that table, and what came back is read from the same wall further on rather than asked for again.
  • rule: each of the three reads as its row of the table says, the spread alone advising to narrow the search or date range.

search_for(page, "zzpick; first:2")
expect(page.get_by_text(re.compile(r"showing the first 2 of \d+$"))).to_be_visible()   # $: nothing follows


search_for(page, "zzpick; last:2")
expect(page.get_by_text(re.compile(r"showing the last 2 of \d+$"))).to_be_visible()


search_for(page, "zzpick; sample:4")
expect(page.get_by_text(re.compile(r"showing a spread of 4 from \d+"))).to_be_visible()
expect(page.get_by_text(re.compile(r"narrow the search or date range"))).to_be_visible()
how
the line is written from the archive’s own answer — whether it dropped rows, and which end was asked for — never from what was typed.

<${Show} when=${() => !photos.loading && !photos.error && items().length === 0 && !authNeeded()}>
  <p class="empty">No photos.</p>
<//>
<${Show} when=${() => items().length > 0}>
  <p class="countline">${() => {
    if(!photos()?.sampled) return `showing all ${items().length}`;
    const end = photos()?.pick;
    return end ? `showing the ${end} ${items().length} of ${total()}`
      : `showing a spread of ${items().length} from ${total()} — narrow the search or date range to see them all`;
  }}</p>
<//>

  • Saying the wall is working

    what : the wall reads afresh on every filter change. - rule: it goes quiet again once the read has answered. - rule: while that read is out the wall says it is busy, so a screen reader holds its reading and anything watching waits for the settled result rather than read a wall mid-load. - how: In practice, the grid carries aria-busy.

    expect(grid(page)).to_have_attribute("aria-busy", "true")      # a read is out — the region is working
print("  PASS: wall reports busy")

    rule : the busy state also covers an edit, from its first write until the edit’s re-read has landed the committed result on the wall. - how: a count of edits under way is kept around each batch edit, and the wall reads busy while a read is out or that count is above zero.

    expect(grid(page)).to_have_attribute("aria-busy", "true")   # busy during the WRITE phase
print("  PASS: wall busy during edit")

    rule : a sighted user sees the wait too, read as working on a known thing, not as broken or already done: while the wall settles it dims and shows a small cue, a pill. - what: searching «…» while a read is out, naming the query it is fetching. - what: updating… while an edit writes.

    BG = "el => getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor"
working = page.get_by_text("updating…")
expect(working).to_be_visible()
pending = working.evaluate(BG)                   # the colour of a wait, to tell a failure from
print("  PASS: wall shows updating feedback")

    how : one pill speaks for every wait: while a read is out it is also that read’s way out, and once an edit is given up on, the notice takes its place.

    <${Show} when=${() => photos.loading || mutating()}>
  <${Show} when=${() => photos.loading && !mutating()}
           fallback=${html`<div class="wall-busy" aria-hidden="true">updating…</div>`}>
    <button class="wall-busy busy-cancel" onClick=${cancelRead}
            aria-label=${() => 'cancel search: ' + (running().label || 'everything')}>${() => `searching «${running().label || 'everything'}»`}</button>
  <//>
<//>
<${Show} when=${() => editStalled()}>
  <div class="wall-busy wall-stalled" role="status">the edit did not go through — try again</div>
<//>

  • An edit that never answers

    what : a write can simply never come back — the connection drops between the phone and the house, and nothing answers. - rule: an edit is only credited as working while its writes keep answering. - what: fifteen seconds of silence is taken as the answer that is not coming. - how: ?editms= in the address overrides the span. - rule: measures the wall giving up and saying the edit did not go through: it goes quiet to the eye and to a screen reader alike, in the colour of something wrong rather than something pending.

    failed = page.get_by_role("status")
expect(failed).to_have_text("the edit did not go through — try again")
expect(page.get_by_text("updating…")).to_have_count(0)      # it stopped claiming to work…
expect(grid(page)).to_have_attribute("aria-busy", "false")  # …to everyone, not just the eye
assert failed.evaluate(BG) != pending, "a failed edit wears the colour of one still going"
print("  PASS: a write that never answers is given up on")

    what : giving up is a guess, though, and the wifi does come back: a write written off can land minutes later. - rule: measures the notice taken back when the write turns up after all: it is not a verdict, and goes the moment the edit it was about finishes.

    for r in dropped: r.fallback()                   # the write we had written off goes out after all
expect(page.get_by_role("status")).to_have_count(0)   # the app stops saying it failed…
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(0)                 # …the edit landed
expect(grid(page)).to_have_attribute("aria-busy", "false")
print("  PASS: a write that lands late takes the notice back")

    how : one wrapper around every edit holds that count of edits under way, the clock and the notice together.

    const [editStalled, setEditStalled] = createSignal(false);
const EDIT_SILENCE_MS = Number(new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('editms')) || 15000;
async function editing(run){
    setMutating(m => m + 1); setEditStalled(false);
    let counted = true, timer = null;
    const giveUp = () => { if(!counted) return;
        counted = false; setMutating(m => m - 1); setEditStalled(true); };
    const tick = () => { clearTimeout(timer); timer = setTimeout(giveUp, EDIT_SILENCE_MS); };
    tick();
    try { await run(tick); setEditStalled(false); }
    catch(e){ setEditStalled(true); throw e; }
    finally { clearTimeout(timer); if(counted){ counted = false; setMutating(m => m - 1); } }
}

    what : slow is not the same as dead, and a run of forty is slow by construction. - how: the two are told apart by a connection that answers late but always — every gap under the limit, the whole edit far over it. - rule: the clock is re-armed by every write that lands, not by the edit as a whole: what is being waited on is one answer. - therefore: an edit whose writes each come back inside the fifteen seconds runs as long as it likes.

    for i in range(len(FIXTURES)):
    wait_until(page, lambda: len(stalled) > i, label="the next write went out")
    page.wait_for_timeout(700)                                  # late, but inside the second
    expect(page.get_by_text("the edit did not go through — try again")).to_have_count(0)
    stalled[i].fallback()                                       # …and it answers
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(0)              # the whole edit landed: the selection cleared…
expect(grid(page)).to_have_attribute("aria-busy", "false")   # …and the wall has read it back
print("  PASS: a slow edit is waited out")

    what : the third way is the plainest: the archive answers, and the answer is no. - rule: a refusal is an answer, so the wall goes quiet at once — but it is not the edit going through, so it wears the same notice as a silence given up on. - rule: only a write that worked retracts the notice; an error arriving after the clock has run out changes nothing about whether the edit happened. - rule: the refusal stops the edit where it stands, rather than carrying on down the run. - rule: the word stays in the box, ready to try again.

    expect(page.get_by_role("status")).to_have_text("the edit did not go through — try again")
expect(page.get_by_text("updating…")).to_have_count(0)
expect(grid(page)).to_have_attribute("aria-busy", "false")
expect(tb.get_by_placeholder("add a label…")).to_have_value("zzrefused")   # ready to try again
print("  PASS: a refused edit says so")
Selecting tiles and batch-editing
what
triage goes far faster in bulk: pick tiles, then apply one change to all of them at once.
  • example: a word merged into each doc’s labels, or a state set on each.
what
the wall holds at most 2000, while a filter may match thousands.
  • how: the reach switch — the toolbar’s all N matching button — turns the same buttons to the archive’s bulk edits, which change every doc the query matches in one statement.
  • rule: touching the picks or the filter turns the switch off, so no edit reaches a stale scope.
what
a plain click toggles one tile and makes it the anchor — the tile a run is counted from.
  • what: the run from the anchor to a target tile, in the wall’s date order, can be picked several ways.
  • rule: those ways share one mechanism, so they cannot drift apart.
rule
the picks persist, so a refresh mid-triage keeps the run in hand.
how
the picks are one signal holding a set; each pick replaces the set, and only the touched tiles redraw.
  • how: beside them sit the flags the gestures read: whether a range is armed for the next tap, and whether the reach switch is on.

const STATES = ['todo', 'next', 'done', 'delete'];
const SEL_KEY = 'memories.selected';
const [selected, setSelected] = createSignal(new Set(JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(SEL_KEY) || '[]')));
createEffect(() => localStorage.setItem(SEL_KEY, JSON.stringify([...selected()])));
const [labelText, setLabelText] = createSignal('');
const [labelFocus, setLabelFocus] = createSignal(false);
const [anchor, setAnchor] = createSignal(null);
const [rangeMode, setRangeMode] = createSignal(false);
const [allMatching, setAllMatching] = createSignal(false);
const canRange = () => !photos()?.sampled || !!photos()?.pick;
createEffect(() => { if(!canRange()) setRangeMode(false); });
const isSel = cid => selected().has(cid);
const selCount = () => selected().size;
const clearSel = () => { setSelected(new Set()); setRangeMode(false); setAllMatching(false); };
const toggle = cid => { setAllMatching(false); setSelected(s => {
    const n = new Set(s); n.has(cid) ? n.delete(cid) : n.add(cid); return n;
}); };

  • Many ways to one run

    • Picking the whole wall

      what : a select all toggle closes the state filter’s row: one tap picks the whole wall shown, another clears it. - scope: it lives outside the toolbar, which is hidden while nothing is picked. - example: with the state filter, it is the fast path: filter next, select all, set done.

      select_all(page).click()
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(n)                # every tile shows its ✓
select_all(page).click()
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(0)                # second tap clears
print("  PASS: select all")

      how : the toggle reads the wall shown: a tap picks every tile on it, unless all of them are picked already, and then it clears.

      const shownCids = () => items().map(p => p.cid);
const allSelected = () => { const a = shownCids(); return a.length > 0 && a.every(isSel); };
const toggleAll = () => allSelected() ? clearSel() : setSelected(new Set(shownCids()));

    • From the anchor to a tile

      what : on a desktop, a shift-click on the target tile picks the whole run from the anchor to it.

      t.nth(0).click()                                  # anchor on the first tile
t.nth(n - 1).click(modifiers=["Shift"])           # extend the selection to the last
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(n)             # the ones between are roped in too
print("  PASS: range select")

      how : the run is added in one shot, every tile from the anchor to the target joining the picks.

      const extendTo = cid => {
    const list = items().map(p => p.cid);
    const a = list.indexOf(anchor()), b = list.indexOf(cid);
    if(a < 0 || b < 0){ toggle(cid); setAnchor(cid); return; }
    const [lo, hi] = a < b ? [a, b] : [b, a];
    setSelected(s => { const n = new Set(s);
        for(let i = lo; i <= hi; i++) n.add(list[i]); return n; });
};
const extendRun = cid => {
    if(!canRange()) return;
    const list = items();
    const a = list.findIndex(p => p.cid === anchor()), ni = list.findIndex(p => p.cid === cid);
    if(a < 0 || ni < 0) return;
    if(!extending){ extending = true; rangeBase = new Set(selected()); }
    const [lo, hi] = a < ni ? [a, ni] : [ni, a];
    setSelected(new Set([...rangeBase, ...list.slice(lo, hi + 1).map(p => p.cid)]));
};

      what : on touch, which has no modifier key, the toolbar’s ↔ range toggle stands in: arm it, tap the target, and the same run is picked. - rule: the toggle disarms once the run is picked.

      t.nth(0).click()                                  # anchor + toolbar appears
rng = toolbar(page).get_by_role("button", name="range")
rng.click()                                       # arm range mode (the touch route)
t.nth(n - 1).click()                              # a plain tap now extends the run
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(n)
expect(rng).to_have_attribute("aria-pressed", "false")   # disarmed after extending
print("  PASS: range select (touch)")

      what : a long-press on a tile arms the range anchored there, with no trip to the toolbar, and the next tap completes the run. - rule: the long-press opens no lightbox; a double-click stays the gesture that opens a doc.

      press_and_hold(page, t.nth(0)); page.mouse.up()   # held past the threshold, then let go
expect(dialog(page)).to_have_count(0)             # no lightbox — the long-press starts a selection
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(1)             # the pressed tile, now the anchor
t.nth(n - 1).click()                              # a plain tap completes the range
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(n)
print("  PASS: long-press arms range")

      how : a click extends the range only with shift on a desktop, or with the range armed on touch, and either way it disarms the range.

      how : a plain click also plants the keyboard cursor on its tile, so the arrows carry on from where you clicked.

      how : arming a range from a tile makes it the anchor and readies a fresh run for the first drag move.

      const onTileClick = (e, cid) => {
    setCursor(cid);
    if((e.shiftKey || rangeMode()) && anchor() !== null && canRange()){
        extendTo(cid); setRangeMode(false); return;
    }
    toggle(cid); setAnchor(cid);
};
const armRange = cid => {
    if(!canRange()) return;
    setSelected(s => { const n = new Set(s); n.add(cid); return n; });
    setAnchor(cid); setRangeMode(true); extending = false;
};

    • The held drag

      rule : the long-press need not end in a second tap: kept down and slid, it grows the run live, the tile under the finger becoming its far end.

      press_and_hold(page, t.nth(0))                    # held past the threshold → armed at the anchor
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(1)             # just the anchor so far
drag_onto(page, t.nth(n - 1))
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(n)             # the whole run roped in mid-drag…
expect(dialog(page)).to_have_count(0)             # …and no lightbox — this is a selection gesture
page.mouse.up()
print("  PASS: long-press drag extends live")

      how : the press starts a 500ms timer; held still past it, the press fires, capturing the pointer and arming the range. - how: a move of more than about 10px before it fires abandons it; a move after drives the drag.

      how : letting go of a drag that moved lands the run and disarms the range; a press that never moved leaves the range armed for a following tap.

      how : the press swallows its own trailing click, so a long-press opens nothing.

      const onTileDown = (e, photo) => {
    lpFired = false; lpMoved = false; lpAt = { x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY };
    lpEl = e.currentTarget; lpId = e.pointerId; lpCancel();
    lpTimer = setTimeout(() => { lpFired = true; lpCancel();
        try { lpEl.setPointerCapture(lpId); } catch(_){}
        armRange(photo.cid); }, 500);
};
const onTileMove = e => {
    if(lpFired){
        lpPos = { x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY };
        dragExtendAt(e.clientX, e.clientY);
        if(!lpRaf) dragTick();
        return;
    }
    if(lpAt && Math.hypot(e.clientX - lpAt.x, e.clientY - lpAt.y) > 10) lpCancel();
};
const dragStop = () => { if(lpRaf){ cancelAnimationFrame(lpRaf); lpRaf = 0; } lpPos = null; };
const onTileUp = () => { if(lpFired && lpMoved){ setRangeMode(false); extending = false; } dragStop(); lpCancel(); };
const onTilePress = (e, cid) => { if(lpFired){ lpFired = false; return; } onTileClick(e, cid); };
onMount(() => gridEl?.addEventListener('touchmove',
    e => { if(lpFired) e.preventDefault(); }, { passive: false }));

      rule : the run shrinks as the finger comes back toward the anchor, never stranding a tail. - scope: a tap only ever adds once, so the tap routes keep the one-shot extension.

      press_and_hold(page, t.nth(0))                    # armed at the anchor again
drag_onto(page, t.nth(n - 1))
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(n)             # grew to the whole run…
drag_onto(page, t.nth(n - 2))
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(n - 1)         # …then coming back drops the far tile
page.mouse.up()
print("  PASS: long-press drag shrinks on return")

      how : it runs on the same grow-or-shrink mechanism as the keyboard’s Shift-arrow run: the run is recomputed from the fixed anchor over the picks held when the drag began.

      const extendRun = cid => {
    if(!canRange()) return;
    const list = items();
    const a = list.findIndex(p => p.cid === anchor()), ni = list.findIndex(p => p.cid === cid);
    if(a < 0 || ni < 0) return;
    if(!extending){ extending = true; rangeBase = new Set(selected()); }
    const [lo, hi] = a < ni ? [a, ni] : [ni, a];
    setSelected(new Set([...rangeBase, ...list.slice(lo, hi + 1).map(p => p.cid)]));
};

      how : the far tile is the one found under the finger, through the wall’s own tile order, not the move’s own target. - what: once the press fires it captures the pointer, so every later move reports the pressed tile.

      const tileCidAt = (x, y) => {
    const tile = document.elementFromPoint(x, y)?.closest('.tile');
    if(!tile || !gridEl) return null;
    const i = [...gridEl.children].indexOf(tile);
    return i < 0 ? null : items()[i]?.cid;
};

    • The held drag under a real finger

      what : a drag over the wall competes with two things the browser would sooner do with it. - rule: on a desktop, a thumbnail must not peel off as a drag-and-drop ghost: the tiles’ images refuse to be dragged. - rule: on a touch screen, a moving finger must not pan the wall while a press is armed: the drag vetoes the scroll. - what: a mouse drag never sets off the touch scroll, so it slips past the veto untouched. - therefore: proving the touch side takes Chromium’s real touch pipeline.

      rule : under a real finger, a held drag from the anchor onto its neighbour picks both.

      a = t.nth(0).bounding_box(); end = t.nth(1).bounding_box()   # its neighbour, wherever the columns fall
x0, y0 = a["x"] + a["width"] / 2, a["y"] + a["height"] / 2
x1, y1 = end["x"] + end["width"] / 2, end["y"] + end["height"] / 2
cdp = page.context.new_cdp_session(page)
cdp.send("Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled", {"enabled": True, "maxTouchPoints": 1})
cdp.send("Input.dispatchTouchEvent", {"type": "touchStart", "touchPoints": [{"x": x0, "y": y0}]})
page.wait_for_timeout(LONG_PRESS_MS)                # hold past the long-press → arms range
for f in (0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0):                    # drag off the anchor onto the next tile
    cdp.send("Input.dispatchTouchEvent", {"type": "touchMove",
             "touchPoints": [{"x": x0 + (x1 - x0) * f, "y": y0 + (y1 - y0) * f}]})
cdp.send("Input.dispatchTouchEvent", {"type": "touchEnd", "touchPoints": []})
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(2)               # the run followed the finger, not one lonely anchor
print("  PASS: long-press drag (touch)")

      how : In practice the veto is a touchmove listener cancelling the scroll while the press is live; it must be non-passive, since a passive one — the framework’s default — may not cancel it.

      onMount(() => gridEl?.addEventListener('touchmove',
    e => { if(lpFired) e.preventDefault(); }, { passive: false }));

    • The held drag below the fold

      what : the wall may run on below the fold, past the last visible tile.

      rule : a held drag kept at the bottom edge picks the run down to the last tile of the wall.

      m = len(DRAG_DOCS)
last = t.nth(m - 1).bounding_box()
xl = last["x"] + last["width"] / 2                   # the last tile's column; its row is below the fold
cdp.send("Input.dispatchTouchEvent", {"type": "touchStart", "touchPoints": [{"x": x0, "y": y0}]})
page.wait_for_timeout(LONG_PRESS_MS)                 # arm range at the anchor
for f in (0.5, 1.0):                                 # drag to the bottom edge, in the last column, and hold
    cdp.send("Input.dispatchTouchEvent", {"type": "touchMove",
             "touchPoints": [{"x": x0 + (xl - x0) * f, "y": DRAG_VIEWPORT["height"] - 10}]})
wait_until(page, lambda: checks(page).count() == m,   # the wall scrolls the rest under the finger
           label="autoscroll ropes in the whole wall", detail=lambda: f"{checks(page).count()}/{m} selected")
cdp.send("Input.dispatchTouchEvent", {"type": "touchEnd", "touchPoints": []})
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(m)
print("  PASS: long-press drag auto-scrolls")

      how : a finger within about 48px of the bottom edge drags the wall up under itself, about 14px a frame, the run growing onto each row that rises into view; the top margin pulls the other way. - how: the margin is read against the floor lifted above the toolbar that the keyboard reveal measures, so the finger lands on a tile and not on the toolbar.

      let lpTimer = null, lpFired = false, lpAt = null, lpEl = null, lpId = null, lpMoved = false, lpPos = null, lpRaf = 0;
const lpCancel = () => { clearTimeout(lpTimer); lpTimer = null; };
const dragExtendAt = (x, y) => { const cid = tileCidAt(x, y); if(cid){ extendRun(cid); lpMoved = true; } };
const EDGE = 48, SCROLL_STEP = 14;
const dragTick = () => {
    lpRaf = 0;
    if(!lpFired || !lpPos) return;
    const bar = document.querySelector('.toolbar');
    const floor = innerHeight - (bar ? bar.getBoundingClientRect().height : 0);
    const dy = lpPos.y < EDGE ? -SCROLL_STEP : lpPos.y > floor - EDGE ? SCROLL_STEP : 0;
    if(!dy) return;                                    // finger left the margin → stop the loop
    scrollBy(0, dy);
    dragExtendAt(lpPos.x, Math.max(EDGE, Math.min(lpPos.y, floor - 1)));   // hit-test clear of the bar
    lpRaf = requestAnimationFrame(dragTick);
};

    • The first pick

      how : the tests here write to the archive, so they work on a few clearly marked docs — the sentinel label zzbatchfix, made-up addresses — inserted before each test and deleted at the end of the run. - therefore: searching the sentinel finds the suite’s three standing docs and nothing else, so every count is exact.

      how : the wall is measured across the first pick, while the toolbar is still absent.

      what : the first pick measures the toolbar arriving with nothing on the wall moving.

      t = tiles(page)
expect(toolbar(page)).to_be_hidden()       # nothing picked yet
before = t.first.bounding_box()
t.nth(0).click()                           # the first pick — the bar arrives on this one
expect(toolbar(page)).to_be_visible()
after = t.first.bounding_box()
assert abs(before["y"] - after["y"]) < 1, f"grid shifted: {before['y']} -> {after['y']}"
print("  PASS: select doesn't shift grid")

      how : the toolbar is fixed across the foot of the screen, overlaying the wall rather than taking room in it.

      /* a fixed bottom action bar, overlaying the wall */
.toolbar{ position:fixed; left:0; right:0; bottom:0; z-index:20; display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap;
          gap:6px; align-items:center; background:#11131f; border-top:1px solid #3a3f5a;
          padding: 8px calc(12px + env(safe-area-inset-right))
                   calc(8px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) calc(12px + env(safe-area-inset-left)); }

      rule : from there each tile toggles, and the toolbar keeps the count of what is picked.

      t.nth(1).click()                           # a second one joins it
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(2)
expect(toolbar(page).get_by_text("2 selected")).to_be_visible()
t.nth(0).click()                           # toggle one back off
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(1)
print("  PASS: select toggles tiles")

  • Words on the run

    rule : one add-label box serves both ＋ label and － label, and the two read it the same way.

    what : ＋ label merges the typed words into every picked doc, and the picks clear once it is applied.

    select_all(page).click()
tb.get_by_placeholder("add a label…").fill("addedbybatch")
tb.get_by_role("button", name="add label").click()
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(0)            # selection clears once applied
search_for(page, "addedbybatch")                # the fresh word now finds them all
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(n)
print("  PASS: batch add label")

    how : with the reach switch off, an edit takes the per-doc path: each picked doc is written in turn, then the picks clear and the wall re-reads its query. - how: it reads each doc’s labels from the wall, so a word can be merged into them. - how: a caller may leave some docs untouched, as moving onto an occasion leaves other owners'.

    what : labels are a ;-separated list, so one split reads a doc’s stored labels and what is typed into a box alike. - example: a; b adds two words in one go.

    async function patchSelected(patchFor){
    return editing(async tick => {
        const byCid = new Map(items().map(p => [p.cid, p]));
        for(const cid of selected()){
            const patch = patchFor(byCid.get(cid));
            if(patch){ await gql(UPDATE_PHOTO, { cid, patch }); tick(); }
        }
        clearSel();
        await refetch();
    });
}
const splitWords = s => (s || '').split(';').map(x => x.trim()).filter(Boolean);
const splitLabels = p => splitWords(p.labels);

    what : － label strips the typed words from every picked doc, which measures words coming off as readily as they go on. - how: the wall stands on the word being stripped, so once it is gone from all of them nothing is left to show.

    select_all(page).click()
tb.get_by_placeholder("add a label…").fill("addedbybatch")
tb.get_by_role("button", name="remove label").click()
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(0)
print("  PASS: batch remove label")

    how : adding and removing a word each take their path by the reach switch, as do the date stamp and moving onto an occasion, the move sent as a dated bulk edit pinned to the occasion’s owner. - what: adding a word also remembers the last word applied, for one-tap reuse on the next doc.

    const addLabel = async () => {
    const words = splitWords(labelText()); if(!words.length) return;
    setLastLabel(words[words.length - 1]);
    if(allMatching()){ for(const w of words) await applyBulk('AddLabel', w); }
    else await patchSelected(p => { const cur = splitLabels(p);
        for(const w of words) if(!cur.includes(w)) cur.push(w); return { labels: cur.join('; ') }; });
    setLabelText('');
};
const removeLabel = async () => {
    const words = splitWords(labelText()); if(!words.length) return;
    if(allMatching()){ for(const w of words) await applyBulk('RemoveLabel', w); }
    else await patchSelected(p => ({ labels: splitLabels(p).filter(x => !words.includes(x)).join('; ') }));
    setLabelText('');
};
const setStateFor = st => allMatching() ? applyBulk('SetState', st)
                                        : patchSelected(() => ({ state: st }));

  • Typing into the add-label box

    what : Enter in the add-label box stands in for ＋, which measures the button and the keyboard never drifting apart. - how: In practice the toolbar tears the box down when the picks clear and builds it again on the next select all, so the box reached for once the picks settle is a new one.

    search_for(page, FIXTURE_LABEL)                  # back to the run itself
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(n)
select_all(page).click()
box = toolbar(page).get_by_placeholder("add a label…")
box.click(); box.press_sequentially("zzbatchret")
expect(box).to_have_value("zzbatchret")          # the word is in the live box
box.press("Enter")                               # ＋ via RET
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(0)            # applied → selection clears
search_for(page, "zzbatchret")
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(n)             # every selected doc got it
print("  PASS: batch enter adds")

    what : Shift+Enter stands in for －.

    select_all(page).click()
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(n)            # selection settled
box.click(); box.press_sequentially("zzbatchret")
expect(box).to_have_value("zzbatchret")          # the word is in the live box
box.press("Shift+Enter")                         # － via S-RET
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(0)             # the docs no longer carry the label → gone from the wall
print("  PASS: batch shift-enter removes")

    what : picking a word from the box’s offers leaves a ; behind it, ready for the next word. - therefore: that trailing separator is the box’s usual state, not an edge case. - rule: removing reads the box the way adding does, and strips the word anyway.

    search_for(page, FIXTURE_LABEL)
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(n)
select_all(page).click()
tb.get_by_placeholder("add a label…").fill(FIXTURE_LABEL + "; ")   # as a picked suggestion leaves it
tb.get_by_role("button", name="remove label").click()
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(0)             # the trailing sep didn't defeat the match

    rule : one pick and the switch, and a state reaches every doc matched.

    search_for(page, FIXTURE_LABEL)

t.nth(0).click()                                              # just one, to raise the bar
tb.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile("all .* matching")).click()   # widen the scope

expect(grid(page).get_by_text("done")).to_have_count(n)       # all of them, off one tick

expect(grid(page).get_by_text("next")).to_have_count(2)  # the ticked ones move…
