what
the list is scoped to the stretch of time the query is already about, and it comes back eight rows at most.
  • what: a real year of somebody’s calendar holds more than eight occasions.
  • therefore: a window over a real year of somebody’s life fills all eight with their own occasions and leaves no room for the ones placed here.
  • therefore: every guess at an occasion below begins by naming the window.
how
three of the four have a doc taken during them, and the fourth deliberately has none.
  • how: one of the three is named in several words.
how
the last sits two years further out with a doc of its own.
  • therefore: what leaves it out of a list is the window and not the want of a doc.

EV_YEAR = datetime.date.today().year + 7       # far enough ahead that the calendar is empty there
EV_FAR = EV_YEAR + 2                           # and outside any window naming EV_YEAR
EV_WINDOW = f"since:{EV_YEAR}; until:{EV_YEAR}; "     # the stretch every guess below is about

EV_KERMESSE, EV_BROCANTE = "zzKermesse", "zzBrocante du Parc"
EV_PHOTOLESS, EV_ELSEWHERE = "zzSansPhoto", "zzHorsFenetre"

def _ev(row, summary, y, mo, has_photo=True):
    e = {"rowId": row, "summary": summary, "owner": "konubinix", "status": "confirmed",
         "starttime": f"{y}-{mo}-01T00:00:00Z", "endtime": f"{y}-{mo}-02T23:59:59Z"}
    p = has_photo and {"cid": f"/ipfs/{row}-p", "date": f"{y}-{mo}-01T12:00:00Z",
                       "thumbnailCid": f"/ipfs/{row}-p-t", "owner": "konubinix",
                       "mimetype": "image/jpeg", "labels": "zzevp", "state": "todo"}
    return e, p

OCCASIONS = [_ev("zzev-kerm", EV_KERMESSE, EV_YEAR, "06"),
             _ev("zzev-broc", EV_BROCANTE, EV_YEAR, "07"),
             _ev("zzev-none", EV_PHOTOLESS, EV_YEAR, "08", has_photo=False),
             _ev("zzev-far", EV_ELSEWHERE, EV_FAR, "06")]

def seed_occasions():
    seed_events([e for e, _ in OCCASIONS])
    for _, p in OCCASIONS:
        if p: gql(DELETE, {"cid": p["cid"]}); gql(CREATE, {"p": p})

def drop_occasions():
    drop_events([e for e, _ in OCCASIONS])
    for _, p in OCCASIONS:
        if p:
            try: gql(DELETE, {"cid": p["cid"]})
            except Exception: pass
Typing a guess
what
a guess that comes to nothing is rubbed out and another tried.
  • therefore: nearly every step below starts its guess over rather than adding to it.
  • how: the one that does not is the one asking whether the list survives a word being accepted.
    • what: that question only exists if you carry straight on from the word you accepted.
how
in practice, a guess begins by waiting for the box to be live.
  • what: while a committed search is still being answered, the controls that build the query are locked, the box among them.
  • what: a locked box still takes the letters but drops the arrows and the Enter that follow.
    • what: that reads afterwards as an offer that refused to go in for no reason at all.
  • how: nothing in this story commits a search, but whatever ran before it might have.
    • therefore: the wait belongs at the start of every guess rather than at the end of something else.

def type_into(page, fragment):
    """Start the term over and type it in, keystroke by keystroke as a hand would."""
    sb = search_box(page)
    expect(sb).to_be_enabled()
    sb.fill(""); sb.click()
    sb.press_sequentially(fragment, delay=20)

def guess(page, fragment):
    type_into(page, fragment)
    expect(options(page).first).to_be_visible()
Completing labels
what
as you type a label, the box offers rather than waits: it offers the labels already in use — the vocabulary.
what
the vocabulary and the query completing a fragment against it are not this app’s.
  • how: they live in the frise’s labels schema; this app only asks the shared LABEL_COMPLETIONS query the frise asks too.
  • rule: below two characters the list offers nothing.
    • how: with the vocabulary held unanswered, one character leaves no completing… row behind — nothing was even asked — while a second one brings it up.

sb.fill(""); sb.click(); sb.press_sequentially("a", delay=20)    # one character, the vocabulary still held
expect(page.get_by_text("completing")).to_have_count(0)          # nothing asked, so nothing pending
expect(options(page)).to_have_count(0)                           # and nothing offered
sb.press_sequentially("u", delay=20)                             # a second character: now it asks
expect(page.get_by_text("completing")).to_be_visible()
print("  PASS: one character offers nothing")
what
one dropdown of suggestions — the list — sits under the search box and under every add-label box, the same everywhere.
  • rule: it completes the fragment under the caret, not the whole field.
    • how: the search box splits on whitespace, its query being space-separated terms.
    • how: an add-label box completes the segment after the last ;, its content being a ;-separated list.
    • example: balade;aure offers aurelie, and a pick swaps just that segment.
  • rule: completion never proposes a label the doc already wears.
    • how: a box that edits a known doc hands the list the labels already on it, and the list drops them.
  • rule: the add-label boxes stay labels-only: a doc takes a label, not an occasion.
what
only one box has the focus at a time.
  • therefore: a single highlight, shared by all the boxes, suffices.
  • how: each box reports its current list to the app and reads the shared highlight back.
  • rule: in the lightbox — one doc opened large over the wall — and in the frame, ←=/=→ step the wall only when no field has focus: inside the add-label box the arrows belong to the text.

// keyboard-driving the suggestion list of the focused box
const [sugItems, setSugItems] = createSignal([]);
const [sugActive, setSugActive] = createSignal(-1);
const [sugLoading, setSugLoading] = createSignal(false);   // the focused box's list is fetching
const reportSug = list => { setSugItems(list); setSugActive(-1); };   // a new list clears the highlight
const sugNav = (e, commit) => {
    const n = sugItems().length;
    if(e.key === 'ArrowDown' && n){ e.preventDefault(); setSugActive(i => i >= n - 1 ? -1 : i + 1); }
    else if(e.key === 'ArrowUp' && n){ e.preventDefault(); setSugActive(i => i < 0 ? n - 1 : i - 1); }
    else if(e.key === 'Enter'){ e.preventDefault();
        commit(sugActive() >= 0 ? sugItems()[sugActive()] : null); setSugActive(-1); }
};
A pick finishes the term
what
a term is one piece of a box’s text, the pieces being separated by ;.
what
measures a word accepted ending with the separator for the next one: pick the first suggestion for a fragment of a known label, and the box holds exactly that word before it.

guess(page, "zzbal")                                     # a fragment of one word we know
word = options(page).first.inner_text().strip()
options(page).first.click()
expect(sb).to_have_value(word + "; ")                    # the picked label, then a ';' for the next
print("  PASS: label completion")
what
the search box also speaks a query language: a key such as since:, owner: or event:, then its value.
rule
the ; follows any pick that completes a term — a label, a full date, a type: or owner: value, an occasion — in the search box and the add-label boxes alike.
rule
a pick that still has somewhere to go keeps the box on that term, with no ;.
  • example: a bare key (since:, event:) about to take a value.
  • example: a partial date, to be drilled from year to month to day.
  • how: which it is is not wired term by term: the box asks the list whether the picked word still has a longer completion to offer.
  • example: owner offers the key, then its values, and owner:konubinix — a closed-vocab value with nothing longer — is done, and a ; opens the next term.

guess(page, "owner")                                        # 2+ chars → the key is offered
expect(options(page).filter(has_text="owner:").first).to_be_visible()
sb.press_sequentially(":k", delay=20)                       # owner:k → its values
opt = options(page).filter(has_text="konubinix").first
expect(opt).to_be_visible()
opt.click()
expect(sb).to_have_value("owner:konubinix; ")               # a closed-vocab value is done — a ';' opens the next token
print("  PASS: owner token completes")


const pickSearch = w => { const [s, e] = segSpan(search(), caret());
    const lead = (search().slice(s, e).match(/^\s*/) || [''])[0];
    // still drillable → hold the box on this token
    const drilling = w.endsWith(':') || dslSuggestions(w).some(v => v.length > w.length);
    const tail = drilling ? '' : '; ';
    const next = search().slice(0, s) + lead + w + tail + search().slice(e);
    setSearch(next); setCaret(s + lead.length + w.length + tail.length); setSearchFocus(true); };
what
a label may hold spaces, its distinctive word often the last.
  • rule: the fragment is matched against the whole label.
  • rule: a pick puts the whole label in the box, replacing what was typed rather than appended to it.
  • rule: it is one word as far as the box is concerned, and finishes like one.

guess(page, "parc des oise")                                # part of a label that has spaces
opt = options(page).filter(has_text="oiseaux").first
expect(opt).to_be_visible()
whole = opt.inner_text().strip()                            # the label as it is written down
opt.click()
expect(sb).to_have_value(whole + "; ")                      # all of it, and not twice over
print("  PASS: a label with spaces completes as one word")
what
measures that completion works on the term under the caret: put the caret back inside an earlier term, and that term is the one completed and replaced.

year = datetime.date.today().year
sb.fill(f"until:; since:{year}")                            # two date terms, the later one filled in
sb.click(); sb.press("Home")
for _ in range(len("until:")): sb.press("ArrowRight")       # back into the first, just past its colon
expect(options(page).get_by_text(f"until:{year}", exact=True)).to_be_visible()
expect(options(page).get_by_text(f"since:{year}", exact=True)).to_have_count(0)
print("  PASS: the list follows the caret, not the line")
how
the app asks that query for eight words at most, and does not ask at all for a shorter fragment.

const fetchCompletions = async word => {
    if((word || '').length < 2) return [];
    const d = await gql(LABEL_COMPLETIONS, { prefix: word, first: 8 });
    return d?.labelCompletions?.nodes ?? [];
};
const EVENT_COMPLETIONS = `query($prefix:String!,$since:Datetime,$until:Datetime,$first:Int){
  eventCompletions(prefix:$prefix, since:$since, until:$until, first:$first){ nodes } }`;
const fetchEventCompletions = async (prefix, since, until) => {
    const d = await gql(EVENT_COMPLETIONS, { prefix: prefix || '', since, until, first: 8 });
    return d?.eventCompletions?.nodes ?? [];
};
how
one function reads what the fragment under the caret is reaching for — a key, a key’s value, a date, an occasion or a label — and asks the vocabularies that can answer it.
  • how: the search box mixes at most five labels and three occasions.

async function suggestFor(text, caret, dsl, present){
    if(dsl && !(text || '').trim()) return DSL_KEYS;
    const word = segAt(text, caret);
    const ev = dsl && /^event:(.*)$/i.exec(word);
    if(ev){ const q = parseQuery(text);
        return (await fetchEventCompletions(ev[1], q.since, q.until)).map(s => 'event:' + s); }
    if(dsl){ const d = dslSuggestions(word); if(d.length) return d; }
    if(word.includes(':')) return [];
    const has = (present || []).map(s => s.toLowerCase());
    const drop = ws => has.length ? ws.filter(w => !has.includes(w.toLowerCase())) : ws;
    if(!dsl) return drop(await fetchCompletions(word));
    const q = parseQuery(text);
    const [labels, events] = await Promise.all([
        fetchCompletions(word),
        word.length >= 2 ? fetchEventCompletions(word, q.since, q.until) : Promise.resolve([]),
    ]);
    return [...drop(labels).slice(0, 5), ...events.map(s => 'event:' + s).slice(0, 3)];
}
how
the list offers words for the live text and hands the picked one back to the box it sits under.
  • how: it recomputes its offers whenever the text or caret moves, the caret defaulting to end-of-text so a box with no cursor of its own still completes its last segment.
  • how: Under the hood, the pick cancels the press that carried it, so pointing at the list never moves the focus off the box; the list closes because its segment is finished, not because anything was blurred.

function Suggest(props){
    const caret = () => props.caret == null ? (props.text || '').length : props.caret;
    const [items] = createResource(() => [props.text, caret(), props.present],
                                   ([t, c, p]) => suggestFor(t, c, props.dsl, p));
    createEffect(() => props.onItems?.(items() || []));
    createEffect(() => props.onLoading?.(items.loading));
    const active = () => props.active == null ? -1 : props.active;
    let listEl;
    createEffect(() => { const i = active();
        if(i >= 0 && listEl) listEl.querySelectorAll('[role=option]')[i]?.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' }); });
    return html`
      <${Show} when=${() => items.loading || (items() || []).length > 0}>
        <ul class="suggest" role="listbox" aria-label="suggestions" ref=${el => listEl = el} aria-busy=${() => items.loading ? 'true' : 'false'}>
          <${Show} when=${() => items.loading}>
            <li class="sug-loading" aria-disabled="true">completing…</li>
          <//>
          <${For} each=${() => items() || []}>${(w, i) => html`
            <li class=${() => 'sug' + (i() === active() ? ' active' : '')} role="option"
                aria-selected=${() => i() === active() ? 'true' : 'false'}
                onMouseDown=${e => { e.preventDefault(); props.onPick(w); }}>${w}</li>`}
          <//>
        </ul>
      <//>`;
}
The query language’s own words
rule
where a fragment could be a key or a label, the list does not offer both: a fragment that begins a key offers that key and nothing else, even when a label would have matched it too.
  • how: the vocabulary seeded for the check holds a label carrying the same fragment.

guess(page, "sin")                                          # begins "since:", and sits inside a label
expect(options(page)).to_have_text(["since:"])              # the key, alone
options(page).first.click()
expect(sb).to_have_value("since:")                          # a key still wants its value
print("  PASS: a key prefix offers the key and nothing else")
rule
a closed vocabulary small enough to show whole is shown whole, rather than waiting to be narrowed.
  • example: type: has two values, and offers both.

guess(page, "type:")
expect(options(page)).to_have_text(["type:image", "type:video"])
print("  PASS: a two-value token shows both")
rule
a date is tapped, not typed: an open since: offers the years, a chosen year its months, a chosen month its days — the date picker, which turns a range into a few taps.
  • rule: a part of a date has further to go, so picking it leaves the term open.
  • rule: a day has not, so picking it closes the term, and the list stands empty for whatever comes next.

year = datetime.date.today().year - 1                       # inside the span the picker offers
guess(page, "since:")
pick = lambda text: options(page).get_by_text(text, exact=True)
expect(pick(f"since:{year}")).to_be_visible()               # the years
pick(f"since:{year}").click()
expect(sb).to_have_value(f"since:{year}")                   # a year has further to go — still open
expect(pick(f"since:{year}-06")).to_be_visible()            # …and what it goes to is months
pick(f"since:{year}-06").click()
expect(pick(f"since:{year}-06-15")).to_be_visible()         # then days
pick(f"since:{year}-06-15").click()
expect(sb).to_have_value(f"since:{year}-06-15; ")           # a whole date is done, like any finished word
expect(options(page)).to_have_count(0)                      # and the list has nothing left to say
print("  PASS: a date is tapped, not typed")
rule
the date picker only drills a date that could be tapped — a month is one to twelve, a day one to that month’s last.
  • therefore: a figure naming none of them leaves it silent rather than inventive.
  • how: each impossible figure is typed after a possible one that differs from it by a digit: the same term, the same typing, the list filling for one and not the other.

for possible, impossible in [(f"since:{year}-1",     f"since:{year}-0"),      # no 0th month
                             (f"since:{year}-12",    f"since:{year}-13"),     # nor a 13th
                             (f"since:{year}-06-1",  f"since:{year}-06-0"),   # no 0th day
                             (f"since:{year}-06-30", f"since:{year}-06-31")]: # nor a 31st of June
    guess(page, possible)                                   # the list fills for the one that exists…
    type_into(page, impossible)
    expect(options(page)).to_have_count(0)                  # …and stays away for the one that doesn't
print("  PASS: the picker offers only dates that exist")
rule
date: is the same picker reached by a different word.

guess(page, "date")                                         # 2+ chars → the key is offered
expect(options(page).filter(has_text="date:").first).to_be_visible()
sb.press_sequentially(f":{year}", delay=20)
expect(options(page).get_by_text(f"date:{year}-06", exact=True)).to_be_visible()   # drilling, as before
print("  PASS: date: drills the same picker")
what
the rolling bounds are named: lastweek, lastmonth, lastyear.
  • rule: the part they share is enough to bring all three up.
  • rule: one of them is a whole bound on its own, with nothing further to drill into, so picking it closes the term like any other finished value.

guess(page, "since:last")                                   # a bound can be a word rather than a date
expect(options(page)).to_have_text(["since:lastweek", "since:lastmonth", "since:lastyear"])
options(page).last.click()
expect(sb).to_have_value("since:lastyear; ")                # a whole bound in one word — done
print("  PASS: a rolling bound completes from its prefix")
Occasions in the box
what
the occasions are a vocabulary like the labels, except that nobody typed them here: they are the calendar’s, written by whoever set the meeting up.
  • rule: inside event:, a fragment offers the occasions’ names, and picking one puts it in the calendar’s spelling and closes the term.

guess(page, EV_WINDOW + "event:zzkerm")                     # a prefix of an occasion's name
opt = options(page).filter(has_text=EV_KERMESSE).first
expect(opt).to_be_visible()
opt.click()
expect(sb).to_have_value(EV_WINDOW + f"event:{EV_KERMESSE}; ")   # the calendar's spelling, and done
print("  PASS: an occasion completes from the calendar")
rule
the pieces of a fragment are matched separately and anywhere in an occasion’s name, rather than as one run from its start — in either order.
  • how: the app sends the segment as typed, and would look the same however the words were matched at the other end.
  • therefore: this behaviour is the occasion query’s to keep or lose.

for pieces in ("brocante parc", "parc brocante"):           # either order finds it
    guess(page, EV_WINDOW + f"event:{pieces}")
    expect(options(page).filter(has_text=EV_BROCANTE).first).to_be_visible()
print("  PASS: an occasion's name matches in pieces, any order")
rule
a bare word is put to the calendar as well as to the labels, and an occasion it matches comes back already wearing event:.
  • therefore: you never have to know the key exists to use it.

guess(page, EV_WINDOW + "zzkerm")                           # no token typed, and none needed
opt = options(page).filter(has_text=f"event:{EV_KERMESSE}").first
expect(opt).to_be_visible()
opt.click()
expect(sb).to_have_value(EV_WINDOW + f"event:{EV_KERMESSE}; ")   # handed back as the token
print("  PASS: a bare word offers an occasion as a token")
what
the calendar is far larger than the archive, and mostly about afternoons no camera came to.
what
measures an occasion offered only if picking it would show a doc.
  • rule: what is offered is held to the window too — the stretch of time the query already names.

guess(page, EV_WINDOW + "event:zz")
expect(options(page).filter(has_text=EV_KERMESSE).first).to_be_visible()
expect(options(page).filter(has_text=EV_ELSEWHERE)).to_have_count(0)    # has a doc; wrong window
expect(options(page).filter(has_text=EV_PHOTOLESS)).to_have_count(0)    # right window; no doc
print("  PASS: only occasions worth picking are offered")
how
the occasions come from a query of their own, eight at most, and handed the window.

const EVENT_COMPLETIONS = `query($prefix:String!,$since:Datetime,$until:Datetime,$first:Int){
  eventCompletions(prefix:$prefix, since:$since, until:$until, first:$first){ nodes } }`;
const fetchEventCompletions = async (prefix, since, until) => {
    const d = await gql(EVENT_COMPLETIONS, { prefix: prefix || '', since, until, first: 8 });
    return d?.eventCompletions?.nodes ?? [];
};
rule
with nothing typed after event:, the list is the whole of what the window holds — a way of browsing the occasions, not only of matching one.

guess(page, EV_WINDOW + "event:")                           # the bare key, nothing typed
expect(options(page).filter(has_text=EV_KERMESSE).first).to_be_visible()
expect(options(page).filter(has_text=EV_BROCANTE).first).to_be_visible()
print("  PASS: the bare key lists the window's occasions")
Driving the list from the keys
what
measures the whole of it working without the hand leaving the keys: ↑=/=↓ move a highlight, and Enter applies the highlighted word.
  • rule: Enter with nothing highlighted runs the box’s own action instead.
    • example: in an add-label box it adds the typed labels and Shift+Enter removes them — the keyboard twins of the ＋ / － buttons.
    • example: in the search box it just leaves the live query be.
  • rule: Enter takes the word the highlight is on, which is only the first word when you stopped there: walking past the first and pressing it brings back the second.

guess(page, "zzup")
offered = [t.strip() for t in options(page).all_inner_texts()]
assert len(offered) == 2, f"this needs two to choose between, got {offered}"
sb.press("ArrowDown"); sb.press("ArrowDown")             # past the first, onto the second
sb.press("Enter")                                        # apply the highlighted one
expect(sb).to_have_value(offered[1] + "; ")              # the second
print("  PASS: search suggestion keyboard")
rule
↑ reaches the list from the other end: with nothing highlighted it enters at the bottom, on the last suggestion.

guess(page, "zzup")                              # two words
items = [t.strip() for t in options(page).all_inner_texts()]
assert items == ["zzupa", "zzupb"], f"unexpected suggestions: {items}"
sb.press("ArrowUp")                              # from nothing selected — must enter at the bottom
wait_until(page, lambda: page.evaluate(HIGHLIGHTED) == "zzupb",
           label="ArrowUp from none highlights the last suggestion",
           detail=lambda: f"offered {options(page).all_inner_texts()}, "
                          f"highlighted {page.evaluate(HIGHLIGHTED)!r}, box {sb.input_value()!r}")
print("  PASS: suggestion up enters from none")
how
In practice the highlight is read out of the page in one go: a completion answering for letters typed a moment ago re-renders the list, so a row asked first for its count and then for its text can be gone.
  • how: the wait carries what it wanted and what it found.

HIGHLIGHTED = """() => { const o = document.querySelector(
    '[role=listbox][aria-label=suggestions] [role=option][aria-selected=true]');
    return o ? o.textContent.trim() : null; }"""
what
measures the highlighted offer staying in view however long the list runs.

sb.fill(""); sb.click()                           # empty box → all the DSL keys, taller than the popover
listbox = page.get_by_role("listbox", name="suggestions")
expect(listbox).to_be_visible()
assert listbox.evaluate("el => el.scrollHeight > el.clientHeight + 4"), \
    "the menu must overflow the popover for scrolling to matter"
for _ in range(options(page).count()): sb.press("ArrowDown")   # walk down to the last key
active = page.get_by_role("option", selected=True)
expect(active).to_have_count(1)
assert active.evaluate("""el => { const b = el.getBoundingClientRect(),
    l = el.closest('[role=listbox]').getBoundingClientRect();
    return b.top >= l.top - 1 && b.bottom <= l.bottom + 1; }"""), \
    "the highlighted option is not within the visible completion area"
print("  PASS: completion keeps highlight in view")
how
the list watches the highlight and scrolls the row it lands on the least distance into view.

let listEl;
createEffect(() => { const i = active();
    if(i >= 0 && listEl) listEl.querySelectorAll('[role=option]')[i]?.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' }); });
rule
a pick never costs the box its focus: it leaves the box on a fresh, empty segment, the caret where you were typing and the list blank, without asking you to click out and back in.
what
measures the list of offers coming back the moment you carry on.
  • how: In practice the check types at the page rather than at the box: aimed at the box, a keystroke would focus it on the way in; typed at the page, the keys go wherever focus is, and nowhere if the pick took it.

page.keyboard.type("zzalo", delay=20)                    # straight on, into whatever holds the keys
expect(options(page).filter(has_text="zzalois").first).to_be_visible()   # must reappear
print("  PASS: completion reopens after pick")
What a fragment matches
what
measures a fragment sitting in the middle of the word: a mid-word smo surfaces cosmo.
  • how: the app hands the fragment over whole, and the vocabulary query is what says a match may begin anywhere.
  • therefore: this promise is the archive’s: no change to the code here can take it away, and the way to break it is to narrow that query, which lives in another note.

guess(page, "osmo")                              # sits inside zzcosmo, nowhere near its start
expect(options(page).filter(has_text="zzcosmo").first).to_be_visible()
print("  PASS: completion matches inside label")
what
measures a fragment coming without the capital or the accent: the match folds both, while the list offers the label exactly as written.
  • example: a bare zzelod surfaces Zzélodie, its capital and accent kept.

guess(page, "zzelod")                            # no capital, no accent
texts = [t.strip() for t in options(page).all_inner_texts()]
assert "Zzélodie" in texts, f"expected the label as written, got {texts}"
options(page).filter(has_text="Zzélodie").first.click()
expect(sb).to_have_value("Zzélodie; ")
print("  PASS: completion preserves case and accent")
The list on screen

  • While the archive thinks

    what : the vocabulary sits behind a GraphQL round-trip, a noticeable beat on a cold box.

    what : measures the list saying so while offers are on their way: it opens while the query is still in flight, not only once it has results, and shows a pulsing completing… row.

    hold_completions(page)                            # the vocabulary query, left unanswered
sb.fill(""); sb.click(); sb.press_sequentially("au", delay=20)
expect(page.get_by_text("completing")).to_be_visible()
print("  PASS: completion shows in-flight hint")

    how : the list draws that row whenever the vocabulary has yet to answer, beside any words it already holds.

    <${Show} when=${() => items.loading}>
  <li class="sug-loading" aria-disabled="true">completing…</li>
<//>

    rule : the words replace that row the moment they arrive. - rule: on a refine, the previous segment’s list stays underneath, so the panel never blanks while it catches up.

    rule : a list that is only thinking is up, and the box says so while it thinks: the one place reporting whether the list is showing never announces collapsed over a list plainly on screen. - rule: a screen reader is told what a sighted reader sees. - how: the completing… row is still on screen from just above, the query unanswered for good.

    expect(sb).to_have_attribute("aria-expanded", "true")
print("  PASS: search expanded while loading")

  • Finding the language

    rule : the year: key completes like the others: typing it offers the key, then its years.

    guess(page, "year")                                         # 2+ chars → the key is offered
expect(options(page).filter(has_text="year:").first).to_be_visible()
sb.press_sequentially(":202", delay=20)                     # year:202 → its year values
expect(options(page).filter(has_text=re.compile(r"year:202\d")).first).to_be_visible()
print("  PASS: year token completes")

    rule : the query language can be found from the box itself: the empty search box, the moment it takes focus, drops down the whole menu of keys — every prefix at once.

    sb.fill(""); sb.click()                               # empty box, just focused — no typing
expect(options(page)).to_have_count(14)               # the whole menu, at once
got = sorted(x.strip() for x in options(page).all_inner_texts())
assert got == sorted(["since:", "until:", "type:", "sort:", "owner:", "month:", "day:",
                      "year:", "date:", "event:", "first:", "last:", "sample:",
                      "onthisday"]), got              # every prefix present (order-free)
print("  PASS: empty box suggests all prefixes")

  • Open and closed, said aloud

    what : the box and its list form a combobox: the box says so, and its aria-expanded reads true whenever the list is up.

    rule : closing is a state flip, not a timed fade: blur the box and the list is gone at once. - therefore: anything watching can wait on the state rather than on a clock.

    expect(sb).to_have_attribute("role", "combobox")          # the box says what it is…
sb.fill(""); sb.click(); sb.press_sequentially(HALF_KNOWN[0][:4])
expect(sb).to_have_attribute("aria-expanded", "true")     # …and open popover → state true
sb.blur()
expect(sb).to_have_attribute("aria-expanded", "false")    # closed → state false (what search_for waits on)
assert page.get_by_role("listbox", name="suggestions").count() == 0, "popover must be gone the instant the state flips"
print("  PASS: search completion state, no timing")

    rule : reporting itself open while it thinks is not the search box’s own arrangement: the three add-label boxes — the lightbox’s, the frame’s and the toolbar’s — each do it on a query that has not answered. - how: each is caught on its first word: after one list has arrived, it stays put while the next is fetched.

    example : the lightbox’s, where somebody is labelling a doc, the vocabulary held quiet under the first thing they type.

    hold_completions(page)                       # the vocabulary, left unanswered
expanded_while_loading(page, box)
print("  PASS: lightbox label expanded while loading")

    example : the frame’s, on the tablet, where the bar has just been woken by a passer-by.

    hold_completions(page)
expanded_while_loading(page, bar.get_by_placeholder("add a label…"))
print("  PASS: frame label expanded while loading")

    example : the toolbar’s, where somebody is labelling a run.

    select_all(page).click()
hold_completions(page)
expanded_while_loading(page, tb.get_by_placeholder("add a label…"))
print("  PASS: batch label expanded while loading")
Back, while the list is open

  • Back asks before leaving

    what : the stack Back unwinds bottoms out at the wall; one more Back would leave the app entirely — easy to do by accident on the cabinet tablet.

    how : a root history entry sits under the wall.

    what : measures going back asking before it leaves the app: confirm and the app is left, cancel and the root is re-pushed so the wall stays put.

    page.go_back()
wait_until(page, lambda: len(asked) == 1, label="going back with nothing up asks first")
expect(grid(page)).to_be_visible()                                    # cancelling kept us in the app
print("  PASS: back at grid asks before exit")

    what : the completion list under the search box is the one thing that can be showing without being a stacked overlay — yet the same reflex applies. - what: retracting the last thing that appeared is what the button is for.

    what : measures going back closing the open list first: only a Back with nothing showing reaches the leave prompt.

    page.go_back()                                 # Back retracts the list — it must not leave the app
expect(options(page)).to_have_count(0)         # the list is gone
expect(sb).to_be_visible()                     # and we're still in Memories
assert len(asked) == 1, f"retracting the list should have asked nothing: {asked}"
print("  PASS: back closes completion")

    rule : retracting the list does not spend the root guard itself: a further Back, now with nothing showing, still meets that prompt.

    page.go_back()                                 # a further Back: must reach the leave guard
wait_until(page, lambda: len(asked) == 2, label="the guard was still there to meet")
expect(sb).to_be_visible()                     # cancelled → still in the app
print("  PASS: back after completion still guards exit")

  • The guard lets go when told

    how : that reading comes last of all, because there is nothing on the other side of it.

    what : measures going back leaving when told to: say yes and the app lets go, back to whatever the tab held before it.

    leaving.append(True)                           # this time the prompt is answered yes
page.go_back()
wait_until(page, lambda: heading(page).count() == 0,
           label="the app let go of the tab",
           detail=lambda: f"still showing {page.url}")
print("  PASS: back confirmed leaves")

    how : In practice the guard reads whether the list is up straight from the page — the rendered list being there — rather than from a state flag. - what: a flag holding the last-offered words keeps its value after the box blurs and the list unmounts, and so would claim a list that is already gone.

    onMount(() => {
    history.pushState({ app: true }, '');          // the root entry the back button stops on
    const onExit = () => {
        const st = history.state || {};
        if(!frame() && !opened() && !st.lb && !st.app){      // popped below the root with nothing open
            if(photos.loading){ cancelRead(); history.pushState({ app: true }, ''); return; }   // bail out of a frozen read; stay
            if(document.querySelector('.suggest')){ setSearchFocus(false); history.pushState({ app: true }, ''); return; }   // retract the list; keep the root beneath
            if(confirm('Leave Memories?')) history.back();   // really leave
            else history.pushState({ app: true }, '');       // stay — restore the root
        }
    };
    window.addEventListener('popstate', onExit);
    onCleanup(() => window.removeEventListener('popstate', onExit));
});
The whole story
how
the story walked end to end — the word in the middle, the spelling, the keys, the dates, the occasions.

@testcase
def test_letting_the_box_do_the_typing(page):
    """Building a query out of what the box knows better than the hand: a word remembered

    nobody wants to spell, and the name of an occasion nobody here chose — with the list
    staying alongside throughout, reachable by the keys however long it runs, and saying so
    even while it is still thinking — and then backing out of it all, one rung at a time,
    the last rung asking before it lets go, and letting go when it is told to."""
    seed_vocab(HALF_KNOWN)
    seed_occasions()
    try:

Working the wall without the mouse

what
a card-dump gets worked in one sitting with both hands on the keys.
  • example: walk the wall, open one to be sure, pick it or leave it, sweep a run of them together, walk back over what you passed, take the lot.
  • what: a sitting is several passes, and the search box is where each one begins.
    • therefore: after the lot, you narrow the run again and start over.
what
the mouse already has this set of gestures.
  • rule: the two have to agree rather than merely coexist.
    • rule: the cursor — the tile the keys are on — that a click leaves behind is the cursor the next arrow moves.
rule
the cursor moves as the wall shows it.
  • rule: a row is however many columns are on show.
  • rule: wherever the cursor lands, its tile is whole and in view.
  • rule: coming back from the lightbox — one doc opened large over the wall — or from the show, the cursor is on the doc you left, and the wall scrolls to it.
  • rule: the run picked and the cursor survive a reload of the tab.
rule
the keys go where you are.
  • rule: while the lightbox is open, it owns the keys.
  • rule: while you type in the search box, the wall’s cursor stands aside.
  • rule: one key reaches the add-label box and another reuses the last word, on a picked run as in the lightbox.
how
the story wants a wall too big for the window — enough docs for several rows, on a screen short enough that the last of them sits below the fold and behind the toolbar that picking brings up.

KEY_N = 24

def key_docs():
    return [{"cid": f"https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzkey-{i}", "date": f"2021-01-{i + 1:02d}T12:00:00Z",
             "mimetype": "image/jpeg", "thumbnailCid": f"https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzkey-t-{i}",
             "labels": "zzkey", "state": "todo"} for i in range(KEY_N)]

def key_thumb(i):
    return f"https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zzkey-t-{i}"

FIRST_WORD, SECOND_WORD = "zzkeyfirst", "zzkeysecond"
how
the last of the story leaves the wall for the two surfaces that work one doc or clip at a time — the lightbox and the show — and comes back to it each time.
  • how: before each trip, it puts the wall back where it started, with the last tile out of sight again.
what
a slide arrives under the eye before the show has decided it has arrived.
  • how: the picture is centred while the step is still settling, and only the settling hands the slide on to anything outside the strip — the show’s row of slides.
  • therefore: leaving the show is the other thing that has to be timed.
  • what: the show calls a step over 150ms after the last scroll.
    • therefore: a quarter of a second of stillness is past it.
    • how: stillness is read from the strip’s own scroll position, held rather than merely sampled.

def back_to_the_top(page):
    """Send the wall back to the top, and wait until its far tile is out of sight again."""
    page.evaluate("() => scrollTo(0, 0)")
    wait_until(page, lambda: not tiles(page).nth(KEY_N - 1).evaluate(IN_VIEW),
               label="the far tile is below the fold, so a scroll to it would show")

STILL_MS = 250                                 # past the show's own settle, whoever is watching

def show_at_rest(page, strip):
    """Wait until the strip has held one position for longer than the show's settle."""
    held = [None, 0.0]                         # where it is, and when it first got there
    def resting():
        at, now = strip.evaluate("el => Math.round(el.scrollLeft)"), time.time()
        if at != held[0]: held[0], held[1] = at, now
        return (now - held[1]) * 1000 >= STILL_MS
    wait_until(page, resting,
               label="the show came to rest on the slide it stepped to",
               detail=lambda: f"it was last at {held[0]}")


@testcase
def test_working_the_wall_without_the_mouse(page):
    """A pass over a card-dump from the keys: walk the wall, open one, pick one, drag a
    run to the foot of it, climb back out, take the lot, reach a label box and the last
    word twice over, turn back to the search box, carry the cursor out to the lightbox
    and the show and back with the wall following it both ways — and lose the tab on all
    of it, to find the run and the cursor where you left them."""
    docs = key_docs()
    for d in docs: gql(DELETE, {"cid": d["cid"]}); gql(CREATE, {"p": d})
    try:
        page.set_viewport_size({"width": 420, "height": 600})   # narrow and short: it overflows
        open_app(page)
        search_for(page, "zzkey")
        expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(KEY_N)
        d = dialog(page)
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")               # the first arrow focuses the first tile
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")               # → the second
        page.keyboard.press("Enter")                    # Enter opens the focused doc
        expect(d.get_by_role("img")).to_have_attribute("src", key_thumb(1))
        page.keyboard.press("Escape")
        expect(d).to_be_hidden()
        print("  PASS: grid cursor opens focused doc")
        expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(0)           # nothing picked by walking about
        page.keyboard.press(" ")                        # Space picks the focused one
        expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(1)
        page.keyboard.press(" ")                        # Space again unpicks it
        expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(0)
        print("  PASS: grid cursor space toggles selection")
        tiles(page).nth(5).click()                       # reach for the mouse for one tile
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")               # the arrows carry on from there
        page.keyboard.press("Enter")                     # open the now-focused tile
        expect(dialog(page).get_by_role("img")).to_have_attribute("src", key_thumb(6))
        page.keyboard.press("Escape")
        toolbar(page).get_by_role("button", name="clear").click()   # drop what the click picked up
        expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(0)
        print("  PASS: cursor starts at last clicked tile")
        page.keyboard.press(" ")                        # one picked already, before any run
        expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(1)
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")               # a plain move re-anchors where it lands
        expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(1)           # and selects nothing of its own
        page.keyboard.press("Shift+ArrowRight")         # reach on…
        page.keyboard.press("Shift+ArrowRight")         # …and on again
        expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(4)           # the run from the anchor, over the one kept
        print("  PASS: grid cursor shift extends selection")
        page.keyboard.press("Shift+ArrowLeft")          # back one → the far end drops off
        expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(3)
        page.keyboard.press("Shift+ArrowLeft")          # back onto the anchor → the run is just it
        expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(2)           # and the one kept underneath is still there
        toolbar(page).get_by_role("button", name="clear").click()
        expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(0)
        print("  PASS: grid cursor shift reduces on return")
        tiles(page).nth(0).click()                      # plant the cursor at the top-left
        toolbar(page).get_by_role("button", name="clear").click()

Driving the wall from the keyboard
what
the wall has a cursor — a focused tile the eye can follow, moved with the arrow keys, the way every file manager gives one.
Walking and opening
rule
the arrows walk the cursor across the wall — left and right by one tile, down and up by a whole row.
  • rule: the first arrow puts the cursor on the wall’s first tile.
rule
Enter opens the cursor’s doc in the lightbox, and Escape leaves it, as it already does.

page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")               # the first arrow focuses the first tile
page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")               # → the second
page.keyboard.press("Enter")                    # Enter opens the focused doc
expect(d.get_by_role("img")).to_have_attribute("src", key_thumb(1))
page.keyboard.press("Escape")
expect(d).to_be_hidden()
print("  PASS: grid cursor opens focused doc")
rule
walking the cursor about picks nothing.
rule
Space picks or unpicks the cursor’s tile — the keyboard twin of a click.

expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(0)           # nothing picked by walking about
page.keyboard.press(" ")                        # Space picks the focused one
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(1)
page.keyboard.press(" ")                        # Space again unpicks it
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(0)
print("  PASS: grid cursor space toggles selection")
what
measures the cursor a click leaves is the one the next arrow moves — the arrows carry on from the clicked tile rather than snapping back to the wall’s first.

tiles(page).nth(5).click()                       # reach for the mouse for one tile
page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")               # the arrows carry on from there
page.keyboard.press("Enter")                     # open the now-focused tile
expect(dialog(page).get_by_role("img")).to_have_attribute("src", key_thumb(6))
page.keyboard.press("Escape")
toolbar(page).get_by_role("button", name="clear").click()   # drop what the click picked up
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(0)
print("  PASS: cursor starts at last clicked tile")
A run under Shift
what
the anchor is the tile a run reaches from.
  • rule: a plain move drops the anchor where it lands, and picks nothing of its own.
rule
arrowing with Shift held picks the contiguous run from the anchor to the cursor.
  • therefore: arrowing away grows it.
  • example: a folder’s Shift-selection, built without the mouse.
rule
what was picked before the run stays picked underneath it.

page.keyboard.press(" ")                        # one picked already, before any run
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(1)
page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")               # a plain move re-anchors where it lands
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(1)           # and selects nothing of its own
page.keyboard.press("Shift+ArrowRight")         # reach on…
page.keyboard.press("Shift+ArrowRight")         # …and on again
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(4)           # the run from the anchor, over the one kept
print("  PASS: grid cursor shift extends selection")
rule
arrowing back toward the anchor shrinks the run — it follows the cursor in both directions, never leaving a stranded tail.

page.keyboard.press("Shift+ArrowLeft")          # back one → the far end drops off
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(3)
page.keyboard.press("Shift+ArrowLeft")          # back onto the anchor → the run is just it
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(2)           # and the one kept underneath is still there
toolbar(page).get_by_role("button", name="clear").click()
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(0)
print("  PASS: grid cursor shift reduces on return")
how
the run is not accumulated as it goes: every step recomputes it from the anchor, over a snapshot of what was picked before the run began.
  • therefore: a reversal and the earlier picks both come out right without being tracked.

const CURSOR_KEY = 'memories.cursor';
const [cursor, setCursor] = createSignal(localStorage.getItem(CURSOR_KEY));
createEffect(() => { const c = cursor(); c ? localStorage.setItem(CURSOR_KEY, c) : localStorage.removeItem(CURSOR_KEY); });
let gridEl, rangeBase = new Set(), extending = false;
const gridCols = () => gridEl ? getComputedStyle(gridEl).gridTemplateColumns.split(' ').length : 1;
const moveCursor = (delta, extend) => {
    const list = items(); if(!list.length) return;
    const at = list.findIndex(p => p.cid === cursor());
    const ni = at < 0 ? 0 : Math.max(0, Math.min(list.length - 1, at + delta));
    setCursor(list[ni].cid);
    if(extend && anchor() !== null){ extendRun(list[ni].cid); }   // grow-or-shrink the run to the cursor
    else { extending = false; setAnchor(list[ni].cid); }   // a plain move re-anchors and ends the run
    requestAnimationFrame(scrollCursorIntoView);
};
A row at a time
what
the wall is responsive, the number of its columns following its size.
what
measures a row is however many columns are on show, at whatever size the wall is drawn.

tiles(page).nth(0).click()                      # plant the cursor at the top-left
toolbar(page).get_by_role("button", name="clear").click()
cols = grid(page).evaluate("el => getComputedStyle(el).gridTemplateColumns.split(' ').length")
page.keyboard.press("ArrowDown"); page.keyboard.press("ArrowDown")   # two rows down
page.keyboard.press("Enter")
expect(dialog(page).get_by_role("img")).to_have_attribute("src", key_thumb(2 * cols))
page.keyboard.press("Escape")
page.keyboard.press("ArrowUp")                  # back up by a row
page.keyboard.press("Enter")
expect(dialog(page).get_by_role("img")).to_have_attribute("src", key_thumb(cols))
page.keyboard.press("Escape")
print("  PASS: grid cursor steps a row, both ways")
Keeping the cursor’s tile in view
what
the toolbar is pinned over the foot of the wall and floats above it.
  • what: that pin makes two separate troubles, and a run driving the cursor down — toolbar up, cursor heading for the bottom — walks straight into both.
what
measures wherever the cursor lands, its tile is whole and in view — more than nudged past the edge.
  • rule: a run dragged to the foot of a tall wall still leaves its last tile whole, and above the toolbar.

tiles(page).nth(0).click()                               # start the run at the top-left
for _ in range(KEY_N): page.keyboard.press("Shift+ArrowDown")   # drag it down past the fold
last = tiles(page).nth(KEY_N - 1).bounding_box()
bar = toolbar(page).bounding_box()                       # the run raised the toolbar
assert last["y"] + last["height"] <= bar["y"] + 1, f"tile foot behind the toolbar: {last} vs {bar}"
toolbar(page).get_by_role("button", name="clear").click()
print("  PASS: grid cursor reveals tile above toolbar")
what
the first trouble is position: a tile scrolled flush to the bottom sits half-hidden behind the toolbar.
  • how: the cursor’s tile is measured against a window whose bottom is lifted by the toolbar’s own height — zero until something is picked.
  • how: the wall scrolls only as far as it takes to clear whichever edge the tile overruns.

const scrollCursorIntoView = () => {
    const tile = gridEl?.querySelector('[data-cursor="1"]'); if(!tile) return;
    const r = tile.getBoundingClientRect();
    const bar = document.querySelector('.toolbar');
    const floor = innerHeight - (bar ? bar.getBoundingClientRect().height : 0);
    if(r.top < 0) scrollBy(0, r.top);                          // head above the fold → pull it down
    else if(r.bottom > floor) scrollBy(0, r.bottom - floor);   // foot under the bar → push it up
};
what
the second trouble is room: the page ends where the last row does.
  • therefore: the bottom tiles have nowhere to scroll to, and no nudge lifts them past a toolbar the page is too short to outrun.
  • how: while something picked holds the toolbar up, a margin as tall as the toolbar is reserved beneath the wall, for those rows to rise into.
  • what: the toolbar’s wrapped height is not known until it has laid out.
    • therefore: the margin is measured on the paint after the toolbar appears.

createEffect(() => {
    const shown = selCount() > 0;   // tracked synchronously; the toolbar mounts on this turn
    requestAnimationFrame(() => {
        const bar = shown && document.querySelector('.toolbar');
        document.body.style.paddingBottom = bar ? bar.getBoundingClientRect().height + 'px' : '';
    });
});
rule
clearing the edge cuts both ways: a wall walked to its foot is walkable back to its head, the cursor’s tile in view as it climbs.

for _ in range(KEY_N): page.keyboard.press("ArrowUp")    # climb back out, plain moves
wait_until(page, lambda: tiles(page).nth(0).bounding_box()["y"] >= 0,
           label="the cursor climbed above the fold and stayed there",
           detail=lambda: f"tile 0 at {tiles(page).nth(0).bounding_box()}; " + str(page.evaluate(
               "() => ({ scrollY, padding: document.body.style.paddingBottom,"
               " focused: document.activeElement?.getAttribute('aria-label') })")))
print("  PASS: grid cursor reveals a tile climbed back to")
Who has the keys
what
measures an open lightbox owns the keys — arrows and all, the same arrows meaning something there.
  • rule: the wall never gathers a run behind a doc you are only looking at.

open_doc(page, 0)
page.keyboard.press("Shift+ArrowRight")         # a wall gesture, aimed at the open doc
page.keyboard.press("Escape")
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(0)           # nothing was gathered behind it
print("  PASS: an open doc owns the keys")
rule
when the whole wall is wanted rather than a run of it, Ctrl+A (⌘A on a Mac) picks it in one — the keyboard twin of the select-all toggle.

page.keyboard.press("Control+a")
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(KEY_N)       # the whole wall at once
print("  PASS: ctrl+a selects whole wall")
what
measures the cursor stands aside while you type in the search box.
  • rule: every wall key goes quiet the moment a field takes the keys — the arrows, and Ctrl+A with them, which in a text box means the text.

on = lambda: grid(page).locator("[data-cursor='1'] img").get_attribute("src")
was = on()
search_box(page).click()                        # the box takes the keys
page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")
page.keyboard.press("ArrowDown")
assert on() == was, f"the wall cursor moved while the search box had focus: {was} → {on()}"
print("  PASS: grid cursor stands aside for a field")
what
the wall has no focus of its own to hear the keys from.
  • therefore: the keys are heard at the window rather than on any tile.
  • therefore: standing aside is done by hand, surface by surface, rather than falling out of where the focus is.
what
The frame is the third of those surfaces, owning the keys the same way for as long as it is up.

onMount(() => {
    const onKey = e => {
        if(opened() || frame() || /^(INPUT|TEXTAREA)$/.test(e.target.tagName)) return;
        const step = d => { e.preventDefault(); moveCursor(d, e.shiftKey); };
        if(e.key === 'ArrowRight') step(1);
        else if(e.key === 'ArrowLeft') step(-1);
        else if(e.key === 'ArrowDown') step(gridCols());
        else if(e.key === 'ArrowUp') step(-gridCols());
        else if(e.key === ' ' && cursor()){ e.preventDefault(); toggle(cursor()); setAnchor(cursor()); }
        else if(e.key === 'Enter' && cursor()){ e.preventDefault(); openPhoto(items().find(p => p.cid === cursor())); }
        else if((e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) && (e.key === 'a' || e.key === 'A')){ e.preventDefault(); setSelected(new Set(shownCids())); }
    };
    window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey);
    onCleanup(() => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey));
});
The ring, and a reload
rule
a tile both under the cursor and picked shows both at once.

both = tiles(page).nth(1)                                # picked, and the cursor's tile after the reload
outline, ring = both.evaluate("el => { const s = getComputedStyle(el);"
                              " return [s.outlineStyle + ' ' + s.outlineColor, s.boxShadow]; }")
assert outline.startswith("solid") and "102, 204, 255" in outline, f"the pick's outline is gone: {outline}"
assert "249, 168, 38" in ring, f"the cursor's ring is gone: {ring}"
print("  PASS: cursor and pick show at once")
how
the cursor’s ring is amber, set apart from the blue outline of a picked tile.

.tile[data-cursor='1']{ box-shadow:0 0 0 3px #f9a826, 0 0 10px #f9a826aa; }
what
measures the run picked and the cursor survive a reload — an accidental one comes back to the tile you were on.

tiles(page).nth(0).click()                       # pick the first — the click plants the cursor there
page.keyboard.press("Shift+ArrowRight")          # extend the run to the next; the cursor lands on it
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(2)
page.reload(wait_until="commit")
heading(page).wait_for(timeout=8000)
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(KEY_N)         # the saved search brings the same wall back
expect(checks(page)).to_have_count(2)            # the picked run survived
page.keyboard.press("Enter")                     # the cursor survived on the second → opens it
expect(d.get_by_role("img")).to_have_attribute("src", key_thumb(1))
page.keyboard.press("Escape")
print("  PASS: cursor and selection survive reload")
how
the cursor and the picked run are each saved in the browser as they change — the way the search box and the state filter already are — and read back on load.
  • scope: the cursor’s half follows; the picks’ half sits in Selecting tiles and batch-editing.

const CURSOR_KEY = 'memories.cursor';
const [cursor, setCursor] = createSignal(localStorage.getItem(CURSOR_KEY));
createEffect(() => { const c = cursor(); c ? localStorage.setItem(CURSOR_KEY, c) : localStorage.removeItem(CURSOR_KEY); });
The cursor follows what you’re viewing
what
the wall’s keyboard cursor marks where you are.
what
in the lightbox, or in the frame, you move through the wall in place.
rule
the cursor rides along while you do, tracking whichever doc you are looking at.
The cursor rides along
what
measures back from the lightbox or the show, the cursor is on the doc you left, ready for the arrows to carry on: the story runs this check once after each.

page.keyboard.press("Enter")                     # the bare wall reopens the doc the cursor rests on
expect(d.get_by_role("img")).to_have_attribute("src", key_thumb(KEY_N - 1))
page.keyboard.press("Escape")
print("  PASS: the cursor follows what you were viewing")
The wall scrolls to it
how
whether a tile is somewhere you could see it is read off its own box against the window.
  • how: both blocks below ask it of the tile the cursor came to rest on.
  • how: the story asks it the other way round first, of the same tile, to be sure it was out of sight before the trip that should bring it back.

IN_VIEW = "el => { const r = el.getBoundingClientRect(); return r.top < window.innerHeight && r.bottom > 0; }"
what
measures the wall scrolls to the doc you left: gone deep into the wall from the lightbox, leaving it lands the wall on your tile, not at the top.

wait_until(page, lambda: tiles(page).nth(KEY_N - 1).evaluate(IN_VIEW),
           label="the wall scrolled the cursor's tile into view")
print("  PASS: wall scrolls to lightbox cursor")
what
measures the wall scrolling to the doc you left the show on: step the show far along, leave it, and that slide is in view.

wait_until(page, lambda: tiles(page).nth(KEY_N - 1).evaluate(IN_VIEW),
           label="the wall scrolled to the slide we stopped on")
print("  PASS: wall scrolls to frame cursor")
how
the doc you are looking at is the lightbox’s open one while it is up, and otherwise the frame’s centred slide.
how
every move on either surface updates one of those — the ‹/› buttons, the arrows, a swipe, a step of the show.
  • therefore: one effect mirroring whichever is live onto the cursor, and scrolling that cursor’s tile into view on the wall behind, covers them all.
rule
with neither surface open, the cursor stays right where you last left it.
what
leaving either surface goes back a step in the browser’s history, and the browser’s own scroll restoration then snaps the window back to where it stood when the surface opened.
  • therefore: left on, that restoration silently undoes the scroll to the cursor.
  • how: the app turns restoration off and owns the wall’s scroll itself — the follow is the authority on where the wall stands.

history.scrollRestoration = 'manual';
createEffect(() => { const c = opened()?.cid || (frame() ? frameCenterCid() : null); if(!c) return;
    setCursor(c);
    gridEl?.children[items().findIndex(p => p.cid === c)]?.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' }); });
Jumping to the add-label box
what
the cursor picks a run of docs without the mouse, and two keys carry on from there to its label.
  • example: pick with Shift+→, press l, type the word; or press . to drop in the label you used last and just hit Enter.
rule
the key that opens a box never lands in it.
l reaches the box
what
measures one key reaches the add-label box: with a doc open, l — for label — focuses its add-label box.

lb_box = d.get_by_placeholder("add a label…")
expect(lb_box).not_to_be_focused()
page.keyboard.press("l")
expect(lb_box).to_be_focused()
expect(lb_box).to_have_value("")             # l opened the box; it didn't type into it
print("  PASS: label shortcut focuses lightbox box")
rule
on the wall, with something picked, l focuses the add-label box of the selection toolbar instead.

tb_box = toolbar(page).get_by_placeholder("add a label…")
expect(tb_box).not_to_be_focused()
page.keyboard.press("l")
expect(tb_box).to_be_focused()
expect(tb_box).to_have_value("")
print("  PASS: label shortcut focuses batch box")
how
a small listener at the window routes l and . to whichever box is live — the open lightbox’s, else the toolbar’s.
  • rule: it stands aside while a field already has the keys, or while the frame is up.
  • how: the keystroke it acts on is swallowed, so it does not land in the box it just opened.

onMount(() => {
    const onKey = e => {
        if((e.key !== 'l' && e.key !== '.') || frame()) return;    // the frame has its own bar
        if(/^(INPUT|TEXTAREA)$/.test(e.target.tagName)) return;    // a field already owns the key
        const box = opened() ? document.querySelector('.lb .batch-label')
                  : selCount() > 0 ? document.querySelector('.toolbar .batch-label') : null;
        if(!box) return;
        e.preventDefault();
        if(e.key === '.' && lastLabel())                           // '.' re-drops the label applied last
            (opened() ? setLbText : setLabelText)(lastLabel());
        box.focus();
    };
    window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey);
    onCleanup(() => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey));
});
. reuses the last word
how
the story reaches this step having already put a different word on from the wall.
what
measures another key reuses the last word: with a doc open, . — repeat — fills its add-label box with the word applied last of all, wherever it was applied, and focuses it.

lb_box.fill(SECOND_WORD); lb_box.press("Enter")             # applied → the newest word remembered
expect(d.get_by_role("button", name=SECOND_WORD, exact=True)).to_be_visible()
lb_box.blur()                                               # leave the field
page.keyboard.press(".")
expect(lb_box).to_be_focused()
expect(lb_box).to_have_value(SECOND_WORD)                   # the newest, not the one before it
print("  PASS: label repeat fills lightbox box")
rule
the toolbar’s box lets its word go once the word is applied.
rule
on the wall, with something picked, . refills the toolbar’s box the same way.

tb_box.fill(FIRST_WORD); tb_box.press("Enter")   # applied to the one picked → remembered, selection clears
tiles(page).nth(1).click()                       # pick another
tb_box = toolbar(page).get_by_placeholder("add a label…")
expect(tb_box).to_have_value("")                 # the bar lets the word go once the write lands
tb_box.blur()                                    # leave the field
page.keyboard.press(".")
expect(tb_box).to_be_focused()
expect(tb_box).to_have_value(FIRST_WORD)
print("  PASS: label repeat fills batch box")
how
before focusing, . drops in the word any earlier apply, here or on a picked run, left behind.

if(e.key === '.' && lastLabel())                           // '.' re-drops the label applied last
    (opened() ? setLbText : setLabelText)(lastLabel());

Asking for more than the archive can hand over

what
an archive of sixty thousand docs can be asked for more than it can hand over, and it happens two ways.
  • what: the answer takes long enough that you are left waiting on it.
    • example: a bare word against all of them, a date range covering a decade.
  • what: or the answer arrives simply too big for a wall — tens of thousands of tiles nobody will ever scroll — and what comes back is a part of it.
what
both are the same failure to be honest if the app says nothing.
  • example: a wait it does not name looks like an app that has stopped.
  • example: a slice it does not name looks like the whole archive.
  • rule: the app says which it is doing.
  • rule: where it is waiting, it lets you change your mind.
how
the slice comes first.
  • rule: the wall says how much of the match it is holding and how it chose — every match, one end of it, or a spread across the whole.
    • rule: the count it names is the true one, not the number of tiles it happens to be showing.
  • what: that count is a promise about the tiles.
    • therefore: the tiles have to be able to keep it.
  • what: two thousand of them is more than one screen and more than one machine’s memory.
    • rule: both have to be answered without shrinking what is on offer.
      • how: a tile out of sight lets go of its picture and takes it back on return.
      • how: a row whose picture does not exist yet is still a tile.
    • what: neither costs the wall a doc.
  • what: which slice it took also changes what you can do with the tiles.
    • what: an end is a run and a spread is not.
    • what: a range gesture across a spread would rope in whatever happened to fall between two scattered tiles and call it a run.
    • rule: the wall lets the gesture through on an end and stands it down on a spread.
what
the search box does not search as you type; it searches when you commit, and says so while it holds something not yet run.
what
once committed, the wall names the query it is fetching, freezes the controls, and offers three ways out of a wait you did not mean to start.
  • scope: the one it cannot offer is a way out of the very first read, where there is no earlier answer to fall back to; that one just has to let go.
  • what: bailing out means going back to the last answer.
    • therefore: there has to be one — a query already asked and settled, sitting behind whatever gets tried next.
what
none of it can be watched while it happens unless the waiting is made to last.
  • how: the hold is put on from outside, not asked for by the query.
    • how: one word is agreed with the network, and a query carrying it is never answered.
    • how: where there is no query to carry a word, as on the first read, or where the query is not the point, the hold is simply laid over whatever read comes next.
    • how: either way the app is left standing in the middle of it for as long as we care to look.

SLOW = "zzslow"

def hold_a_read(page, query):
    """Commit a query the network will never answer, and wait until it has taken hold."""
    search_box(page).fill(query)
    page.get_by_role("button", name="run search").click()
    expect(search_box(page)).to_be_disabled()


@testcase
def test_asking_for_more_than_can_be_handed_over(page):
    """Asking for too much, three ways: a match too big to show, which the wall says it has
    sliced and how — and which of those slices you can still take a run in hand from; a
    wall too long to hold, which lets go of what you are not looking at
    and still counts what has no picture yet; and a read that drags, which the wall names,
    locks the query behind, and lets go of three different ways — including on the very
    first one, where there is nothing to go back to."""

            and seen.append((json.loads(r.post_data).get("variables") or {}).get("search", "")))
    page.on("requestfailed", lambda r: "/graphql" in r.url and aborted.append(1))
    drag_them_all, slow_state = [True], [None]           # the two holds put on from outside
    def hold(r):
        body = r.request.post_data or ""
        if SLOW in body or (slow_state[0] and f'"states":["{slow_state[0]}"]' in body): return

Load only the thumbnails on screen
what
measures a tile out of sight lets go of its picture and takes it back — loading and unloading.
  • rule: a tile carries its picture only while near the screen, the decoded picture released the moment the tile scrolls away.
  • rule: on a wall that overflows its fold, a tile waiting far below carries no picture at all until brought into view.
  • how: the wall this is read from is the one the whole archive draws — two thousand tiles.

far = thumb_imgs(page).nth(200)                                    # hundreds of rows down
expect(far).not_to_have_attribute("src", re.compile(r"/ipfs/"))    # it carries nothing
far.scroll_into_view_if_needed()
expect(far).to_have_attribute("src", re.compile(r"/ipfs/"))        # brought into view → it takes one
thumb_imgs(page).first.scroll_into_view_if_needed()
expect(far).not_to_have_attribute("src", re.compile(r"/ipfs/"))    # left again → it gives it back
print("  PASS: thumbs load in view and unload when they leave")
how
out of reach, the tile shows a blank of one pixel, its square’s own background filling the rest.
how
one watcher, shared by every tile, tells each one when it comes near the screen and when it leaves.
rule
a picture is ready a little before its tile scrolls in, and dropped a little after it scrolls out.
  • how: « near » reaches 300px past the edge of the screen.
rule
a search that swaps the wall leaves no watching behind.
  • how: each picture is watched from the moment it is drawn until it is taken down.

// a 1×1 transparent gif — what a tile shows when its image is unloaded
const BLANK = 'data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAIBRAA7';
const watchVisible = (() => {
    const cbs = new WeakMap();
    const io = new IntersectionObserver(
        entries => entries.forEach(e => cbs.get(e.target)?.(e.isIntersecting)),
        { rootMargin: '300px' });
    return (el, set) => {
        if(!el) return;
        cbs.set(el, set);
        io.observe(el);
        onCleanup(() => { io.unobserve(el); cbs.delete(el); });
    };
})();
rule
letting a picture go costs nothing on the wire when it is wanted again: the memory goes; the bytes never do.
  • how: a picture’s /ipfs/ address names its own content and can never come to stand for anything else.
  • how: the gateway says so, serving every rendition public, max-age=29030400, immutable, so scrolling back is a cache hit.
Placeholders for docs with no media
A tile for every match
what
not every row has its renditions.
  • what: rows arrive before their pictures do — an import lands, and the thumbnails are still being made.
  • therefore: at any moment some of what matches a search has nothing to show for itself.
what
the line above it counts what is shown against what matched.
  • therefore: a match quietly withheld would be a doc the archive says it has and the wall says it does not.
rule
rows that land while the wall is up do not push themselves onto it: the wall holds the answer it was given until it is asked something else.
  • how: the new arrival is met the way any is, by searching for it.
rule
opening a row with no web copy shows a « no preview » placeholder rather than a broken image.

for d in nomedia_docs(): gql(DELETE, {"cid": d["cid"]}); gql(CREATE, {"p": d})
search_for(page, NOMEDIA_LABEL)                     # a label only this doc carries
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(1)
open_doc(page)
d = dialog(page)
expect(d.get_by_text("no preview")).to_be_visible()
expect(d.get_by_role("img")).to_have_count(0)            # nothing broken to show
expect(d.locator("video")).to_have_count(0)
what
measures a row whose picture does not exist yet is still a tile: back on the wall, among the run it landed in, it is counted, tiled, and wearing the icon that says why it has no picture — reachable rather than silently dropped.
  • rule: it raises no notice of a spread, since nothing was sampled away.

d.get_by_role("button", name="close").click()
search_for(page, FIXTURE_LABEL)
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(len(FIXTURES) + 1)     # the no-thumb one shows too
expect(thumb_imgs(page)).to_have_count(len(FIXTURES))    # but it isn't an image
expect(grid(page).get_by_text("🖼")).to_have_count(1)     # it wears the icon
expect(page.get_by_text(re.compile(r"showing a spread"))).to_have_count(0)  # and no notice
What the lightbox opens instead
what
which placeholder the lightbox gives turns on what the row is.
rule
a photo missing its web copy still has its thumbnail, and the lightbox enlarges it — the same picture, only softer — rather than refusing the photo.

search_for(page, "zznwimg")                         # an image with a poster and no web copy
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(1)
open_doc(page)
expect(d.get_by_role("img")).to_have_attribute("src", "https://ipfs.konubinix.eu/p/zznw-img-t")   # its poster, stretched
what
the lightbox opens a clip in order to play it, and a poster cannot be played.
rule
a clip missing its web copy is refused — « no preview », with its type — and its poster is not offered, a photograph where a film was asked for.

d.get_by_role("button", name="close").click()
search_for(page, "zznwvid")                         # a clip with a poster and no web copy
expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(1)
open_doc(page)
expect(d.get_by_text("no preview · video/mp4")).to_be_visible()
expect(d.get_by_role("img")).to_have_count(0)        # and the poster is not offered in its place
The wall fills
how
In practice, asking anew does not empty the wall first: the tiles already up stay where they are until the new answer lands.
  • what: read too early, the wall is the old one, or a half-drawn new one.
  • therefore: a wall is read once it has filled, not the instant its question is asked.
rule
on the whole archive — all on the state filter, rather than the default todo — the wall fills with thumbnails.

wait_until(page, lambda: tiles(page).count() > 10, timeout=15000)   # filled, not still the old wall
wait_until(page, lambda: "/ipfs/" in (thumb_imgs(page).first.get_attribute("src") or ""))
print("  PASS: shows thumbnails")
how
the app holds the search box and the query last committed from it, and reads the wall from that query.

function App(){
    // the search box persists locally
    const SEARCH_KEY = 'memories.search';
    const [search, setSearch] = createSignal(localStorage.getItem(SEARCH_KEY) || '');
    createEffect(() => localStorage.setItem(SEARCH_KEY, search()));
    const [searchFocus, setSearchFocus] = createSignal(false);
    const [caret, setCaret] = createSignal(0);        // cursor position
    // keyboard-driving the suggestion list of the focused box
    const [sugItems, setSugItems] = createSignal([]);
    const [sugActive, setSugActive] = createSignal(-1);
    const [sugLoading, setSugLoading] = createSignal(false);   // the focused box's list is fetching
    const reportSug = list => { setSugItems(list); setSugActive(-1); };   // a new list clears the highlight
    const sugNav = (e, commit) => {
        const n = sugItems().length;
        if(e.key === 'ArrowDown' && n){ e.preventDefault(); setSugActive(i => i >= n - 1 ? -1 : i + 1); }
        else if(e.key === 'ArrowUp' && n){ e.preventDefault(); setSugActive(i => i < 0 ? n - 1 : i - 1); }
        else if(e.key === 'Enter'){ e.preventDefault();
            commit(sugActive() >= 0 ? sugItems()[sugActive()] : null); setSugActive(-1); }
    };
    const pickSearch = w => { const [s, e] = segSpan(search(), caret());
        const lead = (search().slice(s, e).match(/^\s*/) || [''])[0];
        // still drillable → hold the box on this token
        const drilling = w.endsWith(':') || dslSuggestions(w).some(v => v.length > w.length);
        const tail = drilling ? '' : '; ';
        const next = search().slice(0, s) + lead + w + tail + search().slice(e);
        setSearch(next); setCaret(s + lead.length + w.length + tail.length); setSearchFocus(true); };
    // the chip choice persists; the first-ever visit defaults to the triage view (todo)
    const STATE_KEY = 'memories.state';
    const [stateFilter, setStateFilter] = createSignal(localStorage.getItem(STATE_KEY) || 'todo');
    createEffect(() => localStorage.setItem(STATE_KEY, stateFilter()));
    // the last label applied (lightbox or batch), offered for one-tap reuse on the next doc
