const CACHE = 'memories-nil';
self.addEventListener('install', () => self.skipWaiting());
self.addEventListener('activate', e => e.waitUntil((async () => {
    for(const k of await caches.keys()) if(k !== CACHE) await caches.delete(k);
    await self.clients.claim();
})()));
self.addEventListener('fetch', e => {
    const req = e.request, url = new URL(req.url);
    if(req.method !== 'GET' || url.origin !== location.origin
       || url.pathname.includes('/graphql') || url.pathname.includes('/ipfs/')) return;
    e.respondWith((async () => {
        const cache = await caches.open(CACHE);
        const hit = await cache.match(req);
        if(hit) return hit;
        const res = await fetch(req.url, { cache: 'reload' });
        if(res.ok) cache.put(req, res.clone());
        return res;
    })());
});

Annexe

What a sharpened wall holds

what
the refined wall draws two pictures per tile, and a picture unpacked for drawing costs four bytes a pixel however little it weighed compressed.
what
measured on the same docs as the byte figures, a thumbnail is 0.045 Mpx — 256px on its long side — and a rendition 0.79 Mpx, cut to fit 1024px.
  • therefore: a rendition is some eighteen times the pixels of a thumbnail, where it is only five to twelve times the bytes.
scope
how many of those pixels a browser actually keeps is not settled here — it may unpack a rendition at the size the file was written, or at the size the tile draws it.
  • what: the two lead to opposite readings of what happens as the cells grow, and both, though, land on the same ceiling.
what
unpacking at the file’s size, a fold of cells c wide holds area-over-c-squared tiles of 0.18 + 3.15 MB, against the dense wall’s tiles of 0.18 MB at 96px.
  • therefore: the ratio is (96/c)² × 18.5 — 1.9 at the 300px threshold, level by 400px, and falling after that.
  • therefore: the threshold is the worst of it, and the wall gets lighter the further past it you go.
what
unpacking at the drawn size instead, tiles times cell area is just the fold’s area, so a fold holds its own area in pixels once per layer, whatever the cells measure.
  • therefore: two layers is then twice one, at every size, and growing the tiles changes nothing.
what
neither reading is a bound on the other — at cells past 256px the thumbnail layer is upscaled, so drawn-size unpacking holds more for it than its file would suggest, while for the dense wall it holds less.
therefore
what survives both is a ceiling: about twice what the dense wall already held.
  • what: the reach window was drawn around a single fold of thumbnails, so this is that bound doubled — bounded rather than free.
  • scope: what a device actually holds at that ceiling is a reading still to be taken.

Reaching the app as its user does

how
open_app boots the app on a sync room of this run’s own.
  • rule: only the boot is retried, never the test body.
def open_app(page, qs=""):
    # any launch that has not chosen a sync server is pointed at the throwaway one, in a room of this run's own
    if "yws=" not in qs:
        qs += ("&" if qs else "?") + f"yws={require_sync()}&room=scratch-{_RUN_ID}"
    # boot-only retry: only the boot is retried, never the test body
    page.goto(BASE_URL + qs, wait_until="commit")
    try:
        heading(page).wait_for(timeout=8000)             # the titled shell has painted
    except Exception:
        print("  (cold boot stalled — retried)", flush=True)
        page.reload(wait_until="commit")
        heading(page).wait_for(timeout=8000)
rule
a test finds the app as the user sees it — a role, an accessible name, a placeholder, visible text — never a test-only hook.
def heading(page):    return page.get_by_role("heading")
def search_box(page): return page.get_by_label("search labels")
def grid(page):       return page.get_by_role("list", name="photos")
def tiles(page):      return grid(page).get_by_role("listitem")   # one per shown doc (thumb or not)
def thumb_imgs(page): return grid(page).get_by_role("img")        # only the tiles that have a thumbnail
def cell_px(page):    return tiles(page).first.bounding_box()["width"]   # the width a tile is DRAWN at
def tile_dates(page): return thumb_imgs(page).evaluate_all(              # each tile's date, in wall order
    "els => els.map(e => e.getAttribute('alt'))")                        # (the name the tile carries)
def tile_srcs(page, i):   # every layer tile i is showing (thumbnail base, full-res overlay)
    return tiles(page).nth(i).locator("img").evaluate_all("els => els.map(e => e.getAttribute('src'))")
how
what the page fetched is read off its own resource timeline.
how
a tile is opened with a double-click, and armed with a press held past the app’s timer.
# what the page has actually FETCHED, read off its own resource timeline; called before open_app
def watch_fetches(page):
    page.add_init_script("performance.setResourceTimingBufferSize(4000)")
    return lambda: page.evaluate('() => performance.getEntriesByType("resource").map(e => e.name)')
def checks(page):     return grid(page).get_by_text("✓")          # one per selected tile
def open_doc(page, i=0):                                          # a double-click on a tile opens the lightbox
    tiles(page).nth(i).dblclick()
LONG_PRESS_MS = 600                                               # past the app's 500ms press timer
def press_and_hold(page, tile):                                   # the pointer put down on a tile and held
    b = tile.bounding_box()
    page.mouse.move(b["x"] + b["width"] / 2, b["y"] + b["height"] / 2)
    page.mouse.down(); page.wait_for_timeout(LONG_PRESS_MS)
def drag_onto(page, tile):                                        # …and moved until it is over another
    b = tile.bounding_box()
    page.mouse.move(b["x"] + b["width"] / 2, b["y"] + b["height"] / 2, steps=5)
how
pinches and one-finger drags go through Chromium’s own touch pipeline, as real fingers.
def pinch_in(page, cx, cy):                                       # two fingers spreading → the browser's zoom
    cdp = page.context.new_cdp_session(page)
    cdp.send("Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled", {"enabled": True, "maxTouchPoints": 2})
    cdp.send("Input.dispatchTouchEvent", {"type": "touchStart",
        "touchPoints": [{"x": cx - 30, "y": cy}, {"x": cx + 30, "y": cy}]})
    for d in (60, 120, 200, 260):
        cdp.send("Input.dispatchTouchEvent", {"type": "touchMove",
            "touchPoints": [{"x": cx - d, "y": cy}, {"x": cx + d, "y": cy}]})
    cdp.send("Input.dispatchTouchEvent", {"type": "touchEnd", "touchPoints": []})
def drag_touch(page, x0, y0, x1, y1, steps=6):                    # one finger travelling
    cdp = page.context.new_cdp_session(page)
    cdp.send("Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled", {"enabled": True, "maxTouchPoints": 1})
    cdp.send("Input.dispatchTouchEvent", {"type": "touchStart", "touchPoints": [{"x": x0, "y": y0}]})
    for i in range(1, steps + 1):
        cdp.send("Input.dispatchTouchEvent", {"type": "touchMove", "touchPoints": [
            {"x": x0 + (x1 - x0) * i / steps, "y": y0 + (y1 - y0) * i / steps}]})
    cdp.send("Input.dispatchTouchEvent", {"type": "touchEnd", "touchPoints": []})
how
the state filters, the selection toolbar, the lightbox and the label suggestions each have a finder.
how
a held completion query keeps the suggestion list loading.
def filters(page):    return page.get_by_role("group", name="filter by state")
def chip(page, name): return filters(page).get_by_role("button", name=name, exact=True)
def select_all(page): return filters(page).get_by_role("button", name=re.compile("select all|clear", re.I))
def toolbar(page):    return page.get_by_role("toolbar", name="selection actions")
def dialog(page):     return page.get_by_role("dialog")
def options(page):    return page.get_by_role("option")           # label suggestions
def hold_completions(page):   # leave the label-completion query pending → the list stays loading
    page.route("**/graphql", lambda route:
               route.fallback() if "labelCompletions" not in (route.request.post_data or "") else None)
def expanded_while_loading(page, box):   # the popover is up (loading) → aria-expanded must say so
    box.click(); box.press_sequentially("au", delay=20)
    expect(page.get_by_text("completing")).to_be_visible()      # the loading list is on screen
    expect(box).to_have_attribute("aria-expanded", "true")

Waiting on the archive

how
search_for types a query, commits it, and waits for a read issued after the click to settle.
how
wait_until polls a condition and names it when it fails.
# every wall read the page has finished, as (issued_at, search_term); search_for waits on it
SETTLED_READS = []

def search_for(page, text):
    # type the query, then COMMIT it
    search_box(page).fill(text)
    clicked = time.time()
    page.get_by_role("button", name="run search").click()
    search_box(page).blur()
    expect(search_box(page)).to_have_attribute("aria-expanded", "false")   # deterministic: popover closed, no clock
    # a read issued after the click has settled, and the grid is no longer busy
    wait_until(page, lambda: any(issued > clicked for issued, _ in SETTLED_READS),
               label=f"the wall re-read for {text!r}",
               detail=lambda: f"reads settled: {[s for _, s in SETTLED_READS[-4:]]}")
    expect(grid(page)).to_have_attribute("aria-busy", "false")

def wait_until(page, pred, timeout=8000, label="", detail=None):
    # label names the condition in the failure; detail() is read only at timeout
    end = time.time() + timeout / 1000
    while time.time() < end:
        if pred(): return
        page.wait_for_timeout(100)
    raise AssertionError("condition not met within timeout"
                         + (f": {label}" if label else "")
                         + (f" — {detail()}" if detail else ""))
how
gql posts straight to the data layer, as the data layer note defines it.
nil

A sync room of the run’s own

how
a throwaway sync server runs the prod image on a free port, once per run.
import base64
nil
nil
SYNC_IMAGE = "konubinix/ywebsocket:0.1.0"
_RUN_ID = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
_sync = {"at": None}
def require_sync():
    if _sync["at"]: return _sync["at"]
    container, port = f"memories-sync-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}", _free_port()
    subprocess.check_call(
        ["docker", "run", "-d", "--rm", "--name", container,
         "-p", f"127.0.0.1:{port}:{port}", "-e", "HOST=0.0.0.0", "-e", f"PORT={port}",
         SYNC_IMAGE, "y-websocket-server"],
        stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    atexit.register(lambda: subprocess.run(["docker", "stop", "-t", "0", container],
                                           stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL))
    hs = _wait_ws_handshake(port)
    if hs is not True: raise RuntimeError(f"fixture ywebsocket not ready on {port}: {hs}")
    _sync["at"] = f"ws://localhost:{port}"
    return _sync["at"]
how
a second client joins the same room, as the companion app does.
  • therefore: a test reads what the show says it shows, or speaks over it.
# a second client on the same room, as the companion app is
_ROOM_WATCHERS = {}

def watch_room(context, url, room):
    page = context.new_page()
    page.goto(BASE_URL, wait_until="commit")
    page.evaluate("""async ([url, room]) => {
        const Y = await import('https://esm.sh/yjs@13.6.20');
        const { WebsocketProvider } = await import('https://esm.sh/y-websocket@2.0.4?external=yjs');
        const shared = new Y.Doc();
        window.__watch = new WebsocketProvider(url, room, shared);
        window.__showing = shared.getMap('showing');
    }""", [url, room])
    _ROOM_WATCHERS[id(context)] = page
    return lambda: page.evaluate("() => (window.__showing && window.__showing.get('doc')) || null")

# a rival frame, in one line: the watcher's own client writing the entry
def speak_over(context, cid):
    _ROOM_WATCHERS[id(context)].evaluate(
        "cid => window.__showing.set('doc', { cid, webCid: cid, mimetype: 'image/jpeg' })", cid)

The harness’s own writes

how
every write of the harness is logged: the call, the row, how long, what came back.
GQL_LOG = []                                          # (clock, op, cid, ms, outcome), drained per test
_gql_direct = gql
def _gql_op(query, variables):
    v = variables or {}
    op = next((k for k in ("createPhotovideo", "deletePhotovideo", "updatePhotovideo",
                           "photovideosSample") if k in query),
              (query.strip().split("{", 1)[0].strip() or "query")[:40])
    return op, v.get("cid") or (v.get("p") or {}).get("cid") or ""
def gql(query, variables=None):
    (op, cid), t0 = _gql_op(query, variables), time.time()
    def log(outcome):
        GQL_LOG.append((time.time(), op, cid, (time.time() - t0) * 1000, outcome))
    try:
        res = _gql_direct(query, variables)
    except Exception as e:
        log(f"RAISED {e}"); raise
    errs = [e.get("message") for e in (res or {}).get("errors") or []]
    # a pre-clean delete that matched nothing is logged as ok (absent)
    if errs and op == "deletePhotovideo" and all("No values were deleted" in m for m in errs):
        log("ok (absent)")
    else:
        log(f"ERRORS={errs}" if errs else "ok")
    return res
how
in a failure’s dump, runs of quick same-shaped calls fold into one line.
  • rule: a slow, failed or lone call prints as it happened.
def harness_writes(log, t0):
    same = lambda e: (e[1], e[4])
    quick = lambda e: e[4].startswith("ok") and e[3] < 500
    out, i = [], 0
    while i < len(log):
        j = i
        while j < len(log) and quick(log[j]) and same(log[j]) == same(log[i]): j += 1
        head, span = log[i], [e[3] for e in log[i:j]]
        stamp = f"{(head[0] - t0) * 1000:+7.0f}ms"
        if j - i > 3:
            out.append(f"{stamp} {head[1]} ×{j - i} {head[4]} ({min(span):.0f}–{max(span):.0f}ms)")
            i = j
        else:
            out.append(f"{stamp} {head[1]}({head[2]}) {head[3]:5.0f}ms {head[4]}")
            i += 1
    return out

how
open_fixtures starts a test from exactly the three fixtures, on every state, the wall narrowed to them.
def drop_fixtures():
    for f in FIXTURES + [VIDEO_FIXTURE, NOTHUMB_FIXTURE]:
        try: gql(DELETE, {"cid": f["cid"]})
        except Exception: pass
def make_fixtures():
    drop_fixtures()                       # clean slate, independent of test order
    for f in FIXTURES:
        gql(CREATE, {"p": f})

def open_fixtures(page, qs=""):
    """Fresh fixtures, app open on *all* states (default is todo), the wall narrowed
    to just the fixtures — so a test starts from exactly len(FIXTURES) docs."""
    make_fixtures()
    open_app(page, qs)
    chip(page, "all").click()
    search_for(page, FIXTURE_LABEL)
    expect(tiles(page)).to_have_count(len(FIXTURES))
how
a real file can be served from the app’s own origin.
how
any other /ipfs/ fetch gets a fast 404, the answer the gateway gives for a missing one.
# a real byte at a path the app's own origin already serves (next to this script is /debug/memories/)
def serve_bytes(name):
    with open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), name), "wb") as f:
        f.write(b"IPFS")
    return name                                       # the same-origin cid the app will fetch
def unserve_bytes(*names):
    for n in names:
        try: os.remove(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), n))
        except OSError: pass

# /ipfs/ mocked: a fast 404, the same "missing" answer the gateway gives
def _mock_ipfs(route):
    try: route.fulfill(status=404, content_type="text/plain", body="mock ipfs")
    except Exception:
        try: route.abort()
        except Exception: pass

The runner

how
the runner picks the tests named on the command line, or all of them, and runs each in a fresh context.

def main():
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    headed = "--headed" in argv
    stop_on_fail = "-x" in argv or "--exitfirst" in argv
    patterns = [a for a in argv if a not in ("--headed", "-x", "--exitfirst")]
    selected = [t for t in TESTS if not patterns or any(p in t.__name__ for p in patterns)]
    if not selected:
        print(f"no test matches {patterns}"); sys.exit(2)
    passed = failed = 0
    now = lambda: time.strftime("%H:%M:%S")
    try:
        with sync_playwright() as pw:
            # KeyboardFocusableScrollers, the modern-Chrome default (≥130): a scrollable region takes keyboard focus
            browser = pw.chromium.launch(headless=not headed,
                                         args=["--enable-blink-features=KeyboardFocusableScrollers"])
            require_postgraphile()                         # pre-warm the fixture before the loop
            for t in selected:
                t0 = time.time()
                print(f"[{now()}] TRYING {t.__name__}", flush=True)
                ctx = browser.new_context(viewport=VIEWPORT)   # fresh storage per test
                ctx.route("**/graphql", _forward_graphql)      # /graphql → ungated fixture, never the gated proxy
                ctx.route("**/ipfs/**", _mock_ipfs)            # /ipfs/ → deterministic 404, never the flaky gateway
                # unhandled promise rejections forwarded to the console
                ctx.add_init_script(
                    "addEventListener('unhandledrejection', e =>"
                    " console.error('unhandledrejection: ' + (e.reason?.message || e.reason)))")
                page = ctx.new_page()
                page.set_default_timeout(8000)
                events = []
                # every event carries a monotonic #seq + relative ms
                _seq = [0]; _t0 = time.time()
                def ev(msg):
                    _seq[0] += 1
                    events.append(f"#{_seq[0]:03d} +{(time.time()-_t0)*1000:6.0f}ms {msg}")
                # mocked-/ipfs 404 console errors are tallied, not traced; every other console error still traces
                _ipfs404 = [0]
                def _on_console(m):
                    if m.type not in ("error", "warning"): return
                    if "Failed to load resource" in m.text and "404" in m.text:
                        _ipfs404[0] += 1; return
                    ev(f"console.{m.type}: {m.text}")
                page.on("console", _on_console)
                page.on("pageerror", lambda e: ev(f"pageerror: {e}"))
                page.on("requestfailed", lambda r: ev(f"requestfailed: {r.method} {r.url}"))
                watch_graphql_errors(page, events)
                # GraphQL wire trace — every /graphql op when its request is ISSUED (REQ) and when its response RESOLVES (RESP)
                def _op(pd):
                    try:
                        b = json.loads(pd); q = b.get("query", ""); v = b.get("variables") or {}
                        if "photovideosSample" in q: return ("read", f"search={v.get('search','')!r}")
                        if "mutation" in q:
                            op = next((k for k in ("updatePhotovideo", "photovideosAddLabel",
                                                    "photovideosRemoveLabel", "photovideosSetState") if k in q), "mutation")
                            return ("write", f"{op} {({kk: v[kk] for kk in ('cid','label','v','patch') if kk in v})}")
                    except Exception: pass
                    return None
                # each RESP also carries how long its own read was in flight
                _req_t0 = {}
                def _trace_req(req):
                    try:
                        if "/graphql" in req.url and (o := _op(req.post_data or "")):
                            _req_t0[req] = time.time()
                            ev(f"REQ  {o[0]:5s} {o[1]}")
                    except Exception: pass
                def _trace_resp(resp):
                    try:
                        if "/graphql" not in resp.url or not (o := _op(resp.request.post_data or "")): return
                        started = _req_t0.pop(resp.request, None)
                        took = f" [{(time.time() - started) * 1000:.0f}ms]" if started else ""
                        body = resp.json()
                        if body.get("errors"):
                            ev(f"RESP {o[0]:5s} {o[1]}{took} ERRORS={[e.get('message') for e in body['errors']]}")
                        elif o[0] == "read":
                            nodes = ((body.get("data") or {}).get("photovideosSample") or {}).get("nodes") or []
                            labs = [n.get("labels") for n in nodes[:6] if isinstance(n, dict)]
                            tail = "" if len(nodes) <= 6 else f" …(+{len(nodes)-6})"
                            SETTLED_READS.append((started or 0, o[1]))   # search_for waits on this
                            ev(f"RESP {o[0]:5s} {o[1]}{took} → {len(nodes)} nodes labels={labs}{tail}")
                        else:
                            ev(f"RESP {o[0]:5s} {o[1]}{took}")
                    except Exception: pass
                page.on("request", _trace_req)
                page.on("response", _trace_resp)
                # which tests install a /graphql route of their own
                _held_by_route = [False]
                _route = page.route
                def _route_noting(pattern, handler, **kw):
                    if "graphql" in str(pattern): _held_by_route[0] = True
                    return _route(pattern, handler, **kw)
                page.route = _route_noting
                GQL_LOG.clear()                                # this test's own writes, not the last one's
                SETTLED_READS.clear()                          # and this test's own reads
                try:
                    t(page); passed += 1
                    print(f"[{now()}] PASS  {t.__name__} ({time.time()-t0:.1f}s)", flush=True)
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"[{now()}] FAIL  {t.__name__} ({time.time()-t0:.1f}s): {e}", flush=True); failed += 1
                    if _ipfs404[0]: events.append(f"     (+{_ipfs404[0]} mocked-/ipfs 404 console errors suppressed)")
                    # the harness's writes, on the same clock as the timeline above
                    if GQL_LOG:
                        events.append("     --- harness writes (same clock) ---")
                        for line in harness_writes(GQL_LOG, _t0): events.append("     " + line)
                    dump_failure(page, t.__name__, "memories", events)
                    if stop_on_fail: break
                finally:
                    # pending writes drained before the page is torn down; reads left alone; the wait capped
                    _drain0, _stuck = time.time(), []
                    while time.time() - _drain0 < 1.5:
                        _stuck = [o for rq in list(_req_t0)
                                  if (o := _op(rq.post_data or "")) and o[0] == "write"]
                        if not _stuck: break
                        page.wait_for_timeout(25)
                    if _stuck and not _held_by_route[0]:
                        print(f"       LEAKED WRITE past {t.__name__}: {_stuck}"
                              f" — if a later test fails unexplained, start here", flush=True)
                    page.close(); ctx.close()
            browser.close()
    finally:
        drop_fixtures()                   # never leave test rows in prod
    print(f"\n{passed} passed, {failed} failed out of {len(selected)}")
    sys.exit(1 if failed else 0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
how
-x stops at the first failure, --headed shows the browser, any other word picks the tests whose name holds it.

argv = sys.argv[1:]
headed = "--headed" in argv
stop_on_fail = "-x" in argv or "--exitfirst" in argv
patterns = [a for a in argv if a not in ("--headed", "-x", "--exitfirst")]
selected = [t for t in TESTS if not patterns or any(p in t.__name__ for p in patterns)]
if not selected:
    print(f"no test matches {patterns}"); sys.exit(2)
passed = failed = 0
now = lambda: time.strftime("%H:%M:%S")
how
each test gets a fresh context: /graphql goes to the ungated fixture, /ipfs/ to the mock.

t0 = time.time()
print(f"[{now()}] TRYING {t.__name__}", flush=True)
ctx = browser.new_context(viewport=VIEWPORT)   # fresh storage per test
ctx.route("**/graphql", _forward_graphql)      # /graphql → ungated fixture, never the gated proxy
ctx.route("**/ipfs/**", _mock_ipfs)            # /ipfs/ → deterministic 404, never the flaky gateway
# unhandled promise rejections forwarded to the console
ctx.add_init_script(
    "addEventListener('unhandledrejection', e =>"
    " console.error('unhandledrejection: ' + (e.reason?.message || e.reason)))")
page = ctx.new_page()
page.set_default_timeout(8000)

What the runner records of a test

how
console errors, page errors and failed requests go to the test’s timeline, numbered and timed.
  • rule: the mocked /ipfs/ 404s are only counted.

events = []
# every event carries a monotonic #seq + relative ms
_seq = [0]; _t0 = time.time()
def ev(msg):
    _seq[0] += 1
    events.append(f"#{_seq[0]:03d} +{(time.time()-_t0)*1000:6.0f}ms {msg}")
# mocked-/ipfs 404 console errors are tallied, not traced; every other console error still traces
_ipfs404 = [0]
def _on_console(m):
    if m.type not in ("error", "warning"): return
    if "Failed to load resource" in m.text and "404" in m.text:
        _ipfs404[0] += 1; return
    ev(f"console.{m.type}: {m.text}")
page.on("console", _on_console)
page.on("pageerror", lambda e: ev(f"pageerror: {e}"))
page.on("requestfailed", lambda r: ev(f"requestfailed: {r.method} {r.url}"))
watch_graphql_errors(page, events)
how
a GraphQL call is told a read or a write by its query.

# GraphQL wire trace — every /graphql op when its request is ISSUED (REQ) and when its response RESOLVES (RESP)
def _op(pd):
    try:
        b = json.loads(pd); q = b.get("query", ""); v = b.get("variables") or {}
        if "photovideosSample" in q: return ("read", f"search={v.get('search','')!r}")
        if "mutation" in q:
            op = next((k for k in ("updatePhotovideo", "photovideosAddLabel",
                                    "photovideosRemoveLabel", "photovideosSetState") if k in q), "mutation")
            return ("write", f"{op} {({kk: v[kk] for kk in ('cid','label','v','patch') if kk in v})}")
    except Exception: pass
    return None
how
each call goes to the timeline twice: when it is issued, and when it answers, with how long it took.

# each RESP also carries how long its own read was in flight
_req_t0 = {}
def _trace_req(req):
    try:
        if "/graphql" in req.url and (o := _op(req.post_data or "")):
            _req_t0[req] = time.time()
            ev(f"REQ  {o[0]:5s} {o[1]}")
    except Exception: pass
def _trace_resp(resp):
    try:
        if "/graphql" not in resp.url or not (o := _op(resp.request.post_data or "")): return
        started = _req_t0.pop(resp.request, None)
        took = f" [{(time.time() - started) * 1000:.0f}ms]" if started else ""
        body = resp.json()
        if body.get("errors"):
            ev(f"RESP {o[0]:5s} {o[1]}{took} ERRORS={[e.get('message') for e in body['errors']]}")
        elif o[0] == "read":
            nodes = ((body.get("data") or {}).get("photovideosSample") or {}).get("nodes") or []
            labs = [n.get("labels") for n in nodes[:6] if isinstance(n, dict)]
            tail = "" if len(nodes) <= 6 else f" …(+{len(nodes)-6})"
            SETTLED_READS.append((started or 0, o[1]))   # search_for waits on this
            ev(f"RESP {o[0]:5s} {o[1]}{took} → {len(nodes)} nodes labels={labs}{tail}")
        else:
            ev(f"RESP {o[0]:5s} {o[1]}{took}")
    except Exception: pass
page.on("request", _trace_req)
page.on("response", _trace_resp)
how
the runner notes which tests hold /graphql with a route of their own.

_route = page.route
def _route_noting(pattern, handler, **kw):
    if "graphql" in str(pattern): _held_by_route[0] = True
    return _route(pattern, handler, **kw)

how
a failure dumps the timeline, with the harness’s own writes on the same clock.

if _ipfs404[0]: events.append(f"     (+{_ipfs404[0]} mocked-/ipfs 404 console errors suppressed)")
# the harness's writes, on the same clock as the timeline above
if GQL_LOG:
    events.append("     --- harness writes (same clock) ---")
    for line in harness_writes(GQL_LOG, _t0): events.append("     " + line)
dump_failure(page, t.__name__, "memories", events)
if stop_on_fail: break
rule
writes still pending are drained before the page goes, the wait capped at 1.5 s.
  • how: one still pending is printed as a leaked write, unless the test held /graphql itself.

# pending writes drained before the page is torn down; reads left alone; the wait capped
_drain0, _stuck = time.time(), []
while time.time() - _drain0 < 1.5:
    _stuck = [o for rq in list(_req_t0)
              if (o := _op(rq.post_data or "")) and o[0] == "write"]
    if not _stuck: break
    page.wait_for_timeout(25)
if _stuck and not _held_by_route[0]:
    print(f"       LEAKED WRITE past {t.__name__}: {_stuck}"
          f" — if a later test fails unexplained, start here", flush=True)
page.close(); ctx.close()
